CURRICULUM: Single Cycle 6 Years Interuniversity Joint Degree
SECTION: General Description
URL: https://unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10739

[1001S] MEDICINE AND SURGERY Master's Degree Single Cycle 6 Years Interuniversity Joint Degree
INFORMATION ON COURSES General information referring to the current academic year Duration
6 years Organization
2020
Status Open Credits
360 CFU Type Master's Degree programs in a single cycle Category Medical, health and biological sciences Regulation Reform 270/04
Class of degree LM-41 - Class of Master's Degrees in Medicine and Surgery Joint Course Partner Universities University of Verona Admission Programmed (60 Places)
Location City Campus - Palazzo Consolati - via S. Maria Maddalena, 1
Department Interdepartmental Center for Medical Sciences - CISMed Entry requirements verification No Course program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The study program aims to train a physician capable of caring for patients, understanding, utilizing, promoting and governing the development of technology in medicine and related fields, ranging from health promotion, disease prevention and treatment, patient rehabilitation to the development of innovative diagnostic and therapeutic solutions. It is the objective of the study program to provide students with a bio-medical-technical-psychosocial culture characterized by a multidisciplinary and integrated vision of health and disease problems, with education oriented towards technological development, community, territory and fundamentally towards disease prevention and health promotion.
Additionally, the course aims to pursue the objectives expressed in Directive 2005/36/EC and the European Specifications in Medical Education developed by the Thematic Network on Medical Education in Europe (MEDINE), under the joint direction of the World Federation for Medical Education (WFME) and the Association of Medical Schools in Europe (AMSE) on behalf of the European Commission.
The study program distinguishes itself from other courses in the same class of Master's Degree in a single cycle (LM-41 Medicine and Surgery) by integrating and enhancing the typical competencies of the medical profession with basic competencies of digital medicine and typical competencies of "technological" degrees to respond to the challenges and opportunities that the fields of medicine and life sciences will face in the coming years. In particular, from this perspective, the study program aims to prepare students to address developments in genomics, informatics and artificial intelligence, the use of biosensors and interfaces, digital medicine, data analysis, and to understand their application and impact on medical activity and benefits in terms of safety, efficiency and personalization of care.
Training path For the achievement of the above educational objectives, the Master's Degree in a single cycle provides a total of 360 CFU, structured over six years of study, of which at least 60 must be acquired through training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills.
The study program is organized into 2 semesters for 6 years and 35 integrated courses; specific CFU are assigned in accordance with the table of essential training activities of class LM-41.
The training path of the Master's Degree program integrates:
1) Basic sciences, which must be broad and include knowledge of evolutionary biology and biological complexity aimed at understanding the structure and function of the human body under normal conditions, for the maintenance of health conditions. Increasing knowledge of the structure, function and dysfunction of biomolecular systems, including the human genome, makes a deep understanding and comprehension of the fundamental principles of molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, human genetics, applied physics, human physiology, general pathology and biostatistics indispensable.
2) Clinical and methodological medical practice, which must be particularly solid, through extensive use of tutorial teaching capable of transforming theoretical knowledge into personal experience, building one's own value scale and interests, and critically applying diagnostic methods and intervention procedures that rely on artificial intelligence tools and the processing of large data sets.
3) Humanities, which must constitute a useful background to achieve awareness of the medical role with specific attention to relational aspects in reference to medical humanities, narrative medicine and gender medicine.
4) Technological knowledge and skills, which represent a distinctive feature of the training path.
The study program is structured into a first three-year period dedicated to essential training activities for all students and a second three-year period aimed at completing medical training in its various components, as well as offering interdisciplinary pathways particularly suited to applying knowledge and skills acquired in the first three years.
For this purpose, Thematic Orientations are provided: in the 4th, 5th and 6th year, the student must follow a total of 3 (1 per year) of the 8 proposed Thematic Orientations (TO). The number of CFU for each TO is defined in the didactic regulations.
TO 1. Within the scope of precision medicine TO 2. Within the scope of medical technologies 1: robotics, materials, nanomedicine TO 3. Within the scope of reconstructive and regenerative medicine TO 4. Within the scope of medical technologies 2: e-health, telemedicine, artificial intelligence TO 5. Within the scope of gene and cell therapy: genome editing, diseases TO 6. Within the scope of advanced imaging diagnostics TO 7. Within the scope of advanced radiation therapy TO 8. Within the scope of health promotion, prevention, lifestyle and gender medicine Methodological profiles The teaching method is based on a solid cultural and methodological foundation acquired through the study of pre-clinical disciplines and is subsequently predominantly focused on teaching approaches aimed at developing the ability to address problems (problem-oriented learning).
A solid foundation of clinical knowledge is also ensured to students through the organization of certified internships based on tutorial teaching, together with a strong understanding of the scientific medical method and humanities.
The teaching process makes use of modern teaching tools, enhancing their use, consisting of the tutorial system, clinical trigger, problem-oriented learning, experiential learning, problem solving, and extensive use of seminars and conferences, as well as the use of simulated environments based on virtual reality.
Tutors are predominantly used, collaborating in the student's training process with teaching functions (area tutors) and support functions (personal tutors).
Particular attention is paid to the acquisition of practical skills through:
1) Involvement in planning a basic research project in the first three years of study,
2) Learning the basics of clinical semiotics at the patient's bedside and in laboratories during the intermediate period (internship organized as a tutorial-guided activity with certification of skill level, in the 3rd year of study),
3) The professional internship, a fundamental part of the training path also in the form of an internship enabling the profession, requires attendance in university or affiliated departments and outpatient clinics (clinical internship in surgical and general areas with certification by the tutor of achieved skills at the 6th year of study) and territorial ones, such as those of General Practitioners (achieved at the 6th year). A total of 60 CFU are reserved for this, in addition to the period of attendance at a dedicated structure for the preparation of the final thesis. Practical activities and professional internships also include those established for the practical-evaluative internship for the State Exam. Specific professional internships will be activated in the areas of palliative care and pain therapy.
4) Participation in research programs during the internship period for the preparation of the final thesis.
Subject to the possible signing of a specific agreement with the Autonomous Province of Bolzano Healthcare Authority, internship paths may be activated also in German language in the Bolzano province or other nearby affiliated locations.
In an internationalization perspective, activities will be provided to promote the acquisition of good skills in technical scientific English, which will be reinforced through teaching in English and through seminars and specialized teaching. The possibility of carrying out practical activities in international contexts will also be provided.
Particular attention is given to the use of information and multimedia methodologies, also through e-learning, tele-teaching, telemedicine experiences, the use of virtual reality information systems, and the correct use of bibliographic sources and databases.
Assessment of learning Assessment of learning occurs through ongoing assessments (self-assessment tests and intermediate interviews), written reports by students on assigned topics, and through the evaluation of the overall profile developed based on predefined criteria. Examination methods may be structured beyond traditional oral or written exams, including sequences of items to verify acquired knowledge such as multiple-choice tests or short written answers organized around interdisciplinary clinical problems, followed by exams to verify acquired clinical skills, such as the Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE), the mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise, the Direct Observation of Procedural Skills, and the use of the Portfolio. As a general rule valid for all integrated courses, formal assessments will be based on written tests, possibly followed by oral tests. The Progress Test of Maastricht type is used, adhering to the national-scale experimentation, for student assessment to evaluate the actual competence achieved.
Entry requirements To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery, one must possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as suitable.
The knowledge required for entry into the Medicine and Surgery study program is defined by the subjects included in the national written admission test. The subjects of the exam are: general culture and logical reasoning, physics and mathematics, chemistry, biology. The possession of the required knowledge for entry into the course is considered verified through the successful completion of the admission test.
The results of the admission test will be used to verify the need to assign Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) in basic disciplines (biology, chemistry, physics and mathematics) to be fulfilled within the first year of study.

UNIVERSITY: University of Trento
COURSE: [1001S] MEDICINE AND SURGERY
TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM: Single Cycle 6 Years Interuniversity Joint Degree
SECTION: Admission Procedure
URL: https://unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10739

Admission Procedure Access to the Course is nationally regulated in accordance with Law No. 264/1999. The number of students admitted is determined annually by Ministerial Decree, taking into account the training potential declared by the University based on available resources, teaching and clinical facilities, as well as the needs expressed by the Autonomous Province of Trento and the competent Ministry regarding the requirement for healthcare personnel of the relevant professional profile.
Candidates with a secondary school diploma or another foreign academic qualification recognized as equivalent may be admitted to the Course, provided they have passed the national admission test.
The national admission test, prepared by national competent bodies, consists of solving multiple-choice questions, for which the candidate must identify the single correct answer while discarding incorrect ones.
The questions are structured as follows: biology; chemistry; physics; mathematics; general culture and logical reasoning. Significant deficiencies in the above subjects may result in Additional Mandatory Training Requirements.
The ranking is national, merit-based, and individual. Admission rights are acquired by candidates based on the number of available places and their position in the ranking, which is ordered by decreasing score.

Location Hill Campus - Mesiano - Via Mesiano, 77 (Sustainable Use: 75)
Department Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering Required Knowledge Verification No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path The Master's Degree program in Civil Engineering-Architecture U.E. aims to train a highly qualified professional figure capable of designing works in the fields of architecture and urban planning, as well as directing and verifying the complete and correct execution of the designed work, with mastery of the specific methodologies and tools of engineering.
Based on this, the Master's Degree program is structured to ensure, in compliance with directives 85/384/EEC, 85/14/EEC, 86/17/EEC and related recommendations, a balanced distribution between theoretical and practical knowledge.
The fundamental educational objective is the integration of knowledge in the fields of architecture and urban planning according to a teaching approach aimed at preparing a synthesis process and a fundamental and qualifying moment of building.
The training aims to provide a scientific-technical culture that allows operating with specific competence and full responsibility in the design at various architectural and urban scales, technological and productive, and in the qualified control of realization.
The Master's Degree program essentially aims to integrate knowledge in the fields of architecture and urban planning with those typical of civil engineering - architecture, providing advanced training for the exercise of highly qualified activities in the fields of design, construction and management of the building process.
The teaching approach aims at preparation that identifies the project as a synthesis process and a fundamental and qualifying moment of building: the Master's graduate, in addition to possessing mastery of the necessary methodologies and operational tools for the conception of the work, must also be able to follow with competence the complete and correct execution.
The training is based on the acquisition of a solid scientific-technical culture well balanced by historical-critical contributions that allow Master's graduates to operate with specific competence and full responsibility in the fields of activities characteristic of building and architecture: programming, design at various scales, qualified control of realization, conservation of the building heritage.
In detail, the study program aims to train Master's graduates who are able to:
- use acquired knowledge to analyze, interpret and solve, also in an innovative way, complex or interdisciplinary project problems in architecture, building and urban planning;
- design and control, with mastery of tools related to the feasibility of the designed work, operations for modifying the physical environment (with full knowledge of different functional, distributive, formal, structural, technical-construction, management, economic and environmental aspects, as well as critical attention to cultural changes and needs expressed by contemporary society);
- coordinate, where necessary, other specialists and operators in the fields of architecture, civil engineering, urban planning and architectural restoration.
The organization of teaching aims to ensure the acquisition of creative abilities and professionalism related to the operational reality, which is presumed to be constantly evolving.
For this reason, experimental teaching paths (based on international contacts, professional internships, etc.) may be provided, which remain balanced from a humanistic and scientific perspective.
The path is organized into 8 cultural areas (called areas), listed below, to which the individual courses belong:
1. Area of the history of architecture and art;
2. Area of representation and survey;
3. Area of mathematics and physics;
4. Economic, legal and sociological area;
5. Area of architectural design and restoration;
6. Area of urban planning;
7. Area of building production and building technologies;
8. Area of design and structural technologies.
In addition to these, there is the final design laboratory and elective courses.
This structure privileges multidisciplinary cultural areas over traditional scientific-disciplinary sectors, to which courses are normally associated.
In this way, it is the coherence of the overall training path that is emphasized rather than the presence of individual ingredients, that is, the courses.
It is the areas, not the individual disciplinary sectors, that are awarded credit points; the subsequent division of credits within each area among the different courses is discretionary and represents the declination of a particular cultural project.
The course's educational offer is therefore structured in:
a) basic training activities, concentrated in the first three years, except for some specific deepening related to the synthesis laboratory at the end of the training path; basic training activities concern deepening related to the history of architecture and building, tools and forms of representation, theoretical-scientific aspects as well as methodological-operational aspects of mathematics and other basic sciences,
b) characteristic training activities, related to the theoretical-scientific aspects, as well as methodological-operational aspects, of the disciplinary areas characteristic of the study program, with particular reference to the disciplines of architecture and urban planning, building and confined environment,
c) integrative training activities, necessary to reach and connect the disciplinary field proper to architecture and engineering with scientific, technical, humanistic, legal, economic and socio-political culture.
Required Knowledge for Access To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Civil Engineering-Architecture, it is necessary to possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent, in accordance with paragraph 3 of Article 6 of Ministerial Decree 22 October 2004 n. 270.
Access to the Master's Degree program is programmed at the national level according to general criteria set by the Ministry of Education, University and Research (MIUR) in accordance with Article 9, paragraph 4, of Law n. 341/1990 and the Community Directive 384/85 EC.
The available places for admission to the Civil Engineering-Architecture program at the University of Trento for the academic year 2013-2014 are 100 (for EU and non-EU students residing in Italy), in accordance with Annex n. 4 of Ministerial Decree 24 April 2013 n. 334.
To access the study program, it is necessary to pass the mandatory national test organized by MIUR.
For this purpose, a sufficient general culture is required, with particular relevance to historical, social and institutional contexts, accompanied by the ability to work on written texts of various types (artistic, literary, historical, sociological, philosophical, etc.) and by aptitudes for logical-abstractive reasoning in both mathematical and linguistic contexts, in accordance with Ministerial Decree 24 April 2013 n. 334.
In particular, the admission test consists of solving sixty multiple-choice questions with five answer options, of which the candidate must identify only one, discarding incorrect, arbitrary or less probable conclusions, on topics of: general culture and logical reasoning; history, drawing and representation; mathematics and physics, in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 5 of Ministerial Decree 24 April 2013 n. 334.
General Culture and Logical Reasoning Assessment of the ability to logically complete a reasoning, consistently with the premises, which are stated in symbolic or verbal form through multiple-choice questions. The questions will cover scientific or narrative essays by classical or contemporary authors, or current affairs texts from newspapers or generalist or specialist magazines; they will also cover cases or problems, even of an abstract nature, whose solution requires the adoption of different forms of logical reasoning.
Questions related to general culture complete this evaluative area.
History The test aims to verify consistent general chronological criteria regarding key figures and significant historical phenomena (ancient age, high and low Middle Ages, modern age, contemporary age). Such general historical-chronological orientations will also be verified through the assessment of knowledge intertwined with specific artistic-architectural events (architectural works or artistic movements).
Drawing and Representation The test aims to assess the ability to analyze graphs, drawings and iconic representations or terms of correspondence with respect to the represented object, as well as to assess mastery of basic knowledge related to representation (plans, elevations, axonometries).
Mathematics and Physics The test aims to verify mastery of concepts related to:
- numerical sets and arithmetic calculation (natural, relative, rational, real numbers; ordering and comparison of numbers; order of magnitude; operations, powers, radicals, logarithms),
- algebraic calculation, Euclidean geometry (polygons, circumference and circle, measurements of lengths, surfaces and volumes, isometry, similarities and equivalences, geometric loci), analytic geometry (fundamentals), probability and statistics (fundamentals);
- basic knowledge of the principles of Mechanics: definition of fundamental physical quantities (displacement, velocity, acceleration, mass, momentum, force, weight, work and power); law of inertia, Newton's law and principle of action and reaction);
- basic knowledge of the principles of Thermodynamics (general concepts of temperature, heat, specific heat, expansion of bodies).

http://attiministeriali.miur.it/anno-2013/aprile/dm-24042013-(1).aspx Admission Procedures The Ministry of University and Research (MUR) publishes every year, through a decree, the national programmed number, that is, the quota of students admitted to the study program.
Enrollment in the Master's Degree program is governed by the regulations in force for access to university institutions: after completing secondary school studies in Italy, or with an equivalent diploma obtained abroad, it is required to pass the national mandatory test established by Ministerial Decree (Ministerial Decree n. 627 of 24-04-2024.pdf), with the related selection procedures defined in the University's call in accordance with current regulations.
The admission test involves solving multiple-choice questions (50) with five answer options (only one correct) on various topics: general culture and logical reasoning, history (including art history), drawing and representation, physics and mathematics (Ministerial Decree n. 627 Annex A.pdf).
The time available for the test is 100 minutes as established by the aforementioned decree.
The Course adopts the Arched test organized by the Interuniversity Consortium for Integrated Systems for Access (CISIA).
The Course adopts, as indicated in the admission call, for the academic year 2024-25 the online delivery method. The test for 2024 must be completed by September 30, 2024.
The tests for this year are scheduled for July 25 and September 3, 2024.
The tests will be conducted only in online mode (CISIA Arched platform).
If not all available places are assigned in the July selection, the University of Trento will proceed with the selection scheduled for September, through which any vacant places will be assigned.
Those who have taken the test in other locations, if places are available, may proceed with enrollment in the Course.
The Course does not organize any preparation course for the admission test. To improve their preparation, candidates may however use the archive of selection tests conducted in previous academic years currently available on the site: http://accessoprogrammato.miur.it (section dedicated to courses directly aimed at the profession of architect), complete with questions and answers.
The score obtained in the admission test may lead to the attribution of Additional Educational Obligation (OFA). In case the score obtained in the 'Physics and Mathematics' section of the admission test is below 3, the student will be required to attend mandatory tutoring activities, with a minimum attendance of 80%, within the 'Mathematical Analysis 1' course.
If students possess a language certification recognized by the University of Trento at a level corresponding to or higher than the required one, they may request direct attribution of credits related to the foreign language knowledge test. Recognized language certifications are listed in tables published at https://www.cla.unitn.it/575/certificazioni-hai-un-certificato.
Students coming from other university careers may request recognition of activities completed and credit recognition after enrollment in the Course.
Transfers from other locations or credit recognition from closed careers for graduation, decadenza, renunciation of studies or single courses are regulated by a specific Call, which is published annually at the following link https://offertaformativa.unitn.it/it/lmcu/ingegneria-edile-architettura/iscriversi.

Specific Educational Objectives and Description of the Study Path The Single Cycle Law Program aims to train the jurist who understands the legal phenomenon within the social, economic, and institutional reality.
The legal phenomenon cannot be confined in time and space and reduced to a single state legal system (the current Italian one), but must be studied and understood through comparison with others.
This applies both historically (diachronically) and in the contextual dimension (synchronously), with regard to legal systems that express a common evolutionary origin (such as Roman law), as well as to systems that refer to distinct foundational premises (for example, in extra-European contexts).
Comparison thus facilitates the understanding and critical knowledge of one's own legal system and, therefore, determines the acquisition of cultural and methodological foundations that serve as a prerequisite for solid professional knowledge.
This approach proves particularly relevant and current in our time, where phenomena such as European supranational integration, the globalization of social, economic, and cultural relations, and the development of technologies (among which, extremely important, information technologies and biosciences) require appropriate training for the jurist, who is expected to view the legal phenomenon as it manifests today in the global scenario with dialogic sensitivity and methodological skills enabling the exercise of adequate professionalism.
Given this, the curriculum of the Single Cycle Master's Degree Program in Law provides a path where, from the first year onwards, alongside traditional institutional courses (private law, Roman law, public law) and Philosophy of Law (which serves an immediate critical comparison with the phenomenon of normativity and its historical relativity), there are courses introducing comparative methods and the main reconstructions of legal systematics (Comparative Legal Systems), courses aimed at familiarizing students with the main and original institutional features of European integration (Institutions of European Union Law), and an additional course (more concise) on familiarizing students with major economic theories and their terminology (Introduction to Economics).
In the second and third years, the 'threads' introduced (institutional, historical-critical, comparative, European and international, economic) undergo progressive specialization.
The strictly institutional (public and private) strand specializes in the study, particularly, of Constitutional and Administrative Law, International Law, Civil and Commercial Law, Labor Law, and Criminal Law (basic and advanced).
The historical-critical strand specializes in the study of Medieval and Modern Legal History.
The economic strand specializes in the study of Economic Law.
In this, so to speak, 'central' phase of the curriculum, the student is also placed in a position to begin 'choosing' certain disciplines to complete their training (and thus their study plan) beyond the courses described, but always within the relevant scientific-disciplinary sectors and with a preference for highly active and innovative learning methods (procedural clinics, seminar teaching, etc.), and open to legal comparison.
To earn the credits reserved for student free choice, the path includes, besides a foreign language, a wide selection of courses belonging to multiple disciplines: this to allow each student a significant degree of flexibility in their individual training, even in light of the multiple career opportunities.
In the fourth and fifth years, the knowledge and skills acquired in previous specializations are completed (particularly regarding Medieval and Modern Legal History and Roman Law, as the catalyst for the foundations of European law) and are compared with the dynamics of procedural law (Civil, Criminal, and Administrative), leaving further space for free-choice courses (already mentioned) and for the in-depth study of topics related to the broad economic dimension of law (through the study of Tax Law and Advanced Commercial Law), as well as for the deep and reasoned experimentation of some critical and applied paths to improve argumentative skills (through advanced study of Philosophy of Law or, at the student's choice, Methodology of Legal Sciences).
Required Knowledge for Access Enrollment in the Single Cycle Master's Degree Program in Law is regulated by current regulations on access to university institutions. For admission to the Master's Degree Program in Law, a high school diploma or another foreign diploma recognized as suitable is required, in accordance with paragraph 3 of Article 6 of Ministerial Decree 22 October 2004, No. 270. The regulations for the admission of non-EU students not included in the category of Article 26 of Law 189/2002 are defined by the Ministry of Education, University, and Research (MIUR) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAE).
For admission to the Single Cycle Master's Degree Program in Law, general cultural knowledge, logical abilities, text comprehension skills, and analytical abilities are required. The responsible teaching structure may annually establish the verification of the aforementioned knowledge.

Admission Procedure The Single Cycle Degree Program in Law offered by the Faculty is a quota-limited program: until the academic year 2020/2021, 500 students were admitted annually; from the academic year 2021/2022, 600 students will be admitted.
Admission requires passing an entrance test, prepared with technical support from an external company, as is the case for all quota-limited programs at the Trento University.
Specifically, the test, since the academic year 2014/2015, is held twice a year: one session in April and a second session in August. The test consists of 50 general questions (aimed at verifying basic logical reasoning, text comprehension and analysis skills, and general knowledge) and 30 questions specific to the program (in this case, Law, assessing knowledge of basic aspects regarding the identity and functioning of national, European, and international political institutions).
Available places for each academic year are first allocated to candidates scoring above the minimum threshold of the entrance test. If not all places are allocated this way, candidates scoring below the minimum threshold may enroll, provided they complete the Additional Educational Requirements (AER) as specified in the annual Faculty portal announcements.
It is noteworthy that the high number of applicants for the entrance test, a trend now consolidated over time, ensures not only a credible selection process each year but also the maximum enrollment in the program. This figure confirms the enduring appeal of the Trento campus (with matriculations in recent years coming from outside the Trento Province for over 80% of students).

UNIVERSITY: University of Trento
COURSE: [0429H] ART HISTORY AND MUSEOLOGY
TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM: General Description
SECTION: General Description
URL: https://unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10753

[0429H] ART HISTORY AND MUSEOLOGY Master's Degree
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration
2 years Order
2022
Status Open Credits
120 CFU Type Master's degree programs Category Humanities and Linguistic Studies Regulation 270/04
Degree class LM-89 - Master's degree class in Art History Joint Course No Open Access Location City Campus - Palazzo Prodi - via Tommaso Gar, 14
Department Department of Letters and Philosophy Entry Requirements Verification No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The study program aims to provide, alongside a solid specialized knowledge of artworks (examined from a historical, stylistic, iconographic, and material perspective), a comprehensive understanding of modern museological theories and practices, integrated with experiences in cultural heritage mediation and cultural goods education.
Students will acquire, on one hand, specialized training in art history with a historical-philological approach oriented towards research, and on the other hand, develop operational skills related to museum professions, namely the protection, valorization, management, and conservation of historical-artistic heritage. Each student may determine, based on their inclinations, the predominance of one or the other approach when compiling their study plan.
Mandatory courses include those related to historical-artistic SSDs, half of which have a specific museological focus; these are supplemented by a course on cultural heritage legislation, aimed at enhancing students' skills in management and protection areas.
Graduates of the program will develop advanced and articulated critical competence in reading and interpreting artworks and their production context from the Middle Ages to the contemporary era, within a geographical perspective that is not only Italian but also European and global. They will also possess solid analytical and historical-philological research skills related to the history of artworks, collections, museums, and art literature; theoretical knowledge and practical abilities specifically connected to the museum field, particularly concerning the conservation and valorization of collections, organization of exhibitions, mediation and educational services for the public, including the use of discipline-specific information technology tools. To this end, students will carry out internships, traineeships, and laboratory activities at museums, galleries, and other public and private institutions responsible for managing and valorizing heritage, both in the Trentino territory and at national and international levels.
Master's graduates will be able to speak and write fluently in at least one European Union language in addition to Italian, with reference to disciplinary terminology.
Entry Requirements Specific entry requirements for the program are the possession of a bachelor's degree or a three-year university diploma or an equivalent foreign university degree, specific curricular requirements as indicated below, and adequate personal preparation that must be verified. Students must have acquired a minimum number of university credits (CFU) in specific scientific-disciplinary sectors as follows:
1. at least 48 CFU in group L-ANT, group L-ART, group M-STO, group L-FIL-LET, ICAR/16, ICAR/18;
2. of these, at least 24 must be in L-ART/01, L-ART/02, L-ART/03, L-ART/04, ICAR/16, ICAR/18.
Only candidates who meet the curricular requirements are admitted to the personal preparation verification. Personal preparation is considered adequate in case of a final degree mark of 100/110 or higher.
Candidates with a final degree mark below 100/110 must pass an interview to verify general knowledge in art history from the Middle Ages to the contemporary era.
In addition to Italian, knowledge of one further European language (English, French, Spanish, or German) at least at B1 level of the CEFR is required to access the Master's degree. The methods for verifying linguistic skills are defined in the Study Program Regulations.

UNIVERSITY: University of Trento
COURSE: [0423H] LINGUISTIC MEDIATION, TOURISM AND CULTURES
TYPE: Master's Degree
SECTION: General Description
URL: https://unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10165

[0423H] LINGUISTIC MEDIATION, TOURISM AND CULTURES Master's Degree
COURSE INFORMATION General information for the current academic year Duration
2 years Curriculum
2014
Status Open Credits
120 CFU Type Master's Degree Courses Category Humanities and Linguistic Studies Regulation Reform 270/04
Degree Class LM-49 - Master's Degree Class in Tourism System Design and Management Joint Course No Access Open Location City Campus - Palazzo Prodi - via Tommaso Gar, 14
Department Department of Economics and Management Department of Letters and Philosophy (Main)
Access Requirements Verification No Program, Texts and Objectives Specific Educational Objectives and Course Path Description The Master's Degree Course in Linguistic Mediation, Tourism and Cultures aims to train a professional figure in the tourism sector capable of managing offline and online communication and interaction processes between territorial tourism and cultural organizations and the international tourism market. This figure integrates a solid linguistic and cultural preparation with specific theoretical and practical knowledge of an economic, geographical, sociological and computer nature. The linguistic and cultural training will enable interaction between local culture and language and cultures and languages of different international contexts. The economic, geographical, sociological and computer training will allow an interdisciplinary analysis of social and territorial phenomena related to the tourism market, the physical and anthropic geography of the local context and international contexts, and tourism development processes. Computer skills will enable effective management of online communication through the use of various tools.
Particular emphasis will be placed on consolidating the two languages studied in the three-year path, which will be refined in terms of analysis, intercultural skills and communication processes, complemented by the study of the language and culture of a third area – chosen between Russian and Chinese – enabling opening towards new tourism flows with distinctive characteristics in terms of profile and motivations.
At the same time, thanks to the in-depth study of analytical tools in economics and marketing, students will be provided with the necessary knowledge to manage and design, in collaboration with other professional figures, cultural (performances, exhibitions, editorial activities, etc.) and environmental interventions and services that enhance and qualify the existing offer. Moreover, precisely due to the course's intercultural vocation, it will be possible to support the paradigm of sustainable tourism, with particular attention to the identification, valorization and recovery of natural and cultural resources of the territory.
Access Requirements For the Master's Degree Course in Linguistic Mediation, Tourism and Cultures, admission is open to those who have obtained a three-year university degree or diploma, or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent (art. 6, paragraphs 2 and 3 of D.M. 270/2004).
An advanced knowledge of two of the following languages of study: English-French-German-Spanish, and their cultural history is required; good knowledge of the economic sector of business economics and management, with particular reference to marketing, strategy and business organization; good knowledge of political economy; good knowledge in geographical disciplines, with particular attention to the spatial distribution of main types of tourism areas and the identification of the tourism potential of natural and cultural landscapes.
The methods for verifying such preparation will be regulated in the didactic regulations.

Department Department of Letters and Philosophy Prerequisites for admission No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's Degree in Euro-American Literatures, Translation and Literary Criticism aims to provide specialized knowledge of two languages and their respective literatures in order to deepen both the relationships between different cultural traditions and the study of literary texts, in both their thematic and formal aspects, using the methodologies of linguistics, philology and literary criticism.
Upon completion of the Master's Degree, graduates will possess:
- advanced linguistic competence;
- adequate literary and cultural translation skills, generally from and into the two chosen languages;
- in-depth knowledge of the literary traditions and cultural contexts of the languages studied. These educational objectives will be achieved through lectures and seminars, without excluding student participation in translation workshops and computer workshops.
Acquired knowledge will be regularly assessed throughout the course, culminating in final examinations that verify the achievement of educational objectives. A fundamental role is played by agreements, including double degrees, with institutions that allow students to further develop their skills at universities and research centers in Europe and beyond. Similar agreements with institutions responsible for the valorization and protection of linguistic minorities present in the territory also play an important role.
Prerequisites for admission For admission to the Master's Degree in Euro-American Literatures, Translation and Literary Criticism, students with an eligible degree must have earned the required credits in the different scientific-disciplinary sectors determined by the didactic regulations.
In any case, competence in two foreign languages at an appropriate level (C1 according to the Common European Framework) is required, as well as adequate historical-literary knowledge of the respective cultures and computer skills.
Verification of the required knowledge for admission will always take place through an interview.

Program, texts, and objectives Specific educational goals of the course and description of the study path
Specific educational goals of the Master's Degree Course in "Philosophy and Languages of Modernity" are, on one hand, the refinement of knowledge of the history of philosophical thought from antiquity to the present day, including its more specific aspects and its relations with the tradition of scientific and religious thought; on the other hand, the refinement of knowledge of the various aspects of philosophical research in theoretical, ethical, religious, political, aesthetic, linguistic, logical, and epistemological fields, with particular attention to the most recent developments of the philosophical debate.
Extensive space will be devoted to the in-depth study of texts belonging to the philosophical tradition and those belonging to the historical-philosophical and hermeneutical tradition, as well as to the in-depth study of the various forms of philosophical research and the acquisition of analytical, logical-argumentative, and critical evaluation skills aimed at achieving advanced autonomy in reflection and discussion on philosophical topics in both historical and theoretical contexts.
Acknowledging the relevance of other disciplines in contemporary philosophical debate, as well as the contribution of philosophical thought to various theoretical and applied domains, the course includes not only teachings traditionally belonging to the philosophical field itself, but also related teachings in pedagogical, psychological, sociological, religious, linguistic, mathematical, literary, and historical areas.
This expansion of perspective, in addition to improving the quality of training, aims to diversify the professional profiles of graduates, in order to transmit knowledge, skills, and competencies that enable access to specialized sectors of the labor market.
These educational goals will also be achieved through the structuring of the educational offer into study plans aimed at particularly emphasizing the historical-philosophical and humanities field, the ethical, political, and religious field, and the logical and mathematical field.
Access to specialized professional sectors is also facilitated by the targeted activation of internships, traineeships, and specific training activities, as well as by acquiring advanced knowledge of at least one European Union language other than Italian, chosen from German, Spanish, French, English.
Language learning in general is also supported to foster contacts with foreign universities and student mobility in European and extra-European contexts, a privileged means for encountering and gaining knowledge of different study topics, research methodologies, and cultural contexts.
The educational path is structured into teaching activities aimed at acquiring specialized knowledge in the areas defined above and the related methodological competencies. The evaluation moments of the acquired competencies will consider both theoretical knowledge and methodological and analytical abilities.
Required knowledge for access For the purpose of accessing the Master's Degree in Philosophy and Languages of Modernity, students holding an eligible degree must have earned the necessary credits in the various scientific-disciplinary sectors determined by the Didactic Regulations.
Verification of the required knowledge for access will take place in any case through an interview. Such knowledge must also include computer science skills and a sufficient mastery of at least one European Union foreign language.
The methods for assessing the comprehensive set of required knowledge and competencies will be regulated in the Didactic Regulations.

Department Department of Letters and Philosophy Entry requirements verification No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path Based on the knowledge and skills acquired during the first cycle of university studies, the Master's Degree in Linguistics and Literary Criticism aims to provide students with in-depth methodological, historical and critical training in linguistic, philological and literary disciplines from antiquity to the contemporary era. In particular, the course aims to provide the following competencies:
- Ability to analyze any type of text in all linguistic, philological, stylistic, historical-literary aspects;
- Ability to elaborate complex texts;
- Ability to organize and produce compilative texts;
- Textual and editing skills;
- Ability to use main computer tools in specific areas of competence.
Graduates must therefore possess solid literary and linguistic knowledge, with particular experience in direct analysis of texts and documents. They must demonstrate full mastery of at least one EU language, in addition to Italian. The teaching delivery methods for courses included in the training path respond to the types of frontal lectures and seminar activities; frontal lectures and seminar activities aim to develop students' critical and presentation skills, both oral and written.
The training path includes specialized study of themes related to the cultural heritage transmitted from classical civilization to Italian literature, through the novel world, within the context of European literary civilization. Two standard pathways are offered:
- Classical Philology: focused on the study of Greek and Latin language and literature;
- Modern Philology: focused on the linguistic and philological study of medieval and modern literatures with particular reference to Italian literature.
Entry requirements
1. Required knowledge for entry Students intending to enroll in the Master's Degree in Linguistics and Literary Criticism must hold an appropriate academic qualification and must have earned, during previous studies, at least 60 CFU in disciplines of the following SSD: L-FIL-LET; L-ART; L-ANT; M-STO; L-LIN, M-GGR. In particular, the following are required:
24 earned in the following areas: L-FIL-LET/10 Italian Literature, L-FIL-LET/11 Contemporary Italian Literature, L-FIL-LET/12 Italian Linguistics, L-FIL-LET/13 Philology of Italian Literature, L-FIL-LET/14 Literary Criticism and Comparative Literature.
Students not holding the required credits may obtain them by enrolling in single courses at the undergraduate level. Additionally, admission requires IT skills and adequate mastery of at least one EU language.
2. Method of verifying initial preparation A teaching committee, appointed annually within the teaching area, will assess candidates' competencies through an interview. Exempt from the interview are graduates of the three-year degree course in Historical and Philological-Literary Studies (Classical Letters and Modern Letters paths) and graduates of the three-year degree course in Letters (Ordinamento 509) of the University of Trento.

Department Department of Sociology and Social Research Required knowledge verification for admission No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path Graduates of the Master's degree in Sociology and Social Research must:
- possess a deep understanding of the most advanced developments of models for analyzing social structure and cultural analysis (Social structure and inequalities; Sociology of culture);
- possess advanced knowledge of the logical-conceptual and methodological tools necessary for all phases of social research: hypothesis formulation; research design; data collection, construction and processing (Research methodology and design; Quantitative methods of social research; Qualitative methods of social research; related laboratories; computer skills);
- possess advanced knowledge of methods and techniques for analyzing social phenomena, with particular reference to classification, processing and analysis of quantitative and qualitative data (Social statistics; methodology laboratories);
- possess advanced knowledge of methodologies and analytical tools of historical and political sciences (Historical research methods; Political research methods);
- be able to conduct in-depth analyses on substantive fields of social research, such as welfare regimes, public policies, social change, intergenerational relations, collective action dynamics, gender differences;
- be able to analyze communication processes and cultural dynamics of advanced societies, such as value changes, public opinion, mass society and media systems, social networks, consumption dynamics, myths, symbols and rituals, sociology of language, daily life, science-society relations, religion's role and secularization processes;
- possess and develop language skills (English language) (other activities; examination texts in English).
The training path is structured in a first year with strong methodological emphasis and a second year with a more substantive and disciplinary focus. In the first year, students acquire skills related to research design and quantitative and qualitative, historical and political research methods, with strong investment in integrated laboratory activities. In the second year, through the choice of substantive courses of a study track, the free-choice exam, the internship and the thesis topic, students acquire substantive specialization.
Required knowledge for admission To successfully enter and progress in the Master's degree program in Sociology and Social Research, a solid foundation in basic sociological subjects is required, including major classical and contemporary sociological theories, social sciences methodology, and methods and techniques of research in the social sciences.
Additionally, a basic preparation in disciplines related to sociology such as history, cultural anthropology, psychology, law, economics, political science, and philosophy is necessary.
Finally, specific preparation in quantitative mathematical and statistical methods for analyzing social phenomena and knowledge of the English language is required.
The study program's didactic regulations will precisely define the specific formal requirements for admission to the Master's degree program. The didactic regulations will also define the methods for verifying the adequacy of personal preparation.

[0804H] STUDIES ON INTERNATIONAL SECURITY Master's Degree InteruniversityJoint Title English
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration

2024

Master's degree class LM-52 - Class of Master's degrees in International Relations Joint course Partner universities Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna - School for Advanced Studies and Perfectionment Quota-limited (27 places)
Location City campus - Palazzo Prodi - via Tommaso Gar, 14 (Sustainable capacity: 26)
Department School of International Studies Entry requirements No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's degree in International Security Studies (MISS) trains graduates with the necessary theoretical, conceptual and analytical tools to understand the complexity and multiplicity of issues related to national, international, transnational and global security through an inter- and multi-disciplinary approach. The study programme prepares students for highly qualified roles and responsible positions concerning the design, implementation and monitoring of security policies, participating in analytical, implementation and evaluation processes of national and international intervention programmes with a leadership role.
The specific educational objectives of the course are:
a) To be able to identify, understand and analyse issues related to national and international security, evaluating actions and tools for managing and responding to crises, conflicts, and security challenges at transnational and global levels;
b) To be able to coordinate and contribute to the design, drafting, implementation and monitoring of programmes and policies aimed at preventing, containing and countering major international security challenges;
c) To be able to understand the socio-political, legal, economic, ethical implications of major issues related to national and international security, and the mechanisms through which such implications are manifested;
d) To develop a critical understanding of theoretical approaches and internal debates in security studies, conflict studies, political violence, and the elaboration of public policies concerning the containment of risks and threats, independently developing original analyses on these topics and using multiple analytical and methodological tools;
e) To develop the ability to articulate a specific topic related to national and international security by drawing on different disciplinary perspectives and approaches such as political science, law, economics, to address diverse audiences and convey analyses and evaluations through different formats;
f) To be able to analyse how national, transnational, and international security issues are addressed and debated by a plurality of actors at multiple levels, including the role of national and international institutions, regional and non-governmental organizations, and social movements;
g) To acquire and refine skills and abilities in synthesis, communication, relationship management, project management, and decision-making necessary in multidisciplinary and responsible work environments.
These skills and abilities will be stimulated and developed through continuous attention to interactive and participatory teaching methods, and the inclusion of seminar formats on advanced and specific topics.
The structure of the training path is divided between the two locations and concentrates lectures and exams in 3 semesters, while the second semester of the second year is dedicated by students to a mobility experience that, although not strictly aimed at attending courses and taking exams, enriches their educational experience (internships, thesis research abroad). From the perspective of the educational offer content, the study path is characterized by a continuous dialogue and cross-pollination between disciplinary approaches, and aims to combine a more traditional state-centric interpretation of security, typical of strategic studies and military studies, with a more extended conceptualization that has developed over the last three decades. Courses therefore integrate different interpretations of the concept of security such as human security, societal security, economic and financial security, environmental and climate security, resource and food security, cyber and digital security. Particular importance is given to the critical approach (critical security studies), which emphasizes the social construction of the very definition of security and insecurity, and to the emerging agenda aimed at moving beyond an exclusively Euro-centric perspective on these issues. The MISS programme is structured to offer a wide range of compulsory, constrained choice, and optional courses that stimulate students to follow their intellectual and professional interests and develop an area of specialization independently, while respecting the inter- and multi-disciplinary nature of the study programme and thus maintaining balance between different disciplinary fields regarding both core and related activities. Constrained choice courses are grouped in clusters of 2-3 courses sharing thematic and/or disciplinary coherence. Regarding the historical field (core activities), the maximum credit range is 18, when normally it should not exceed double the minimum (12). However, it is considered useful and appropriate to offer students the possibility to choose, among the optional courses for acquiring free-choice credits, also courses originally designed as constrained choice but not selected in that format by the student. The rationale, more generally, is to offer as flexible and customizable a range of courses as possible for acquiring free-choice credits, within the limits of the pedagogical functionality of the study programme. In this sense, the number of free-choice credits is 18, consistently also with the objective of valuing the skills of the respective faculties, and therefore the inter-university nature of the Master's, realizing "research-driven" courses.
Finally, during the first year, students will have the opportunity to attend the Applied Workshops on Global Affairs, organized annually by the School of International Studies (from academic year 2019/2020), aimed at bridging the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical skills through innovative and laboratory-based learning methods (simulations, debates, role-playing games, moot courts, and theme-based seminars) and involving experts, officials, practitioners, and professionals from backgrounds not necessarily and/or exclusively academic. During the second year, students will acquire 3 ECTS through a series of professionalizing activities, which also value the network of institutional partners of both locations.
Entry requirements The MISS Master's is quota-limited and requires selection among students who meet minimum curricular requirements and demonstrate adequate personal preparation.
Minimum curricular requirements:
Access is conditional on holding a first-level degree, obtained at Italian universities or another foreign degree deemed suitable. Suitable first-level degrees are those whose study curriculum includes at least 60 ECTS credits related to courses belonging to at least two of the following disciplinary groups:
historical and philosophical; economic; legal; political; sociological; linguistic. For each disciplinary group, the following scientific-disciplinary sectors are specified:
- historical and philosophical group: L-OR/01, L-OR/10, L-OR/14, L-OR/17, L-OR/23, M-FIL/02, M-FIL/03, M-FIL/06, M-STO/01, M-STO/02, M-STO/03, M-STO/04, M-FIL/01, M-FIL/02, M-FIL/03, M-FIL/04, M-FIL/05, M-FIL/06, SECS-P/12, SPS/02, SPS/03, SPS/05, SPS/06, SPS/13, SPS/14;
- economic group: M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02, SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/04, SECS-P/05, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/10, SECS-P/11, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/04, SECS-S/05, SECS-S/06;
- legal group: IUS/01, IUS/02, IUS/03, IUS/04, IUS/05, IUS/06, IUS/07, IUS/08,
IUS/09, IUS/10, IUS/11, IUS/12, IUS/13, IUS/14, IUS/15, IUS/16, IUS/17, IUS/20, IUS/21;
- political group: SPS/01, SPS/04;
- sociological group: M-DEA/01, M-PED/01, M-PSI/05, SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/10, SPS/11, SPS/12;
- linguistic group: L-LIN/03, L-LIN/04, L-LIN/05, L-LIN/06, L-LIN/07, L-LIN/08, L-LIN/09, L-LIN/10, L-LIN/11, L-LIN/12, L-LIN/13, L-LIN/14, L-LIN/21, L-OR/09, L-OR/12, L-OR/13, L-OR/15, L-OR/21, L-OR/22.
Adequate personal preparation:
Access is also conditional on meeting language requirements. In particular:
1. Knowledge of English at least at level B2;
2. Knowledge of a second language at least at level A2 and different from Italian, among the following languages: Arabic, Chinese, French, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, German.
The methods for verifying adequate personal preparation are specified in the didactic regulations.
Selection is carried out based on educational and professional experiences, verified through the evaluation of the curriculum, supplementary documentation, and the titles specified in the admission notice, and on criteria determined in detail by an annual appointed Evaluation Committee.

Admission Procedures The MISS is a limited-enrollment Master's program that requires selection among students who meet minimum requirements. To be admitted to the MISS, students must meet language requirements (English and a second language) and disciplinary requirements (in terms of a minimum number of credits acquired in specific disciplinary areas listed in the call). Program, Texts, and Objectives Specific Educational Objectives of the Course and Description of the Study Path The Master's Degree in Security, Intelligence and Strategic Studies aims, in accordance with the qualifying educational objectives of the reference class and thanks to the program's structure across four different periods of international mobility, to provide advanced preparation in political, legal, economic, sociological, and historical disciplines, enabling the ability to address key theoretical and practical issues in three core sectors: security, intelligence, and strategic studies.
The multidisciplinary nature of the Master's program, cooperation between universities of different traditions and approaches, and the international dimension of the analyzed phenomena contribute to forming professional profiles possessing theoretical knowledge and analytical methods capable of fully understanding the theoretical concepts informing current debates on security studies, intelligence, and strategic studies. Upon completion of the program, Master's graduates will have acquired in-depth knowledge of the main themes and theoretical concepts related to international security studies, both through the examination of more orthodox approaches and through reference to the so-called 'critical security studies'. Additionally, they will have gained familiarity with the main debates and ideas associated with realism on one hand, and 'human security' on the other, as well as approaches linked to feminism, emancipation, and post-colonialism. Through this comprehensive perspective, Master's graduates will have developed a full awareness and critical understanding of the concept of security in contemporary international political contexts.
In particular, through in-depth case studies, Master's graduates will have learned the evolution of national grand strategies as tools for pursuing and defending national interest and security. Direct study of primary sources will have enabled graduates to identify how state authorities implement processes for defining their national security strategic documents. Through knowledge of various theoretical approaches, Master's graduates will also have acquired understanding of the main determinants of state power tools used to pursue and defend national interest.
Methodologically, Master's graduates will have mastered empirical research methods and competencies specific to intelligence activities and security-related professions, enabling them to critically address and resolve problems arising from the application of security, intelligence, and strategic policies. In particular, Master's graduates will have developed the ability to analyze the multidisciplinary dimensions of human security issues related to the causes of conflicts, identifying, interpreting, and connecting social, institutional, economic, and political elements that fuel them. Graduates will recognize the relevance of factors related to economic geography, environmental protection, and resource exploitation in the global context, the role of religious phenomena in internal and international conflicts, the balance of powers, as well as the dynamics of opposition and social conflict. In this context, they will have acquired: a) understanding of territorial and resource conflicts and their impact on migration phenomena and global imbalances; b) understanding of the role of international law in resource allocation and protection of economic and social rights; c) understanding of the key features of internal state social conflicts and the role played by social movements; d) understanding of the role of symbolic sources of power, from a historical and political perspective, with particular reference to religious and ideological factors in the Middle Eastern context.
Upon completion of the program, through case studies analysis and understanding how historical, social, legal, and economic factors influence security issues, graduates will have learned to identify risks and threats (traditional and non-traditional) to security. Master's graduates will have developed interdisciplinary knowledge enabling them to navigate the complexity of the international landscape and contribute to the definition of policies, strategies, and activities of public and private institutions, intergovernmental and national organizations operating in the international field and engaged in activities or locations exposed to high levels of social, political, economic, and military risk. They will be able to evaluate the genesis and functions of national grand strategies, analyzing the impacts of intervention programs and appreciating the ethical dilemmas posed by the adoption of securitization policies and technological development in this sector at the national, European, and international levels.
Furthermore, through a practical and experiential learning approach (reinforced by internship opportunities), Master's graduates will be able to design, formulate, implement, and monitor national and international security policies, also with reference to strengthening institutional human rights, consolidating democratization processes, and protecting victims of crimes against humanity.
Through access to at least two mandatory international mobility experiences, Master's graduates will have also gained a broad intercultural understanding of security-related issues, thanks to the program's structure. Networking of skills and academic and non-academic contacts across three different universities will ensure a current educational offer with extensive opportunities for interaction with sector operators.
The Master's program is structured over two years, to be completed at the University of Glasgow, the University of Trento, and Charles University Prague. The Master's Degree is structured across four different mobility periods, enabling the acquisition of 120 ECTS credits (30 of which must be completed in Trento to obtain the degree).
Students will complete the four mobility periods as follows:
1) Glasgow (first mobility, 1 semester, September-December);
2) Trento (second mobility, 1 semester, February-May), followed by a flexible period to allow for exams and other activities;
3) Prague (third mobility, 1 semester, September-February);
4) One of the three previous locations, chosen based on the thesis or internship supervisor's location (fourth mobility, 1 semester, March-August).
The mandatory training activities in the first and second mobility periods ensure the acquisition of theoretical knowledge and analytical skills related to intelligence, strategic studies, and security. In particular, during the period at the University of Trento, students must complete four mandatory courses in different disciplinary areas to develop the ability to understand the multidisciplinary dimensions of human security issues related to conflict causes.
The wide range of constrained elective activities in political science (offered during the mobility period in Prague), combined with students' choice of a core prerequisite activity from a limited set of related SSD courses, allows students to build a personalized study path focusing on more specific dimensions of security and strategic studies (such as regional issues or those related to technological development).
Master's graduates will have acquired adequate computer skills through specialized laboratories within the core courses and/or methodological laboratories for thesis writing.
In light of the above, Master's graduates in Security, Intelligence, and Strategic Studies will have acquired, through a practical and experiential learning approach:
- a full understanding of the theoretical concepts informing current debates on security studies, intelligence, and strategic studies;
- the necessary competencies to critically address problems arising from the application of policies in security, intelligence, and strategic studies;
- the necessary competencies to analyze the multidisciplinary dimensions of conflict causes, identifying, interpreting, and connecting social, institutional, economic, and political elements that fuel them;
- the ability to interact and relate with sector operators, from academic staff to non-academic personnel from businesses, non-governmental organizations, and public institutions;
- an intercultural understanding of security-related issues, thanks to participatory learning opportunities during the program;
- the ability to practically apply the skills acquired during the program within the professional profiles outlined in this curriculum.
Admission Requirements Admission to the Master's Degree in Security, Intelligence, and Strategic Studies is conditional upon meeting curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation.
The required curricular requirements consist of holding a three-year degree in one of the following classes: L-5 Philosophy, L-6 Geography, L-10 Letters, L-14 Legal Services Sciences, L-18 Economics and Business Management Sciences, L-33 Economic Sciences, L-36 Political Sciences and International Relations, L-37 Social Sciences for Cooperation, Development, and Peace, L-40 Sociology, L-42 History, or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent.
These curricular requirements must be met prior to verification of personal preparation.
Personal preparation will be verified through methods specified in the course's didactic regulations.
The required personal preparation for admission also includes written and oral knowledge at B2 level in English and another language different from Italian.

[0624H] ORGANIZATION, SOCIETY AND TECHNOLOGY Master's Degree
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration 2 years Curriculum 2021 Status Open Credits 120 ECTS Type Master's Degree Programs Category Sociology and International Studies Regulation Reform 270/04 Degree Class LM-88 - Master's Degree Class in Sociology and Social Research Interuniversity Course No Open Access Location City Campus - Sociology - via Verdi, 26 Department Department of Sociology and Social Research Verification of required knowledge for access No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the study path In line with the educational objectives of the Master's Degree Class in Sociology and Social Research, the Master's graduate in Organization, Society and Technology (OST) will have acquired:
- advanced knowledge of sociological disciplines and skills in analyzing and interpreting social phenomena related to organizational processes and the implementation of new technologies;
- knowledge and skills in psychological, political, historical, philosophical, legal, and economic disciplines useful for understanding the dynamics involved in organizational processes mediated by digital technologies;
- research methodology skills, enabling the conduct of empirical research and action research in specific contexts, to decipher organizational needs, criticalities, vulnerabilities, and requirements in contexts where human subjects and technological devices are in continuous and reciprocal interaction;
- factual knowledge and skills regarding intervention strategies in organizational contexts to promote innovation or harmonize the use of technologies with work processes;
- ability to orient in the job market and position oneself through internships, traineeships, in-depth seminars, workshops, and other forms of interaction with economic actors, thereby developing more application-oriented skills and strengthening ties with stakeholders and the labor market;
- linguistic knowledge, with particular reference to the English language.
Maintaining an interdisciplinary profile, the Master's Degree in Organization, Society and Technology trains Master's graduates who can perform high-responsibility functions in public or private institutions and organizations. The OST Master's graduate will be able to decipher organizational needs, criticalities, and vulnerabilities in the personal and interpersonal dynamics of members and work teams within an organization. The OST Master's graduate, working in synergy with other professional figures involved in the design and implementation of new technologies (managers, engineers, computer scientists, designers), will be able to harmonize social practices and dynamics in the adoption and development of technological innovations within specific work, organizational, and social contexts. During the first year of the course, the main theoretical teachings related to the fields of organizational and work sociology, organizational psychology, and social studies of science and technology (historical, sociological, and philosophical) are delivered, along with methodological teachings. In the first year, students of the Master's in Organization, Society and Technology will also acquire legal and political knowledge that forms part of the study path. In the second year, both methodological teachings with an applied character and sociological teachings are delivered, allowing students to deepen their knowledge of theoretical approaches and sociological studies on organizational, technological, and innovative processes.
In addition, through both methodological and laboratory courses, as well as through a specific program of seminars and workshops with actors from the business world, students will acquire:
- ability to apply knowledge gained in courses to operational contexts for problem-solving, adapting technological innovations to organizational and social dynamics in work contexts;
- ability to cooperate with experts from diverse backgrounds in multidisciplinary contexts and work in teams;
- communication skills, such as writing and presenting a project outline clearly and effectively;
- ability to learn in concrete situations, in organizational contexts where one must operate to harmonize work practices with technological systems, decipher vulnerabilities and criticalities, and plan strategies to resolve them;
- independent judgment, provided by the ability to go beyond acquired knowledge, critically elaborating and applying it to specific contexts.
Required knowledge for access Admission to the program is conditional on possessing the following curricular requirements:
a bachelor's degree or university diploma obtained after a course of study lasting at least three years in the following degree classes: L16 (Sciences of Administration and Organization), L36 (Political Sciences and International Relations), L39 (Social Service), L40 (Sociology), or another degree obtained abroad and recognized as suitable;
or a bachelor's degree or university diploma obtained after a course of study lasting at least three years or another degree obtained abroad and recognized as suitable, and possession of at least 60 ECTS credits related to courses belonging to at least two of the following disciplinary groupings (or equivalent, in the case of degrees obtained abroad and deemed equivalent to the bachelor's degree):
- sociological grouping: SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/10, SPS/11, SPS/12;
- historical-philosophical grouping: M-FIL/01, M-FIL/02, M-FIL/03, M-FIL/04, M-FIL/05, M-FIL/06, M-STO/02, M-STO/04, L-ANT/09;
- geographical-economic-statistical grouping: M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02, SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/04, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/10, SECS-P/12, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/04, SECS-S/05;
- political-legal grouping: SPS/01, SPS/02, SPS/03, SPS/04, SPS/06, IUS/07, IUS/09, IUS/13, IUS/14;
- psychological-pedagogical and anthropological grouping: M-PSI/01, M-PSI/02, M-PSI/03, M-PSI/04, M-PSI/05, M-PSI/06, M-PSI/07, M-PED/01, M-PED/02, M-DEA/01;
- civil engineering and architecture grouping: ICAR/03, ICAR/06, ICAR/13, ICAR/14, ICAR/15, ICAR/20, ICAR/21;
- engineering-informatics and mathematical grouping: INF/01, ING/INF-03, ING/INF-05, ING-IND/35, MAT/04, MAT/05;
- linguistic-literary grouping: L-LIN/01, L-LIN/10, L-LIN/12, L-FIL-LET/11, L-FIL-LET/12, L-ART/05, L-ART/06, L-ART/07.
In addition, the following personal preparation requirements apply:
- English language knowledge at B1 level (Common European Framework of Reference);
- sufficient personal preparation, verified through the grade of the first-level degree according to the procedures specified in the course's teaching regulations.
The student must possess the curricular requirements before verifying personal preparation; in particular, no additional academic debts or supplementary academic obligations are permitted.
