Department Department of Sociology and Social Research Entry Requirements Verification No Course Program, Texts and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The specific educational objectives to be achieved through the Master's Degree are:
- Acquisition by students of competencies in the direction, coordination, programming, management, organization and evaluation of social, socio-health, socio-educational and employment integration services.
While maintaining a focus on the methodology and organization of social services, particular attention has been given in the new order to provide competencies through specific courses on the organization of social services, evaluation of social and socio-health services, applied research techniques for services and social policies, economic management and management and organization of new third-sector organizations operating within the broader framework of so-called social innovation;
- Development of the ability to connect theoretical knowledge acquired in lectures with the practical reality of services and intervention programs. All courses have a focus not only nominal but also substantive on social services; the aim is to create teaching driven by excellence research lines but closely linked to the operational reality of services and their evolution.
- Development of self-reflection and learning from field experience. All courses will be structured to promote and develop the ability to analyze reflexively the objects of study. For this purpose, courses based on the experimentation of practices and work tools, analysis of empirical evidence, and close connection of courses with research and multidisciplinarity will be prioritized.
Entry Requirements For successful enrollment and progression in the Master's Degree program in Methodology, Organization and Evaluation of Social Services, the following are required:
- Adequate preparation in the analysis of social issues and social research, psychology, public and administrative law, as well as economics and basic economic disciplines (refer to the disciplinary groups indicated below);
- Preliminary preparation on the topic of work in social services. This knowledge can be certified through the completion of training internships in social services professions for a minimum of 10 credits or through the evaluation of equivalent professional experiences. Annually, the responsible structure determines the possible admission procedures for candidates who do not possess this requirement or possess it partially. Candidates who acquire the required internship credits and meet the criteria specified in the following paragraphs may enroll in the Master's Degree program.
- Specific preparation in at least one European Union language;
- A motivation letter in which candidates describe their interests, motivations for applying to the Master's Degree, professional and personal expectations. A positive evaluation of the motivation letter is an indispensable condition for admission to the course.
The minimum level of required knowledge includes the equivalent of at least 30 credits related to courses belonging to at least 2 of the following disciplinary groups (or equivalents, in the case of foreign degrees deemed equivalent to the bachelor's degree):
- Sociological grouping: SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/10, SPS/11, SPS/12;
- Economic grouping: SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08;
- Psychopedagogical grouping: M-PED/01, M-PED/03, M-PED/04, M-PSI/01, M-PSI/04, M-PSI/05, M-PSI/06, M-PSI/08;
- Legal grouping: IUS/01, IUS/09, IUS/10.
Additionally, candidates with a bachelor's degree grade below 90/110 must pass a selective admission interview.

[0623H] GLOBAL AND LOCAL STUDIES Master's Degree English Italian
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration
2 years Order
2020
Status Open Credits
120 CFU Type Master's Degree Program Category Sociology and International Studies Regulation Reform 270/04
Master's Degree Class LM-62 - Class of Master's Degrees in Political Science Interdepartmental Course No Open Access Location City Campus - Sociology - via Verdi, 26
Department Department of Sociology and Social Research Access Requirements Verification No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Global and Local Studies (Glocal Studies) program aims to train professionals capable of designing and guiding public policies and development interventions by combining the analysis of local context peculiarities with the analysis of global processes affecting them. The graduate will be able to rigorously analyze the local context in light of changes induced by global dynamics, manage participatory processes aimed at producing public policy decisions, interact with multilevel decision-making processes and institutions, and provide local actors with comprehensive knowledge regarding development opportunities. More specifically, the graduate will be a professional: a) expert and consultant in public policies operating within local, national, and international organizations, whether governmental or non-governmental; b) consultant for territorial projects, with analytical skills applicable to the design and implementation of development and governance interventions in local contexts. In general, the program prepares students to analyze and intervene in specific territorial areas and at different scales, with awareness of the global processes affecting them. The term Glocal, acquired and consolidated in social, political, and territorial studies for several decades, refers precisely to processes that intersect, concretize, and locally shape globalization dynamics, constituting a particular subject of study for the program. The program is characterized by a strongly interdisciplinary approach, grounded in political, sociological, historical, economic, and legal-institutional studies.
During the first year, students will acquire:
- Research methodology skills, both quantitative and qualitative, enabling the conduct of empirical research, whether based on primary or secondary data. Specifically, students will learn methods and techniques for collecting, processing, and analyzing data, both statistical (from questionnaire design to result coding) and ethnographic (from conducting interviews and focus groups to observation) related to the study areas covered by the program;
- Factual knowledge regarding social, political, economic, and historical processes related to globalization, enabling the specification and documentation of multilevel challenges affecting local contexts;
- Ability to define a specialization area among various possible thematic fields. The program's teaching offer explores and deepens heterogeneous glocalization processes concerning environmental and migration issues, urban and territorial dynamics, national and European policies, development cooperation, conflict, and democratization;
- Skills in designing and managing research, action research, and policies, forming professionals capable of following the empirical implementation of acquired knowledge at every stage, from design and planning to public reporting of investigations and implemented interventions within local development and governance contexts;
- Language knowledge, with particular reference to English. The Master's program offers mandatory courses in both Italian and English, allowing students to practice written and oral expression in multiple languages through participatory teaching.
In the second year of the program, students will deepen, based on their chosen path, public policy analysis or theories of local and territorial development. Students may also choose to deepen their knowledge in various areas concerning the environment, migration dynamics, ethnic relations, geography and demography, transformations of democracy, and political culture. These courses are particularly important for acquiring theoretical and empirical knowledge on socio-political dynamics characterizing specific activity areas, such as environmental sustainability or the reception of refugees and immigrants.
Through the training activities and internship opportunities offered by the program, graduates will have acquired a series of soft skills, including:
- Ability to work in multidisciplinary contexts, collaborating with people possessing diverse disciplinary backgrounds;
- Communication skills, such as writing and presenting a policy brief and/or project outline clearly and effectively;
- Ability to research information from online and offline sources, discerning reliability and credibility;
- Ability to work in teams.
Additional professional skills are acquired through specialized seminars organized specifically for students of the program.
Required Knowledge for Access Admission to the program is conditional upon possessing the following academic requirements:
1) Bachelor's degree or university diploma obtained after completing a course of study of at least three years in the following degree classes L36 (Political Science and International Relations), L37 (Social Sciences for Cooperation, Development and Peace), L39 (Social Service), L40 (Sociology), or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent;
or:
1) Bachelor's degree or university diploma obtained after completing a course of study of at least three years or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent
2) Possession of at least 36 CFU in at least one of the following fields SPS/04, SPS/07, SECS-P/02, IUS/09, M-STO/04
3) Possession of at least 12 CFU in at least one of the following fields SECS-S/04, SPS/01, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/10, SPS/11, M-DEA/01, M-GGR/02.
These are supplemented by requirements regarding the personal preparation of the student:
1) English language knowledge at least at B2 level (Common European Framework of Reference).
2) Adequate personal preparation, verified through the undergraduate degree grade according to the procedures specified in the program's teaching regulations.
For international students, admission to the program is conditional upon possessing all the above requirements, and additionally:
3) Italian language knowledge at least at B2 level (Common European Framework of Reference).
Students must possess the academic requirements before verifying personal preparation; in particular, no academic debts or additional training obligations are permitted.

Department School of International Studies Entry requirements verification No Course content, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's degree in European and International Studies aims to train professional figures capable of operating in international contexts and understanding, interpreting and managing the economic, legal, political and social transformations of the contemporary world.
The Master's degree aims to train professional figures capable of carrying out economic, legal, political-social analysis and research activities of an institutional and comparative nature, who are able to dialogue with experts from multiple disciplines in a context characterized by regional integration processes and issues related to international security, poverty, economic development, democratization and the protection and promotion of human rights.
To this end, systematic and critically aware learning with an interdisciplinary approach is encouraged. Particular attention is given to the learning of quantitative and qualitative analysis methods for economic and demographic dynamics, the interaction between individuals and collectives, within European and international institutions and governance systems. The activation of specific language courses promotes the development of communication skills for presenting such analysis to specialist interlocutors.
Students are directed to carry out internships and training stages at national and multinational companies, national and international public bodies and administrations, as well as at European Union institutions.
The courses of the Master's degree will be taught in English; however, some courses may exceptionally be taught in other European Union languages. During the study program, Italian language courses will also be offered to enable all students to acquire adequate knowledge.
In particular, the courses offered will focus on themes related to European studies and regional integration, international economic organizations, economic development and international studies, particularly regarding diplomatic relations, international security and the transformation of the international system.
The various courses aim to provide institutional and historical knowledge and the analytical methods necessary for understanding the main aspects of the themes they address.
Required entry knowledge For admission to the Master's degree in European and International Studies, candidates must meet the following requirements:
- Academic requirements:
• Hold a first-level degree (of at least 180 credits) obtained from an Italian university or an equivalent recognized title;
• Demonstrate good command of English at B2 level, verified according to the procedures specified in the study program's didactic regulations and the annual call;
• Demonstrate basic knowledge of a second foreign language.
- Specific preparation requirements:
• Demonstrate good multidisciplinary knowledge in the fields characterizing European and International Studies;
• Demonstrate good analytical skills regarding international issues.
The minimum level of this specific preparation typically corresponds to at least 60 CFU related to courses belonging to at least two of the following disciplinary groups, which include in particular the following scientific-disciplinary sectors:
- Historical and philosophical group: L-OR/10, M-FIL/02, M-FIL/03, M-FIL/06, M-STO/02, M-STO/03, M-STO/04, SECS-P/12, SPS/02, SPS/03, SPS/05, SPS/06, SPS/13, SPS/14;
- Economic group: M-GGR/02, SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/04, SECS-P/05, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/04, SECS-S/05;
- Legal group: IUS/01, IUS/02, IUS/03, IUS/04, IUS/05, IUS/06, IUS/07, IUS/08, IUS/09, IUS/10, IUS/11, IUS/12, IUS/13, IUS/14, IUS/15, IUS/16, IUS/17, IUS/18, IUS/19, IUS/20, IUS/21;
- Political science group: SPS/01, SPS/04;
- Sociological group: M-DEA/01, M-PED/01, M-PSI/05, SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/10, SPS/11, SPS/12;
- Linguistic group: L-LIN/04, L-LIN/07, L-LIN/09, L-LIN/12, L-LIN/14, L-LIN/21, L-OR/12, L-OR/21, L-OR/22.
The possession of these requirements is verified through a curriculum screening and an initial assessment of personal preparation, carried out according to the procedures defined in the study program's didactic regulations and the annual call.

Admission Procedures The MEIS is a Master's program with limited enrollment that requires selection among students meeting minimum requirements. To be admitted to MEIS, students must meet language requirements (English language and second language) and disciplinary requirements (in terms of minimum number of academic credits acquired in disciplines related to international studies). Students must also demonstrate a profile, both personal and academic-professional, aligned with the multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary nature of the Master's program. Details regarding admission requirements and selection criteria are specified in the selection notice, published approximately in November each year for admission to the following academic year.
Students interested in applying for MEIS must submit an online application to participate in the selection process, which takes place during the following periods:
February/March for non-EU candidates;
June/July for EU candidates.

[0521H] QUANTITATIVE AND COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY Master's Degree English
COURSE INFORMATION General information for the current academic year Duration
2 years Structure
2016
Status Open Credits
120 CFU Type Master's degree programs Category Medical, health and biological sciences Regulation Reform 270/04
Master's degree class LM-8 - Master's degree class in Industrial Biotechnology Joint Course No Limited Access (45 Places)
Location Hill Campus - Povo B - via Sommarive, 9 (Sustainable capacity: 45)
Department Department of Cell, Computational and Integrated Biology - CIBIO Prerequisites for admission No Program, textbooks and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The professional figures to be formed will be able to understand the biology of the phenomena considered, the complexity of mathematical and computational models, and the analytical approach for representing physical phenomena. Competencies are acquired in the following disciplinary areas: biotechnology area, computer science area, physical-mathematical area.
The specific objectives of the biotechnology area are: to provide advanced competencies on cellular metabolism and how it can be manipulated through genetic and metabolic engineering approaches applicable to both microbial systems and mammalian cells, to provide competencies for the generation, analysis, representation and interpretation of "-omics" data (essentially genomics and transcriptomics), to provide competencies for the use of complex experimental equipment and related software.
The specific objectives of the computer science area are: to introduce students to computational problem solving, to provide practical foundations of scientific programming, to provide basic knowledge on biological networks and competencies to manipulate them by integrating with data, to provide competencies and knowledge for modeling and simulating the dynamics of biological systems, to provide knowledge on algorithms specific for bioinformatics applications, competencies for the design and implementation of bioinformatics resources, to provide knowledge and competencies on machine learning and practical and theoretical notions on specific data mining applications for biological data.
The specific objectives of the physical-mathematical area are: to introduce fundamental notions of likelihood-based statistical inference, to provide knowledge for the construction and use of statistical models for the analysis of univariate and multivariate data, with particular reference to biomolecular data, and of deterministic or stochastic dynamic models for describing biological and biochemical phenomena, to provide competencies for building computer numerical simulations and recognizing the potential and limitations in model use, to provide competencies on the fundamental equations of quantum mechanics and the main elements of atomic and molecular physics phenomenology, to introduce approximation methods for the theoretical description of many-body systems physics, to acquire competencies for critically evaluating the limitations of molecular models, to provide notions on fundamentals and applications of statistical mechanics of biomolecular systems and numerical techniques for studying their thermodynamic and kinetic properties.
To achieve these specific educational objectives, the training path is structured in three phases:
- in the first semester, students from different three-year degrees (biological sciences, biotechnology, computer science, mathematics, physics, chemistry, etc.) will follow different courses to standardize their background ("bridge courses");
- in the second and third semesters students follow a common block of courses ("core courses") while taking into account each student's background and affinities. Project-based learning is encouraged, with group study activities involving students from different degree programs;
- the fourth semester will be entirely dedicated to the preparation of the thesis, with a rotation system through the research groups of each involved structure. The final part of the path is crucial to verify that students have acquired the ability to actively dialogue and collaborate with people from different disciplines and have acquired the ability to practically work with large volumes of biological data.
Prerequisites for admission Those who hold a first-level degree in the following disciplines and corresponding classes of D.M. 270/04 (with the corresponding classes of the previous D.M. 509/99 in parentheses) may access the Master's Degree in Quantitative and Computational Biology.

-Mathematical Sciences ─ L-35 (32)
Those who hold another foreign degree recognized as suitable according to current regulations may also access, provided they have acquired the basic curricular requirements defined according to the procedures established in the Didactic Regulations of the Master's Degree Course.
Considering that the language of instruction for the Master's Degree in Quantitative and Computational Biology is English, a sufficient level of English proficiency is required for understanding the courses defined in the Didactic Regulations. The Didactic Regulations will also specify the timing and methods for verifying students' personal preparation.

No Course Program, Texts and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path Graduates in Cellular and Molecular Biotechnology are experts with high-level competencies to design and conduct analysis and research activities, technological and experimental research, and research and development in Cellular and Molecular Biotechnology, with particular reference to the biomedical field.
The course aims to prepare graduates with advanced capabilities in developing scientific methodologies, able to coordinate study and research projects at national and international levels, and possessing in-depth specialized knowledge in the fields of biotechnology applied to biomedical interests. In particular, the course deepens the topics of the genetic and molecular bases of diseases and the pathophysiology of the human organism, providing the necessary knowledge to develop diagnostic and prognostic pathways, as well as therapeutic strategies based on the use of biotechnology. These knowledge are integrated with solid bio-physical-technological, statistical and computer training, enabling the Cellular and Molecular Biotechnology graduate to perform, based on genomic data, preclinical experiments on the molecular pathogenesis of human diseases and the definition of new therapeutic approaches.
The training path allows students to acquire:
-in-depth knowledge of the mechanisms of functioning and regulation of eukaryotic cells, under physiological and pathological conditions;
-in-depth knowledge of human pathological processes at molecular, cellular and systemic levels;
-skills in methodologies related to cell culture and genetic engineering techniques for eukaryotic cells;
-in-depth knowledge of physical methods for the structural and functional characterization of biological macromolecules and the cellular processes in which they are involved;
-bioinformatics methodology skills for organizing and accessing databases, with particular reference to genomics, proteomics and metabolomics;
-knowledge and skills in molecular modeling for the design of biomedically relevant molecules;
-knowledge for the industrial design and production of biotechnological products, such as biotherapeutics, diagnostics, vaccines;
-fundamental knowledge related to business economics, organization and management, and management of innovation and biotechnology development projects, including intellectual property aspects.
Additional knowledge is also acquired through the student's autonomous choice of training activities among those suggested by the study course or offered by the University to complete preparation in fields related to Cellular and Molecular Biotechnology.
The training path is completed with a phase of experimental research activity, aimed at preparing the final exam, in specialized academic laboratories, companies, public administration structures and laboratories, as well as other Italian and European universities, within the framework of international agreements.
Entry Requirements Those who hold a degree obtained in class L-2 (Biotechnology) under D.M. 270/04 or in class 1 (Biotechnology) under the previous D.M. 509/99 may access the Master's Degree in Cellular and Molecular Biotechnology. Those who hold a three-year degree or equivalent qualification deemed suitable under current regulations, or other foreign qualifications recognized as suitable, may also access the course, provided they have acquired the basic curricular requirements defined according to the procedures established in the Teaching Regulations of the Master's Degree Course.
Considering that the language of instruction for the Master's Degree in Cellular and Molecular Biotechnology is English, a sufficient level of English proficiency to understand the courses is mandatory, as defined in the Teaching Regulations. The Teaching Regulations of the study course will also define the timing and methods for verifying students' personal preparation.

[0912H] AGRIFOOD INNOVATION MANAGEMENT Master's Degree English
COURSE INFORMATION General information for the current academic year Duration
2 years Order
2020
Status Open Credits
120 CFU Type Master's degree programs Category Agricultural and food sciences Regulation Reform 270/04
Class of degree LM-69 - Class of Master's degrees in Agricultural Sciences and Technologies Joint Course No Limited Access (25 Places)
Location Hill Campus - San Michele a/A - via Edmund Mach, 1
Department Center for Agriculture, Food and Environment-C3A Entry requirements verification No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's Degree in Agrifood Innovation Management is designed to train professional figures (Agrifood innovation managers) capable of introducing innovation elements in companies in the sector and/or initiating business or supply chain initiatives that enhance the typicality and excellence of the territories where they operate, promoting a sustainable and quality agricultural and food production that also includes new market trends (organic, vegan, novel food, etc.). These figures will be able to manage innovation throughout the entire supply chain, from production to processing, including promotion and marketing, but also to read the evolution of food culture and understand the dynamics of agricultural and food markets, considering the evolution of legislation, tastes, and consumer behavior.
The specific educational objectives are aimed at providing professional and scientific skills in the field of innovation management in the agricultural and food sector and in the valorization of products and quality processes, both within companies and in the creation of innovative start-ups, through the consolidation of skills useful for developing self-entrepreneurship. These professional and scientific skills may also be directed towards providing technical support for innovation in public and private research centers.
The specific educational objectives at the end of the study path include the acquisition of:
- a solid foundational cultural preparation in the themes characterizing the agricultural and food system (plant and animal production, management of defense and fertility, agricultural technologies for production and preservation, rural planning, agricultural law and sector community policies);
- a high level of scientific and technological preparation to design and manage innovation throughout the entire supply chain: from agricultural production to preservation and processing of agricultural products and their marketing;
- the ability to design, manage and certify systems and processes of agricultural production and processing, also in relation to technical means, machinery, plants, workplace safety, and environmental impact;
- a high level of preparation in biology and genetics, innovative agricultural practices, and applied physiology to operate on the qualitative and quantitative improvement of agricultural production, its defense, and the safeguarding of natural resources, also in relation to the introduction of invasive alien species of agricultural interest and zoonotic organisms;
- a comprehensive view of rural territory issues, such as landscape valorization, assessment of agricultural impact, development of strategies for rural territory development and planning of activities included therein;
- the ability to consider the current reality as the result of an ongoing evolutionary process; awareness that the sustainability of a productive district lies in finding new and shared solutions to the various problems that arise, the ability to combine tradition, typicality, belonging to a territory with product, process, distribution innovation, and relationships between district subjects;
- knowledge of techniques for controlling various aspects of quality (sensory, nutritional) and food safety, traceability of different agricultural production supply chains, solution of organizational, logistical, and supply problems, and knowledge of legislation related to the agricultural and food sector;
- knowledge of the agricultural and food system and the ability to address issues related to the management of relationships and coordination between the various sectors of the system (primary production, food processing industry, and food distribution), as well as the logic governing the management of key business functions in relation to the specificity of the agricultural and food system;
- knowledge of methods for analyzing consumer behavior and its drivers, the role of commercial distribution, marketing and communication techniques, and socio-cultural aspects of the context in which one operates.
The specific educational objectives also include the acquisition of some transversal skills, obtained mainly through innovative teaching activities (learning by doing, challenge-based learning, role playing, problem solving) in the core and related courses and additional teaching activities: good mastery of the scientific method of investigation, ability to operate with wide autonomy assuming responsibility for evaluating and managing projects or structures, skills in using computer tools and new media for communication, advanced skills in managing businesses, food and non-food supply chains, and agencies of consulting and services connected to them.
At the end of the study path, the Master's graduate will be able to fluently use English, both written and oral, with particular reference to the technical/scientific terminology of the discipline. Where necessary, activities will be provided to adapt the knowledge of Italian for international students, with modalities defined in the study course didactic regulations.
The course is structured with a base of core courses aimed at acquiring skills on innovation in short-cycle species breeding and plant production, on the most advanced agronomic techniques, genetic improvement, and crop protection, on marketing approaches and agricultural and food law aspects, on the design of innovation and automation in agricultural and food production and processing (first year of study), followed by an in-depth study of methods for evaluating the quality of agricultural and food products and consumer preferences and a more specific training program (second year) that includes, thanks to the courses chosen by the student, in-depth studies that may range from aspects related to the sustainable management of territory and resources with attention also to tourism and new consumption trends, to the sustainable production of typical species and crops of the Alpine arc, to the management of invasive alien species and eco-parasitology, and to cultural techniques improving the nutritional and nutraceutical aspects of foods, including novel foods.
The course also includes, in the first and second year, training activities aimed at learning tools, also of an information/statistical nature, and specific approaches for the management and valorization of innovation in the agricultural and food sector (models, processes, projects, strategic innovation management, innovation dynamics, value proposition, communication, intellectual property, business models, and financial plan).
The study course provides for the completion of a research-based thesis to be carried out within the internship, including the preparation of the written work and public discussion.
The internship period will allow the student to learn to know and operate in the business/organization where the experimental work for the thesis will be carried out, stimulating the ability to transfer the acquired knowledge in terms of innovation, as well as communication and autonomous learning.
Entry requirements For entry into the Master's Degree in Agrifood Innovation Management, the possession of curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation as specified below is required.
Curricular requirements:
1) possession of a first-level degree diploma in class L-25 Agricultural and Forest Sciences and Technologies (ex D.M. 270/04 or class 20 ex D.M. 509/99), L-26 Agricultural and Food Sciences (ex D.M. 270/04 or class 20 ex D.M. 509/99), or another foreign degree recognized as suitable;
2) If the first-level degree diploma held is in classes different from those above, it is required to have acquired at least 66 CFU in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors during the previous university career, and in particular:
- a total of at least 18 CFU in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors:
From AGR/01 to AGR/06, AGR/14, AGR/15, from AGR/17 to AGR/20, from VET/01 to VET/04, VET/07, MED/49;
- a total of at least 18 CFU in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors:
AGR/07, AGR/11, AGR/12, AGR/16, MED/07, MED/42, VET/05, VET/06, from BIO/01 to BIO/05, BIO/07, from BIO/09 to BIO/11, BIO/13, BIO/18, BIO/19;
- a total of at least 12 CFU in the scientific-disciplinary sectors:
From MAT/01 to MAT/09, INF/01, ING-INF/05, from FIS/01 to FIS/08, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/02, SECS-S/06;
- a total of at least 6 CFU in the scientific-disciplinary sectors:
From CHIM/01 to CHIM/07, CHIM/10, CHIM/11, AGR/13, BIO/10;
- a total of at least 6 CFU in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors:
From AGR/08 to AGR/10, ICAR/06, ICAR/15, from ING-IND/09 to ING-IND/11, ING-IND/22
- a total of at least 6 CFU in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors:
AGR/01, ICAR/22, ING-IND/35, IUS/03, IUS/04, IUS/13, IUS/14, SECS-P/01, from SECS-P/06 to SECS-P/10, SECS-P/13.

- The modalities for verifying the adequacy of personal preparation, which will take place through an interview or a test in English in the basic and core areas of first-level degrees in class L-25 and L-26, are outlined in the study course didactic regulations.

120 CFU Type Master's degree programs Category Psychology and Neuroscience Regulation Reform 270/04
Class of degree LM-51 - Class of Master's degrees in Psychology Joint Course No Programmed Access (122 Places)
Location Rovereto Campus - Piomarta Palace - Bettini Street, 84
Department Department of Psychology and Cognitive Sciences Entry requirements verification No Program, textbooks and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The graduate who obtains the Master's degree in Psychology will have acquired in-depth knowledge in the field of psychology, based on scientifically valid models, as well as the necessary operational skills for practicing psychological professions. In particular, the aim of the study course is to provide students with advanced theoretical knowledge and methodological skills in psychological disciplines necessary for application in various professional contexts of psychology. The training path is based on a solid preparation in different disciplinary fields ranging from clinical psychology to neuropsychology, to social and organizational psychology, with particular attention to the neurobiological bases of psychological phenomena, methodological and research aspects, and psychological and psychosocial intervention aspects.
The student will consolidate specialized knowledge on cognitive, affective and social processes, their biological bases and development, as well as operational skills in the study of the most advanced methods of these functions and the main techniques of rehabilitation and training. The student will also acquire advanced methodological skills in diagnostic contexts aimed at promoting understanding of different intervention models.
The educational objectives of the study course are achieved through the articulation of the teaching offer into training paths that share some formative activities in the disciplinary fields characteristic of Psychology but differentiate during the biennium, allowing in-depth study of specific themes. This will enable the student to deepen specific areas, such as Neurosciences, which focuses on mental mechanisms and the neurobiological bases of cognitive and affective functions, their disorders and rehabilitation; Clinical Psychology, focused on themes related to the main explanatory models of distress and psychological disorders throughout the life cycle, as well as their treatment, from a multi-approach perspective integrated with cognitive neuroscience; Human Resources and Organizational Psychology, which allows acquisition of the knowledge and skills necessary to work in complex organizational contexts and effectively manage human resources present therein. The training paths will be detailed in the Study Course Teaching Regulations.
The student will be involved in frontal and seminar teaching activities, with ample space dedicated to participatory teaching activities, which offers the most appropriate context for personal discussions and reflections on study topics and for acquiring professional tools and working methods. Training is also directed towards acquiring advanced knowledge of the English language, including the specialized vocabulary used in psychology, necessary for continuous updating of professional skills. Students are also offered the possibility to attend training activities abroad within the Erasmus program and numerous collaborations with foreign universities.
Pursuant to Articles 1 and 3 of Law No. 163 of November 8, 2021, the final exam for the Master's degree in Psychology - class LM-51 enables the practice of the profession of psychologist. For this purpose, the final exam includes the performance of a practical assessment (PPV) of the professional skills acquired through the internship within the study courses, aimed at verifying the technical preparation level of the candidate for professional qualification, which precedes the defense of the thesis. To pass the PPV, the student must obtain a suitability assessment, after which they proceed to the thesis defense. Students who obtain a suitability assessment for the Practical-Valuation Internship (TPV) within the study courses are admitted to the final exam. Within the professional training activities, 20 university credits (CFU) are acquired through the performance of a TPV within the study courses. The TPV consists of supervised, contextualized practical activities involving direct observation and execution of activities aimed at situated learning and the development of fundamental procedural and relational skills for professional practice. These skills refer to typical and reserved acts characteristic of the psychologist profession, also as per Article 1 of Law February 18, 1989, No. 56, and include the use of knowledge and intervention tools for prevention, diagnosis, rehabilitation and training activities, support in psychological contexts for individuals, groups, social organizations and communities, as well as experimentation, research and teaching activities. The TPV is passed by obtaining a final suitability assessment. For the acquisition of the 30 CFU of TPV, part of the professional training activities, corresponding to 10 CFU, is carried out according to the modalities provided by the Interministerial Decree No. 654 of July 5, 2022, and subsequent amendments.
Entry requirements Those who possess the following curricular requirements may be admitted to the study course:
- a three-year university degree or equivalent diploma, or another foreign degree recognized as suitable;
- psychological knowledge certified by the possession of at least 88 CFU distributed across multiple psychological disciplines (M-PSI/01, M-PSI/02, M-PSI/03, M-PSI/04, M-PSI/05, M-PSI/06, M-PSI/07, M-PSI/08) as specified in the Study Course Teaching Regulations;
- CFU for the Practical-Valuation Internship as provided by Interministerial Decree No. 654/2022 and subsequent amendments. In case of total or partial non-recognition of the CFU referred to in paragraph 6, the three-year graduates acquire the missing TPV CFU in addition to the 120 CFU of the Master's degree.
Additional personal preparation requirements apply:
- English language knowledge at least at B1 level (Common European Framework);
- Adequate personal preparation, verified through a test with questions related to different areas of psychology, according to the modalities specified in the Study Course Teaching Regulations.
The preparation for the test and the evaluation of results will be monitored by a dedicated committee, according to the modalities specified in the Study Course Teaching Regulations.
Students must possess the curricular requirements before the verification of personal preparation; in particular, no academic debts or additional training obligations are permitted.

Master's degree class LM-55 - Class of Master's degrees in Cognitive Sciences Interuniversity course No Limited access (30 places)
Location Rovereto Campus - Palazzo Piomarta - corso Bettini, 84
Department Department of Engineering and Information Science Department of Psychology and Cognitive Sciences (Main)
Access requirements verification No Program, textbooks and objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path The Master's in Human-Computer Interaction aims to prepare qualified graduates with strong multidisciplinary competence. In particular, the interdepartmental nature of the course allows to provide (a) an integrated curriculum that will enable students to pursue their research interests in an interdisciplinary and structured research environment (b) research skills and potential in areas not covered by a single department (c) specialized skills not covered by traditional teaching programs.
Specific educational objectives of the Course:
- Familiarity with simulation, observational and experimental methodologies used in the study of the mind-brain system and human-machine interfaces and between humans and other complex systems;
- Ability to design models and interventions for the reorganization of interfaces between humans and complex systems;
- Acquisition of theoretical and operational knowledge on communication and decision processes;
- In-depth knowledge of methodologies for collecting and analyzing both quantitative and qualitative data;
- Ability to analyze decision-making processes at individual and collective levels, in organizational, economic and social contexts;
- Ability to conduct basic and applied research activities independently.
With these objectives, the Master's in Human-Computer Interaction is structured into three strongly interconnected learning areas:
- Socio-cognitive area, with themes of mind-brain interaction and cognitive constraints, enabling and rehabilitative technologies, social interaction, inclusive design;
- Computer science area, with themes of user-centered design, participatory design, human-computer interaction, prototyping of interactive systems, affective computing, e-learning;
- Methodological area, with themes of quantitative and qualitative research methodology, visual design, ethics and epistemology of design.
The internship can be carried out in one of the University's laboratories with an academic supervisor, or at companies, with an academic supervisor and a company supervisor.
The thesis has a dual purpose: assessment of acquired skills and theoretical-conceptual deepening of topics related to cognitive aspects of interaction design, typically accompanied by an empirical component.
Required knowledge for access Admission to the Master's degree is conditional on verification of the following requirements, which must be met for enrollment:
a) academic requirements:
- Hold a first-level degree, obtained at Italian universities or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent;
- Possess certified English language proficiency;
b) specific preparation requirements:
- Demonstrate good analytical ability regarding cognitive sciences and information sciences topics,
- Demonstrate good ability to address methodological problems,
- Demonstrate good ability to read research data in the field of technologies.
Academic and disciplinary knowledge typically corresponds to at least 50 CFU related to courses belonging to the core and characterizing disciplines of classes L-20, L-24, L-31 (ex DM 270/04) or classes 14, 34, 26 (ex DM 509/99).
Assessment of personal preparation is conducted according to the criteria and methods defined in the course's didactic regulations.

Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path The Master's Degree in Cognitive Science aims to acquire advanced theoretical and methodological knowledge in the field of cognitive sciences through an interdisciplinary approach to the study of the mind-brain system and human-machine interaction. The adopted perspective is interdisciplinary, integrating biological, technological and cognitive approaches, with the aim of enabling a better understanding of human behavior, focusing teaching and other training activities mainly on cognitive neuropsychology and the ergonomic aspects of human-machine interaction.
The training path is characterized by internship experiences and significant research moments in highly qualified laboratories in the fields of brain-imaging (fMRI, EEG, TMS, etc.) and multimodal interaction (cognitive interfaces, multimedia, etc.), also to operationalize the acquired skills, and internships are planned at external structures. Students are also offered the possibility to attend courses abroad within international exchange programs and the numerous collaborations with foreign universities. The study course aims to attract students from other countries and prepare Italian students for international comparison. Therefore, the study course will be entirely in English and will feature a significant presence of teachers from foreign institutions affiliated with the Faculty.
The evaluation of acquired skills will consider both theoretical knowledge and operational abilities acquired by students, also within integrated courses across multiple disciplines.
Required knowledge for access Admission to the Master's Degree in Cognitive Science is subject to verification of the following requirements:
- Curricular requirements:
  • Hold a first-level degree, obtained at Italian universities or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent,
  • Possess certified English language proficiency and computer skills, the level of which will be defined in the course's didactic regulations;
- Specific preparation requirements:
  • Demonstrate good analytical ability regarding cognitive science topics,
  • Demonstrate good ability in addressing methodological-quantitative problems,
  • Demonstrate good ability in reading research data in the fields of mind-brain and technology.
These knowledge typically correspond to at least 50 CFU related to courses belonging to the five disciplinary areas characterizing cognitive sciences. The possession of these requirements is verified through curriculum screening and evaluation of the student's personal preparation, according to the procedures defined in the course's didactic regulations.

Master's Degree Class LM-40 - Class of Master's Degrees in Mathematics Joint Course No Open Access Location Hill Campus - Povo A - via Sommarive, 14 (Sustainable energy use: 47)
Department Department of Mathematics Entry Requirements Verification No Course Program, Texts and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Course aims to train graduates with solid knowledge of various areas of mathematics (algebra, analysis, geometry, probability, numerical analysis, mathematical physics), and more in-depth knowledge in at least one specific area. This knowledge is typically accompanied by practical familiarity with at least one other discipline.
Such knowledge, in addition to being based on solid theoretical foundations, includes the ability to
- solve non-routine mathematical problems, independently drawing on one's cultural background to select the most appropriate tools;
- conduct complex bibliographic research to identify useful tools in recent literature for solving given problems;
- effectively present mathematical topics, also in English, adapting the exposition to different audiences, including non-specialized ones.
Through the thesis, the student is ultimately guided to move autonomously and creatively in a specific field.
The entire Master's Degree course is taught in English.
The Didactic Regulations of the Master's Degree Course provide for targeted pathways aimed at a broad mathematical cultural training and pathways intended to enable the Master's graduate to understand the language, methods, and issues characteristic of a non-mathematical discipline, together with its relationship to mathematics itself. With this training, the Master's graduate will be able to more effectively work in multidisciplinary teams, making a significant contribution to modeling and solving complex problems.
Entry Requirements For admission to the Master's Degree in Mathematics, a Bachelor's degree or university diploma of at least three years duration, or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent, and specific curricular requirements specified in the Didactic Regulations of the Master's Degree Course are required.
The student's personal preparation will also be verified, using the methods detailed in the Didactic Regulations of the Master's Degree Course.
Considering the specificities of the initial preparation, according to the procedures outlined in the Didactic Regulations of the Master's Degree Course, admission may be conditional on the student selecting a study plan, agreed with the Course Council, which must still comply with the Didactic Framework.
This option is particularly aimed at enabling and regulating admission to the Master's Degree Course for Bachelor's graduates (three-year) in other disciplines who wish to follow an interdisciplinary path between that discipline and Mathematics, and who have obtained a certain number of Mathematics credits in their previous career. Typically, these students will be required to dedicate a substantial number of credits to Mathematics, while remaining free to choose other credits as per the student's discretion.
An English language level of B1 or higher will be required.

Degree Class LM-17 - Master's degree class in Physics Interdepartmental Course No Open Access Location Hill Campus - Povo A - via Sommarive, 14 (Sustainable use: 45)
Department Department of Physics Prerequisites for admission No Program, textbooks and objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path
1. The Master's graduate in Physics:
a) possesses a solid cultural preparation in various fields of modern physics and its theoretical, experimental and applied aspects, as well as a solid mastery of the scientific method of investigation;
b) possesses in-depth and flexible training, attentive to the most recent developments in scientific research and technology;
c) has an in-depth knowledge of measurement instruments and data analysis techniques, as well as mathematical and computer tools for support;
d) is able to operate with wide autonomy, also assuming responsibility for projects and structures, in the field of scientific and technological research and innovation;
e) is able to use the specific knowledge acquired, either for the use and design of sophisticated measurement instruments or for modeling complex systems in various scientific fields and also in areas outside the scientific field;
f) is able to use English fluently in written and oral form, referring also to disciplinary and technical lexicons.
2. The Master's degree course in Physics is delivered entirely in English. Only one training path is offered, consisting of two common and mandatory courses, supplemented by characterizing training activities chosen by the student from a list of activities offered in the fields of nuclear and subnuclear physics and condensed matter physics, and related and free-choice activities.
The common and mandatory courses aim to acquire advanced knowledge of quantum mechanics, with particular reference to its theoretical aspects, and to acquire experimental physics skills dedicated to the operational knowledge of the most recent and sophisticated measurement and data analysis methods.
The characterizing activities aim to acquire in-depth knowledge in the field of theoretical, computational and experimental physics in relation to the most recent developments in theoretical physics, the foundations of physics, nuclear and subnuclear physics, the structure of matter, experimental physics and its applications.
The study path is structured into different orientations that reflect the research activities within the Department of Physics, with particular reference to the fields of fundamental interactions physics, gravitation, nuclear physics, condensed matter physics, atomic and molecular physics, structure and dynamics of complex systems, quantum sciences and technologies, nanosciences, physics applied to materials for energy and environment, biophysics and medical physics. These orientations, communicated to students in the form of suggested study plans, require the acquisition of specific knowledge through the selection of recommended characterizing and related activities by the research groups present in the Department, also in relation to possible thesis topics offered.
The study path may include external activities such as study stays at other Italian and foreign universities, also within international agreements.
Prerequisites for admission
1. To be admitted to the Master's degree course in Physics, the following are required:
a) academic requirements:
I. Three-year university degree or diploma, or other foreign degree recognized as suitable;
II. a total of 84 CFU in SSD MAT/* and FIS/*, including at least 24 CFU in SSD MAT/* and at least 54 CFU in SSD FIS/*;
b) adequate personal preparation, including knowledge of English at least at B2 level of the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR).
2. The adequacy of personal preparation will be verified by a dedicated committee, following the procedures defined in the course's didactic regulations. Only candidates meeting the academic requirements may undergo verification of personal preparation.

[0341H] ENVIRONMENTAL METEOROLOGY Master's Degree InteruniversityDouble Degree English
COURSE INFORMATION General information for the current academic year Duration
2 years Organization
2018
Status Open Credits
120 CFU Type Master's degree programs Category Mathematics and Physics Regulation Reform 270/04
Degree class LM-75 - Master's degree class in Environmental and Territorial Sciences and Technologies Joint Degree Partner Universities Leopold Franzens University, Innsbruck Limited Access (30 Places)
Location Hill Campus - Mesiano - Via Mesiano, 77 (Sustainable capacity: 30)
Department Center for Agriculture, Food and Environment-C3A Department of Physics Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering (Main)
Access Requirements No prior knowledge assessment Program, textbooks and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The training path provides preparation for two professional profiles respectively as "meteorologist" and "environmental meteorologist", whose competencies and functions are better specified in the following section "Career opportunities and professional prospects for graduates".
Graduates of the Master's program in Environmental Meteorology must:
- be able to analyze, monitor, and manage complex environmental realities, with particular reference to the atmospheric environmental matrix and its interactions with other environmental matrices, also in relation to long-term climate effects;
- have a solid cultural preparation in basic disciplines (particularly mathematics, physics, and chemistry) as well as in systemic disciplines focused on the environment, with particular reference to meteorology and climatology, and a good mastery of the scientific method;
- have the ability to identify, evaluate, and manage interactions between components of environmental systems and between different factors determining environmental processes and problems, with particular regard to processes involving the atmosphere;
- know and be able to develop methods and techniques for territorial investigation and data analysis, and simulation methods using numerical models (meteorological, hydrological, pollutant transport) that also allow integration of processes at different scales;
- know and be able to apply technical regulations and guidelines provided by authorities and technical bodies for the correct installation, regular maintenance, and conscious and appropriate use of instrumentation for observing physical variables related to the atmosphere;
- be able to synthesize observations from various monitoring instruments and results from numerical meteorological models to produce short and medium-term meteorological forecasts;
- know the methodologies and use technologies for prevention and management of atmospheric pollution, as well as for protection of people and the environment;
- have competencies for the assessment of resources (environmental, energy, etc.) and environmental impacts;
- possess good written and oral mastery of the English language.
To achieve these goals, the curriculum:
- includes training activities, lectures, laboratory exercises, and field activities, aimed at acquiring experimental methods, technology use, data collection and processing, as well as simulation and forecasting of environmental atmospheric processes using numerical models;
- may include, in relation to specific objectives, external activities such as training internships at companies, public administration bodies (particularly environmental protection agencies and meteorological services), and laboratories, as well as study stays at other universities, research institutions, meteorological services, environmental agencies, or international organizations (WMO, IPCC, EEA, EPA, etc.), in Italy and abroad, also within international agreements;
- requires the completion of a final exam consisting of original scientific and technological research with the production of a thesis.
The study path provides that the first year lectures are given in Trento. In the first semester, the foundations of atmospheric structure and processes governing its interactions with other environmental systems, as well as measurement methods for main quantities, will be covered. In the second semester, applications to the hydrological cycle, atmospheric pollutant transport, interactions with the biosphere, and simulation methods using numerical models will be introduced.
The second year, first semester lectures will be given in Innsbruck, focusing on radiation-atmosphere interactions and biogeochemical cycles relevant to Earth's climate, as well as dynamic meteorology.
The second semester of the second year will be mainly dedicated to activities related to the preparation of the Master's thesis, to be carried out at the candidate's chosen location, in agreement with the supervisor.
Required Knowledge for Access Admission to the Master's program in Environmental Meteorology is conditional on possessing the following curricular and personal preparation requirements:
1) a university degree or diploma obtained after a study program of at least three years, or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent;
2) possession of:
-at least 24 CFU in the fields from MAT/01 to MAT/09;
-at least 24 CFU in the fields from FIS/01 to FIS/08, GEO/10, GEO/11, GEO/12, ICAR/01, ICAR/02, ING-IND/06, ING-IND/10, ING-IND/11, ING-IND/12 and ING-INF/02;
-at least 6 CFU in the fields CHIM/01, CHIM/02, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, CHIM/07, CHIM/12.
The curricular requirements specified in points 1) and 2) must be held by students before the personal preparation assessment.
3) English language knowledge at least at B2 level (Common European Framework of Reference).
4) The adequacy of personal preparation will be verified through methods specified in the study program's didactic regulations. As master's degree admission with academic debts is not permitted, curricular and personal preparation requirements must be met before enrolling in the study program.

Admission Procedures Access to the Master's Degree program in Environmental Meteorology is subject to the possession of the following academic and personal qualifications:
a. a university degree or diploma obtained upon completion of a study program of at least three years, or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent;
b. possession of:
i. at least 24 CFU in the fields from MAT/01 to MAT/09;
ii. at least 24 CFU in the fields from FIS/01 to FIS/08, GEO/10, GEO/11, GEO/12, ICAR/01, ICAR/02, ING-IND/06, ING-IND/10, ING-IND/11, ING-IND/12, and ING-INF/02;
iii. at least 6 CFU in the fields CHIM/01, CHIM/02, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, CHIM/07, CHIM/12.
c. proof of English language proficiency at least at B2 level of the Common European Framework of Reference.

The academic requirements specified in points a) and b) must be held by the candidates before the verification of personal preparation.

For holders of a degree from a previous academic system prior to the introduction of CFUs or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent, the verification of academic requirements is conducted by the examining committee designated by the Joint Board of Lectures, taking into account appropriate equivalences between the content of courses taken and those corresponding to the disciplinary fields mentioned above.

The adequacy of personal preparation is also verified by the examining committee through an individual interview with candidates as specified in the selection notices for admission to the study program. In particular, the committee will assess the actual mastery of the basic disciplines of mathematics, physics, and chemistry, as well as any additional competencies already acquired in the more specific areas of the Study Program (e.g., environmental sciences, meteorology, applied physics, hydrology, oceanography).

Access to the Master's Degree program with academic deficiencies is not permitted; the academic and personal preparation requirements must be met before enrollment in the study program.

Each year, a call for admission to the following academic year is published in November. The call provides for two evaluation rounds. In the first round, candidates who submitted their application by the first deadline (end of February) are evaluated; in the second round, those who submitted by the subsequent deadline (end of June).

The first round is the only one admitting candidates who are not EU citizens or who are not already regularly residing in an EU country. This is because subsequent procedures for obtaining an entry visa require several months and would not be compatible with the timing of the second round.

The judging committee is appointed by the JBL and includes both professors from the University of Innsbruck and professors from the University of Trento. Admission applications are first evaluated based on qualifications. After the evaluation of qualifications, candidates admitted to interviews are individually heard to assess their preparation and suitability to successfully complete the Study Program.

[0344H] MECHATRONICS ENGINEERING Master's Degree English
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration
2 years Order
2021
Status Open Credits
120 ECTS credits Type Master's degree programs Category Engineering, computer science and technologies Regulation Reform 270/04
Master's Degree Class LM-33 - Class of Master's degrees in Mechanical Engineering Interdepartmental Course No Open Access Location Hill Campus - Povo B - via Sommarive, 9 (Sustainable use: 35)
Department Department of Industrial Engineering Verification of required knowledge for admission No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path The general educational objective of the study program is to promote an innovation culture in all aspects of the professional activity of the mechatronic engineer. The objectives of class LM33 serve as high-level references that, within this study program, are instrumental in providing the ability to innovate in the ideation, planning, design and management of systems, processes and services. Basic sciences are primarily interpreted as disciplines aimed at describing the functional aspects of the mechatronic system, understood as a set of subsystems interacting at multiple levels (mechanical, electronic, computer) and increasingly integrating cognitive and connectivity capabilities. The training focuses on developing transversal skills that allow students to organize necessary connections between disciplines, understanding the experimental purpose (through physical laboratories and/or simulations) of the learning process.
The organization of the training path is based on a first year aimed at providing students with the fundamental theoretical tools of numerical analysis and mechatronics (mechanics, automation, signals and measurements), consolidating the ability to understand, formalize, model, simulate and control an intelligent mechanical system. The second year completes the training by focusing on specific deepening in advanced mechanics, dynamics, distributed systems, robotics, innovative control applications and intelligent transport systems, organized according to the study program curricula.
From the general objective derive the educational objectives of the different curricula of the study program, which are aimed at equipping students with tools and methods to successfully carry out the profession of the modern mechatronic engineer. The curricula focus on application contexts in different fields, considered strategic and consistent with the identity of the training project. Among these declinations of the training project, the innovative mechanics (and the related design, verification and control tools), robotics (from enabling technologies to industrial applications and innovative developments), intelligent vehicles (from autonomous driving to advanced transport systems), and autonomous systems (integrated with aspects of entrepreneurial innovation) are highlighted.
The professional profiles of the study program refine the general profile of the systems engineer in the specificity of the modern mechatronic field. The latest developments in advanced industrial reality, identified in the trends of Industry 4.0, increasingly require professional profiles capable of integrating skills from traditionally different fields. The reference profiles draw inspiration from fundamental interdisciplinary figures to successfully carry out numerous professional activities both in manufacturing or service companies, public administrations and research institutions, as well as in free profession or entrepreneurial contexts. The figure of the mechatronic engineer, which forms the basis of the study program design, was created with the idea of integrating disciplines related to mechanics and electronics-automation, elevating the study perspective to the entire system rather than its components. The general educational objective of the study program remains to promote an innovation culture in all aspects of professional activity.
Master's graduates in Mechatronics Engineering have mastery of the main reference methods for the design, development, production and management of modern Cyber Physical Systems and know how to apply them appropriately, addressing their inherent interdisciplinarity, using suitable theoretical tools and applied skills. They know how to apply these methods to various functional subsystems, defining interfaces and maintaining an overall vision, appropriately described by engineering requirements. They know how to use modern methods for updating knowledge and understand their impact on existing technologies, in addition to having innovative tools to increase competitiveness. They know how to convert technological and scientific development trends into innovation projects and/or the conception of new products and processes. They have the necessary skills to apply Artificial Intelligence technologies to modern mechatronic products, with particular attention to intelligent vehicles.
Required knowledge for admission The curricular requirements and the suitability of personal preparation for admission to the Master's Degree course, in accordance with Article 6, paragraph 2, of Ministerial Decree 270/2004, are established based on the following curricular and preparation criteria.
Curricular requirements
• Admission is open to graduates in class L-9 (ex DM 270/2004) who have acquired:
- At least 18 ECTS credits in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD): ING-IND/12, ING-IND/13, ING-IND/14, ING-INF/01, ING-INF/04, MAT/07.
• Admission is open to graduates in other classes who have acquired:
- At least 24 ECTS credits in SSD: MAT/02, MAT/03, MAT/05, MAT/06, MAT/07, MAT/08, SECS-S/06;
- At least 15 ECTS credits in SSD: FIS/01, FIS/02, FIS/03, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, CHIM/07;
- At least 18 ECTS credits in SSD: ING-IND/12, ING-IND/13, ING-IND/14, ING-INF/01, ING-INF/04, ING-INF/07.
• For holders of other foreign degrees recognized as suitable, the verification of curricular requirements is carried out by a committee appointed by the Department Council, considering appropriate equivalences between the contents of exams taken in the previous study path and those corresponding to the above-mentioned fields and disciplinary sectors.
Suitability of personal preparation The suitability of personal preparation must be verified. Only candidates meeting the curricular requirements have access to this verification.
The methods for verifying personal preparation are defined in the course didactic regulations.
For admission to the Master's degree course, students must also demonstrate knowledge of English at least at level B2 (CEFR).

Admission Procedures The Master's Degree in Mechatronics Engineering does not have a quota system.
To enroll in the Master's Degree in Mechatronics Engineering, a degree or other foreign qualification recognized as equivalent is required.
Access to the program is also subject to meeting curricular requirements and verification of adequate personal preparation as specified below. Regarding curricular requirements, see the previous Table A3.a.
Personal preparation for access to the Master's Degree in Mechatronics Engineering is considered adequate for graduates who meet the curricular requirements and have achieved an average grade, weighted by corresponding credits, of at least 23/30 in examinations taken for the degree (excluding the final exam). In the calculation of the average, a grade of thirty with honors is considered equivalent to 31/30.
To access the Master's Degree program, students must also possess proven knowledge of English at least at level B2 (CEFR). Students who have not acquired this knowledge in their previous studies must provide an official certification of equivalent or higher level issued by an official body or by the University of Trento Language Center (CLA). The list of accepted certificates is available on the CLA website (www.unitn.it/cla).
No interviews to verify basic preparation are required, but the documents attesting to the curriculum, average grade, and English knowledge provided at the time of application via the online procedure (active from early June to late November) are binding.
For students from non-EU countries, a selection based on qualifications and possible interview is provided. For the academic year 2022/2023, 25 places were reserved for the Master's Degree in Mechatronics Engineering, including non-EU students selected under the EIT Digital double degree program.
