Degree class LM-53. - Materials engineering Interdepartmental course No Open access Location Hill Campus - Povo B - via Sommarive, 9 (Sustainable use: 35)
Department Department of Industrial Engineering Entry requirements verification No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path The general educational objective of the study course is to train Master's graduates with solid cultural foundations in engineering and qualifying knowledge regarding production processes, properties, development and applications of materials, ideation, design and development of innovative products, management of the product life cycle in line with the current evolution of modern manufacturing industry, where the systemic approach prevails, necessary for applying sustainability criteria and implementing the principles of the circular economy.
The training path aims to achieve the following specific objectives:
- Provide in-depth knowledge of materials science and engineering;
- Enable mastery of the main reference methods for the design, development, production, transformation, characterization, quality control and management of traditional and innovative materials for specific applications in the manufacturing industry;
- Provide a strong innovation culture and sensitivity to design, develop and manage products and their production processes with attention to the entire life cycle;
- Provide skills for leading and coordinating innovation and development projects of materials and industrial products, with a systemic vision and particular attention to the application of emerging technologies;
- Develop the ability to use modern methods for updating knowledge, innovative tools to enhance competitiveness and understand their impact on existing technologies;
- Develop the ability to convert development and technological/scientific trends into innovation projects and/or the conception of new products and processes for modern industry, particularly in the manufacturing sector;
- Provide the skills to intervene with a strong innovative vision in fundamental areas of modern industry, such as energy, biomedical technologies, production processes and eco-sustainable materials;
- Develop the ability to harmonize acquired technical-specialist skills with transversal, non-disciplinary skills (such as working in teams, creative thinking, communicating with specific professional figures, expressing and drafting technical reports in English) and digital skills (such as using modeling and design software, conducting online data/information research);
- Develop the skills and knowledge to organize necessary connections between disciplines, understanding the technical and experimental purposes of the learning process through practical laboratory, design and simulation activities.
The achievement of the educational objectives set by the study course occurs through a training path where in the first common year, within mandatory characteristic training activities, fundamental theoretical-applicative tools regarding condensed matter chemistry and physics, thermodynamics, structure and properties of different material classes, their production processes are provided, consolidating the ability to understand their operation, design their application, evaluate their degradation in service, and plan their restoration.
The second year provides specific training activities related to advanced materials, modern production technologies, product design and development methods, strategies for managing materials throughout the entire life cycle, with particular attention to sustainability and recycling. In particular, the courses offered in both characteristic and related disciplines allow consolidating the basic competencies of materials engineers on different material classes, their manufacturing processes, advanced and "smart" properties and applications, and enable acquiring interdisciplinary competencies that contribute to consolidating technical preparation and increasing the ability of graduates to interact within different company functions throughout the product design and development phase, as well as in managing its life cycle and defining enabling technologies for production systems.
At the second year, students are also offered the possibility to choose between differentiated in-depth curricula that, integrating innovation and entrepreneurial aspects, focus on application contexts of different areas, considered strategic and fully consistent with the overall educational project of the study course. In particular, examples include in-depth studies on manufacturing processes and product development, sustainable use of energy, materials and technologies for biomedical and functional applications, and sustainable materials.
Entry requirements The curricular requirements and the suitability of personal preparation for entry into the Master's Degree course, in accordance with Article 6, paragraph 2, of Ministerial Decree 270/2004, are established based on the following curricular criteria and personal preparation.
Curricular requirements For entry into the Master's Degree in Materials Engineering, possession of a degree or other foreign degree recognized as suitable is required.
Eligible candidates are those who have acquired:
- At least 24 CFU in SSD: MAT/02, MAT/03, MAT/05, MAT/06, MAT/07, MAT/08, ING-INF/05;
- At least 18 CFU in SSD: FIS/01, FIS/03, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, CHIM/07;
- At least 45 CFU in SSD: ING-IND/03, ING-IND/04, ING-IND/05, ING-IND/06, ING-IND/07, ING-IND/08, ING-IND/09, ING-IND/11, ING-IND/12, ING-IND/13, ING-IND/14, ING-IND/15, ING-IND/16, ING-IND/17, ING-IND/19, ING-IND/21, ING-IND/22, ING-IND/23, ING-IND/24, ING-IND/25, ING-IND/26, ING-IND/27, ING-IND/31, ING-IND/32, ING-IND/34, ING-IND/35, ICAR/01, ICAR/08, of which at least 12 CFU in the characteristic SSD subgroup of materials engineering: ING-IND/16, ING-IND/21, ING-IND/22, ING-IND/23, ING-IND/24, ING-IND/27 and ICAR/08.
For holders of other foreign degrees recognized as suitable, curricular requirements verification is carried out by a committee appointed by the Department Council, considering appropriate equivalences between the contents of exams taken in previous university study paths and those corresponding to the above-mentioned fields and disciplinary sectors.
Suitability of personal preparation The suitability of personal preparation must be verified. Only candidates meeting the curricular requirements may access this verification.
The methods for verifying personal preparation are defined in the course didactic regulations.
For admission to the Master's degree, students must also demonstrate knowledge of English at least at B2 level (CEFR).
For non-native Italian speakers, the knowledge of the Italian language will be verified. The verification methods will be defined in the didactic regulations of the course, which will also indicate - in cases of negative verification result - the training activities to be included in the study plan for acquiring the required Italian language knowledge for graduates.

Degree Class LM-31 - Class of Master's Degrees in Management Engineering Interuniversity Course No Open Access Location Hill Campus - Povo B - via Sommarive, 9
Department Department of Industrial Engineering Entry Requirements Verification No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the educational path The educational path aims to respond to the strong demand for skills expressed by the labor market, particularly in the industrial sector, where engineers are increasingly called to:
- manage complex systems with an holistic vision, ensuring attention to the various factors contributing to overall performance in the industrial context;
- design, manage and optimize industrial processes, both productive and logistic, as well as organizational;
- manage technological and organizational innovation by adopting multi- and interdisciplinary approaches;
- promote the development of new production and economic paradigms derived from the cognitive and connectivity potential offered by recent developments in digital technologies, while managing the profound changes in roles and operational contexts that arise;
- complement technical knowledge and skills with economic and organizational knowledge and capabilities.
To this end, the Master's Degree in Management and Industrial Systems Engineering provides a very solid, yet balanced, competence in both technical disciplines and disciplines related to the management of systemic complexity in modern industry, considering also economic-organizational aspects and challenges arising from environmental sustainability of industrial development. In particular, the study program provides Master's graduates with intellectual tools to:
- apply tools and methodologies for the design and management of complex systems;
- apply modern quantitative techniques to support decision-making;
- manage the main digital technologies underlying the new industrial revolution;
- apply methodologies for promoting and managing innovation;
- evaluate the environmental sustainability of industrial products and processes, focusing on an holistic and integrated view of problems rather than specific aspects or technologies.
The educational content will be aligned with recent technological and organizational developments revolutionizing the industrial world, from product personalization to environmental sustainability of processes, from digitalization of industrial plants to quality and safety of production systems.
Students will also have the opportunity to complete their training through training internships and/or placements at companies, professional offices, and other public and private entities.
On this consolidated foundation, based on a solid education in the disciplines characteristic of management engineering and industrial systems, differentiated educational paths are also defined to allow students to integrate their training in thematic areas characteristic of either industrial engineering or information engineering, always respecting the constraints imposed by the academic framework.
At the end of the educational path, the Master's graduate will have solid knowledge regarding methodologies for the design and management of industrial plants, logistic systems, and production processes, together with managerial skills necessary for the organization and development of various business functions, such as research and development, and marketing. Transversally to these competencies, Master's graduates will have acquired relevant knowledge in the field of managing innovation projects, quality and safety of industrial systems, enabling digital technologies for production systems, with particular emphasis on automation and control of industrial processes.
Master's graduates will be able to appropriately, interdisciplinary, and innovatively apply these competencies, always considering the high degree of dynamism that characterizes modern industrial systems. Master's graduates will be able to effectively interpret rapid organizational changes and the constant technological evolution typical of the current industrial development period. Master's graduates will have solid engineering and technological skills that will allow them to fully understand ongoing changes and guide them towards configurations of greater benefit for the system in which they will operate. In particular, Master's graduates will have the opportunity to develop knowledge in various areas relevant to modern industrial systems, such as the economic, environmental, and social sustainability of production processes, digitalization of processing and logistic systems, modeling and optimization of business and industrial processes, as well as management of complex and interdisciplinary projects, organizing their multifunctional teams.
Master's graduates will have acquired specific, in-depth knowledge in various disciplines of mechanical industrial plants, economic-management engineering, technologies and processing systems, industrial automation, and some related disciplines that will consolidate their technical preparation and enhance their ability to interact with different business functions throughout the entire product design and development phase, in managing its lifecycle, in selecting materials and related production and transformation technologies, in defining optimization strategies, and in selecting enabling digital technologies for production systems.
In particular, the training will include in-depth study of product and production system design methods, logistic systems, storage and warehousing, organizational strategies, methodologies for personalized production, process control, and intelligent product manufacturing, as well as modeling of complex systems and analysis of dynamic networks.
The educational framework is completed by the possibility offered to students to choose between differentiated educational paths, allowing them to complete their preparation by deepening studies on themes related to management engineering, with emphasis on thematic areas characteristic of industrial engineering and information engineering, respectively.
The educational program concludes with a final examination requiring the preparation of an original thesis.
The educational activities may include laboratory experiences within specific courses, group work, seminars, and company internships.
Entry Requirements for Access The curricular requirements and the adequacy of personal preparation for access to the Master's Degree, in accordance with Article 6, paragraph 2, of Ministerial Decree 270/2004, are established based on the following curricular and preparation criteria.
Curricular Requirements
• Access to the course is open to graduates in class L-9 (former DM 270/2004) who have acquired:
- at least 12 CFU in the disciplinary sectors (SSD) of the characteristic disciplines of Management Engineering: ING-IND/16, ING-IND/17, ING-IND/35, ING-INF/04.
• Access to the course is open to graduates in other degree classes who have acquired in their first-level study path:
- at least 24 CFU in SSD: MAT/02, MAT/03, MAT/05, MAT/06, MAT/07, MAT/08, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/02, SECS-S/06;
- at least 15 CFU in SSD: FIS/01, FIS/03, FIS/07, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, CHIM/07;
- at least 12 CFU in SSD: ING-IND/16, ING-IND/17, ING-IND/35, ING-INF/04;
- at least 36 CFU in SSD: ING-IND/06, ING-IND/08, ING-IND/09, ING-IND/10, ING-IND/11, ING-IND/12, ING-IND/13, ING-IND/14, ING-IND/15, ING-IND/21, ING-IND/22, ING-IND/23, ING-IND/31, ING-IND/32, ING-IND/34, ING-INF/01, ING-INF/02, ING-INF/03, ING-INF/05, ING-INF/06, ING-INF/07, ICAR/01, ICAR/08, SECS-P/08.
• For holders of other foreign degrees recognized as suitable, the verification of curricular requirements is carried out by a committee appointed by the Department Council, considering appropriate equivalences between the contents of exams taken in the previous study path and those corresponding to the above-mentioned disciplines and sectors.
Adequacy of Personal Preparation The adequacy of personal preparation must be verified. Only candidates meeting the curricular requirements may access this verification.
The methods for verifying personal preparation are defined in the course's didactic regulations.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree, students must also demonstrate knowledge of English at least at level B2 (CEFR).
For non-native Italian speakers, the knowledge of Italian will be verified. The verification methods will be defined in the course's didactic regulations, which will also indicate - in cases of negative verification results - the training activities to be included in the study plan for acquiring the required Italian knowledge for graduates.

Department Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering Required knowledge for admission No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's graduate in Engineering for Environment and Territory is able to design, plan, design and manage works, systems, plants and services in various fields of civil-environmental engineering, which are deepened within specific curricula in different thematic areas, such as:
- Protection of the territory from natural and anthropic hazards, hazard analysis and mitigation of hydrogeological risk, protection and rehabilitation of environmental fluid bodies;
- Urban and river hydraulic infrastructure and works, reinforcement and protection works for defense systems, and in general civil works integrated into the territorial context;
- Sustainable management of environmental resources, treatment of emissions in solid, liquid and gaseous form, monitoring of quality, prevention of pollution and remediation of environmental matrices (air, water, soil);
- Management of territory and built environment, even in the presence of conflicting resource uses, in the perspective of environmental sustainability and within specific socio-economic contexts.
Additionally, the Master's graduate in Engineering for Environment and Territory is able to:
- Select and therefore use mathematical and numerical models consciously;
- Use techniques and technologies for data acquisition and analysis for environmental monitoring;
- Analyze and interpret environmental data characterized by significant complexity;
- Analyze and evaluate the environmental impact of civil and industrial works and develop procedures for strategic environmental assessment of plans and programs;
- Interact with experts from different disciplines to solve complex environmental problems.
The training path includes a core of common courses, mainly in the first year and delivered in English, with the aim of providing the typical competencies of the engineer operating in the civil-environmental field, combining them with the ability to use numerical tools for modeling environmental processes and knowledge of approaches to ecologically oriented territorial planning.
The methods and competencies acquired in the common courses are functional to deepen the more applied aspects addressed in curricula focused on specific themes. The language of the curriculum courses varies between Italian and English depending on the characteristics of the theme addressed.
Required knowledge for admission For enrollment in the Master's Degree in Engineering for Environment and Territory, possession of a bachelor's degree or another foreign degree recognized as suitable is required.
Direct admission is granted in the case of a bachelor's degree or university diploma obtained after a study course of at least three years in class L-7 (DM 270/04) or class 8 (DM 509/99), or a foreign degree recognized as suitable.
In the case of a bachelor's degree or university diploma obtained after a study course of at least three years in classes other than those listed above or another foreign degree, admission to the study course is also subject to the possession of the following minimum curricular requirements:
- 24 CFU in SSD MAT/03, MAT/05, MAT/06, MAT/07, MAT/08;
- 18 CFU in SSD CHIM/06, CHIM/07, FIS/01, FIS/03, ING-IND/10, ING-IND/11, ING-IND/22;
- 30 CFU in SSD ICAR/01, ICAR/02, ICAR/03, ICAR/06, ICAR/07;
- 12 CFU in SSD ICAR/08, ICAR/09.
Admission to the Master's Degree in Engineering for Environment and Territory is subject to verification of the student's adequate personal preparation, assessed based on results obtained in previous university studies and an interview, according to the procedures specified in the Study Course Didactic Regulations.
Admission requires knowledge of English at a level not lower than B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference.
For students not of Italian mother tongue – or who have not completed a higher education cycle in that language – who wish to choose a curriculum with mandatory courses in Italian, knowledge of Italian at least at B2 level is also required.
Students must possess the curricular requirements before the verification of personal preparation.
No academic debts or additional training obligations are allowed.

Department Department of Engineering and Computer Science Required Knowledge Verification No Program, Texts and Objectives Specific Educational Objectives of the Course and Description of the Educational Path SPECIFIC EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES Master's graduates in Information Engineering (Information Engineering):
i) are able to design, develop and manage complex systems for the acquisition, processing, extraction of information, as well as data transmission, storage and protection aspects; for this purpose, they must acquire a broad set of skills centered on Telecommunications Engineering but extended towards interdisciplinary application contexts;
ii) possess a solid technical-scientific culture in Information Engineering, as well as mathematics acquired transversally in mandatory courses;
iii) are able to integrate engineering skills with business organization elements related to development, innovation and business management;
iv) thanks to a completely English-taught curriculum, they have in-depth knowledge of the technical-scientific terminology of the field, both orally and in writing.
Additionally, based on the chosen educational orientation, they may further expand their interdisciplinary skills through in-depth study, for example, of one of the following objectives:
1) further theoretical and methodological knowledge to achieve a high degree of specialization in the field of telecommunications system design;
or acquire advanced knowledge in Information Engineering disciplines:
2) Computer Engineering disciplines for the design and development of artificial intelligence and distributed information systems;
3) Electronic Engineering disciplines for the development of electronic systems for signal acquisition and advanced computing architectures;
4) Biomedical Engineering disciplines for the acquisition, processing and automatic analysis of biomedical signals and data.
DESCRIPTION OF THE EDUCATIONAL PATH The educational path of the Master's Degree in Information Engineering includes common activities in the following learning areas:
i) disciplines related to communication systems and telecommunications networks and their applications;
ii) disciplines related to information acquisition and processing systems (signals, voice, images and video) and their applications;
iii) disciplines related to information analysis and automatic recognition systems and their applications;
iv) disciplines related to economic-management areas with an innovation perspective in business contexts.
After a substantial common path, the educational offer is divided into multiple orientations, which will be defined in the Didactic Regulations of the study program. These orientations include:
- further in-depth study of fundamental and applied disciplines of Telecommunications Engineering, such as communication systems, next-generation telecommunications networks, simulation techniques, satellite and radar systems;
- acquisition of a stronger foundation in Computer Engineering disciplines, such as artificial intelligence systems, distributed systems and IoT;
- opening to disciplines related to the electronic field, particularly the study and development of sensors for signal acquisition and processing, and advanced high-performance computing architectures;
- study of disciplines in the biomedical field, such as biomedical engineering, processing and management of biomedical data.
The educational path offered to students includes substantial laboratory activities prioritizing various application and industrial domains, projects, seminars and company internships, which promote the evaluation and development of real systems, communication skills and autonomous learning, activities dedicated to challenge-based learning, as well as renewed attention to soft skills, considered essential in a professional profile linked to scientific and technological innovation in the field of Information Engineering.
Required Knowledge for Admission To enroll in the Master's Degree in Information Engineering, a Bachelor's Degree or other foreign degree recognized as equivalent is required.
Access is subject to the possession of curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation, as described below.
Those possessing the necessary curricular requirements for admission to the Master's Degree are those who hold a Bachelor's Degree in classes L-8, or have earned a sufficient number of credits in specific CFU groups during their previous university studies, summarized below:
- 36 CFU in the group CHIM/03, CHIM/07, FIS/01-03, INF/01, MAT/02-03, MAT/05-09
- 24 CFU in the group ING-INF/01-07
For holders of other recognized equivalent degrees, curricular requirements are verified by an annual committee responsible for evaluating student curricula based on the relevance of the degree, the educational path completed in the previous studies, and the results of individual exams.
Students must possess the curricular requirements before verifying personal preparation; in particular, no academic debts or obligations are permitted.
Adequacy of Personal Preparation:
To access the Master's Degree, students must have proven knowledge of English at least B2 level (CEFR). The methods for verifying personal preparation are outlined in the study program's Didactic Regulations, which also govern the methods for verifying English language knowledge.
For students whose native language is not Italian, the knowledge of Italian will be verified. The verification methods will be defined in the Didactic Regulations of the Study Program, which will also indicate, in cases of negative verification results, the training activities to be included in the study plan for acquiring the required Italian language knowledge for Master's graduates.

Dates and deadlines for selection participation are defined in the Admission Notice. The committee evaluates only complete applications submitted within the deadlines specified in the Notice and establishes rankings separately for non-EU citizens residing abroad and for EU citizens and equivalent non-EU citizens.
Rankings are determined based on the following criteria:
- Maximum 20/100 points for coherence between the acquired degree title and the objectives of the Master's Degree in Energy Engineering;
- Maximum 60/100 points for academic curriculum and oral interview result;
- Maximum 10/100 points for proven language skills exceeding minimum requirements;
- Maximum 10/100 points for the presentation video;
Candidates with a score of 50/100 or higher are considered eligible.
Rankings are published on the University website https://international.unitn.it/masterenergy/results-and-pre-enrollment-procedures) and are valid only for the academic year for which they were established. Successful candidates must follow the procedures indicated on the Master's Degree program website in the 'Application and Admission' section to confirm their assigned study place.

Department Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering Required Knowledge Verification No Program, Texts and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's Degree in Civil Engineering is oriented towards training a high-level professional figure prepared to address and solve in a coordinated manner the complex set of design, operational, organizational and management problems characterizing the civil engineering sector or requiring an interdisciplinary approach; it consolidates the knowledge acquired in the previous career in basic scientific disciplines such as physics, mathematics and civil engineering disciplines, reaching high capacities to design, plan, program and manage complex systems, processes and services, particularly in the areas of small and large structures, structural rehabilitation and conservation, infrastructure design and integrated design with additional solid knowledge and competence in new digital technologies.
The course provides a core of common courses in the first year, with the aim of consolidating the knowledge acquired in the previous career and acquiring common specific knowledge in the field of civil engineering, particularly construction techniques, geotechnics and structural science, all in an advanced mode; specific and design knowledge is then transmitted in the characteristic and related curriculum courses, starting already from the first year, in order to form a graduate capable of moving competently in various thematic areas of civil engineering related to the design of civil engineering works in their different application fields.
The second year is entirely dedicated to specific training that differs based on the different choice areas but all with the purpose of offering the student not only theoretical, technical and regulatory knowledge and skills but also design skills in areas that allow in-depth study and specialization:
− in the design, analysis, realization and control of structures in civil and industrial contexts, referring to traditional materials (concrete, steel, wood) and advanced materials (composite materials, metamaterials) with particular attention to exceptional actions (fire, earthquakes, NaTech events, etc.);
− in the rehabilitation of civil and industrial structures, with attention to reducing seismic vulnerability and compatibility of interventions with conservation principles (reversibility, minimal impact) and environmental sustainability (use of sustainable materials such as wood), also referring to historically or monumentally significant buildings;
− in the design, realization, management and maintenance of infrastructure works (roads, bridges and hydraulic works), underground structures, support structures and foundations, with strong competencies in new digital technologies (sensors, telecommunications, data inversion techniques, optimization and artificial intelligence, decision support systems);
− in the integrated design of buildings developed in a digital BIM/HBIM environment (Building Information Modeling/Heritage Building Information Modeling) in the different phases of ideation, realization, management, maintenance and decommissioning, with particular regard to energy saving, residential comfort and innovation of technical/technological systems in new and existing civil works.
All profiles will be characterized by specific digital skills, consistent with the professional requirements of the Industry 4.0 Revolution in the construction sector. These skills include: systems and methods for monitoring, managing and controlling civil structures and infrastructure with specific competencies in new digital technologies (wireless communication infrastructures, distributed wireless monitoring and non-invasive techniques, data inversion techniques, optimization and artificial intelligence, numerical methods, decision support systems).
Ethics and professional deontology are specifically addressed by sector professionals, within a specific agreement that the Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering has with the Engineering Professional Orders through seminars proposed within specific teaching activities.
The course will provide the appropriate conditions to create a context in which students can be involved in design activities and create moments of comparison, discussion and reflection. Some curricula will offer courses in English, ensuring compliance with the regulations regarding courses declared in two languages; for non-native Italian students who choose an English or English-Italian curriculum, training activities are provided for acquiring the required knowledge of Italian.
The training provided enables the Master's Civil Engineer to develop scientific and study skills that encourage both individual learning and research as well as collaborative learning, allowing Master's graduates to participate in selections for access to academic careers or professional contexts.
The educational content offered in the curricula is specified in the Course Regulations.
Required Knowledge for Access For access to the Master's Degree, specific curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation are required, which must be verified. The required curricular requirements for access to the Master's Degree consist of:
- Possession of a first-level degree in classes L-7 ex DM 270/04 and Class 8 ex DM 509/99;

- Possession of a first-level degree in classes other than L-7 ex DM 270/04 and Class 8 ex DM 509/99 or a foreign degree recognized as equivalent, and having acquired a minimum number of credit points (CFU) in specific groups of scientific-disciplinary sectors in previous study paths:
• At least 20 CFU in SSD MAT/02, MAT/03, MAT/05, MAT/08;

Admission Procedures For admission to the Master's Degree, specific curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation are required, which must be verified. - holding a first-level degree in classes other than L-7 under DM 270/04 and Class 8 under DM 509/99 or a foreign degree recognized as suitable, and having acquired a minimum number of credits (CFU) in specific groups of scientific-disciplinary sectors in previous study paths:

• at least 18 CFU in the SSD CHIM/03, CHIM/06, CHIM/07, FIS/01, FIS/02, FIS/03, FIS/04, FIS/05, FIS/06, FIS/07, FIS/08;

The Teaching Area Committee is responsible for verifying the curricular requirements and appropriate equivalences for holders of degrees with an ordering different from that regulated by DM 270/04, and also states that candidates not meeting the required admission requirements must independently prepare and complete the credits before the verification of the adequacy of their preparation.
If a student from another Department or University wishes to submit a request for evaluation of curricular requirements, the student must first ensure they have earned at least 150 CFU.
The entrance knowledge assessments concern:
a. The results obtained in the previous university career:
• direct admission: students who in previous exam sessions achieved a weighted average grade of at least 24/30 are directly admitted;
• admission by assessment: students who in the exam sessions for the degree achieved a weighted average grade between 22/30 and 24/30 (inclusive of 22/30 but exclusive of 24/30) are subject to an assessment of the adequacy of their personal preparation, including an oral interview.
• exclusion criterion: Students who in the exam sessions for the degree achieved a weighted average grade below 22/30 are excluded from the possibility of enrolling in the Master's Degree course.
b. Foreign language knowledge: To access the Master's Degree course, the student must possess proven linguistic skills in English at least at level B2 (Common European Framework of Reference). The methods for verifying linguistic knowledge are defined within the Course of Study Teaching Regulations.

Department Department of Engineering and Information Science Entry Requirements Verification No Study Program, Texts and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the study path The Master's Degree in Computer Science aims to train individuals possessing both in-depth knowledge of the theoretical principles underlying computer science, and specific skills in one of the macro-areas related to software technologies, systems and networks, bioinformatics, multimedia, dedicated systems, service engineering, or security.
The study program provides acquisition of specialized computer science knowledge, methodologies and technologies enabling graduates to plan, design, develop, manage, estimate, test and manage complex or innovative systems for the generation, transmission and processing of information.
During the study path, after acquiring the aforementioned knowledge and skills, students may choose to further consolidate their expertise in a path focused on computer science and technologies, providing advanced, innovative or experimental methodologies to address particularly complex technological problems at an industrial level, or to pursue a PhD program.
Alternatively, students may pursue interdisciplinary paths aimed at completing their computer science preparation with economic/managerial knowledge on technological innovation and entrepreneurship in the ICT sector, or through interdisciplinary study, or leading to a double degree with a foreign university.
Among the common objectives we recall:
- The ability to work with broad autonomy, also assuming responsibility for large-scale projects and structures.
- Deepening the scientific method of investigation, the logical-deductive reasoning method, and inductive methods related to experimentation;
- Knowledge of the fundamentals, techniques and methods for designing and implementing both basic and applied information systems;
Among the specific objectives we recall:
- Deepening the scientific and technological aspects of one of the macro-areas of computer science or expanding one's skills through the study of more than one macro-area.
- Completing one's education through training activities offered by other study programs at the University of Trento (biology, economics, mathematics, etc.) or through activities related to entrepreneurship and innovation offered within the educational programs of the European Institute of Innovation and Technology.
Among the activities that specialist graduates will perform, in particular:
- Analysis and creation of models for complex problems in various application contexts.
- Design and development of high-quality information systems.
- Design of systems in areas related to computer science, in the fields of research, industry, services, environment, health, cultural heritage, and public administration.
Additionally, specific courses and seminars related to entrepreneurship will be offered, also with participation from successful entrepreneurs, to facilitate full satisfaction in the job market and the creation of new companies.
The courses of the Master's Degree in Computer Science will be taught in English; this allows, and already allows, attracting international students from all over the world, and establishing double degree programs with the most prestigious European and American universities. This will allow students to immerse themselves in an international cultural environment that fosters both English communication skills and intercultural relationships.
Entry Requirements Students admitted to the Master's Degree must hold a First Level Degree or another foreign degree recognized as suitable, whose study curriculum includes, as a minimum requirement, basic computer science knowledge and skills in programming, algorithms, data management, and systems (hardware, operating systems, networks, etc.); as well as theoretical knowledge in the field of analysis and discrete mathematics. Advanced knowledge in computer architecture, operating systems, algorithms, networks, language theory, and web systems may be essential depending on the chosen path in the Master's Degree. A knowledge of English at least at level B1 is also required.
The Didactic Regulations detail in detail:
- The disciplinary and general knowledge and skills required for entry to the Master's Degree;
- The methods by which the competent teaching structure verifies such knowledge and skills, specifying which Bachelor's Degrees can be considered "transitional," i.e., allow automatic entry to the Master's Degree, and which instead require a detailed analysis of the student's curriculum and motivations.
- The methods by which the competent teaching structure makes available to students and pre-enrollees appropriate forms of self-assessment of such knowledge and skills.

Verification of required knowledge for admission No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's Degree in Data Science trains a professional with strong cross-disciplinary competencies capable of: 1) managing and analyzing large volumes of data produced by natural and social systems to support decision-making processes in economic-production, political-social contexts, and scientific research activities in public administration, industry, public and private services, and the third sector; 2) occupying high-level technical and/or managerial roles in contexts requiring a good combination of competencies in computer science, mathematics, statistics, and social, psychological, and economic disciplines.
More specifically, Master's graduates in Data Science are able to:
- identify, represent, acquire, manage, and analyze large quantities of heterogeneous data in the most appropriate way, using state-of-the-art techniques to decisively contribute to achieving the goals of the organization/agency they collaborate with;
- interpret and/or anticipate the needs of the sector in which they operate and propose effective solutions, thereby supporting decision-making processes and strategic choices of companies and management, and contributing to developing evolution lines, operational plans, and generating indications and programs for the development of the organization/agency's actions;
- recognize and leverage the peculiarities as well as manage the challenges of the infrastructures underlying Data Science, both regarding the generation and processing of large volumes of structured and unstructured data;
- operate in multiple contexts, even highly interdisciplinary ones, due to possessing systematic computer science and mathematical-statistical competencies as well as fundamental knowledge of legal, ethical, business, and/or social aspects related to data acquisition, management, processing, and use;
- effectively communicate the results of their work using new technologies, techniques, and visualization tools.
These objectives are achieved through a structured path consisting of:
1) a first-year alignment phase that includes: a) an integration activity of existing competencies through differentiated attendance, depending on the first-level degree background, of a series of courses aimed at strengthening knowledge and competencies in information science, social sciences, economic, and psychological-cognitive disciplines; b) specific training in Data Science through a series of courses for all students designed to provide specific competencies in computer science and mathematical-statistical disciplines fundamental for operating in this field;
2) a second-year specialization phase for students in different application areas of Data Science. The training activity provides a single exit path that can be flexibly characterized by combining courses aimed at providing specific domain knowledge in Data Science application areas (social, economic, psychological, mathematical, computer science) with laboratory courses aimed at providing advanced competencies in the collection, analysis, and interpretation of large data volumes and high-level, cutting-edge technical competencies in Data Science. The second year's training offer is completed by the possibility to include in the study plan freely chosen credits obtained by successfully passing any course offered by the Master's Degree or by the university academic structures, provided they are consistent with the course's educational objectives.
As this is a Master's Degree taught in English, students whose native language is not Italian are required to complete training activities to acquire the necessary Italian language knowledge required for the graduate.
Required knowledge for admission To access the Master's Degree, a first-level university degree or diploma of at least three years' duration, or another foreign degree recognized as suitable, and specific curricular requirements are required. Additionally, adequate personal preparation must be verified.
Formative deficits or additional formative obligations are not permitted under any circumstances.
Admission to the Master's Degree Course is subject to verification of the following requirements, which must be met for enrollment:
a) curricular requirements:
i. having obtained a first-level degree from Italian universities or another foreign degree recognized as suitable according to current regulations;
ii. possessing at least:
- 6 CFU in SSD INF* and/or ING-INF*
- 6 CFU in SSD SPS* and/or SECS-P* and/or M-PSI*/IUS*
- 6 CFU in SSD MAT* and/or SECS-S*
- additional 24 CFU in total in the SSDs listed above The possession of fundamental knowledge in computer science and probability and statistics will be verified through the evaluation of syllabi of exams taken and related to the relevant disciplinary areas.
b) possessing an English language certificate at least at B2 level.
The possession of candidates' personal preparation as well as English language knowledge will be verified according to the methods indicated in the course's didactic regulations.

Verification of required knowledge for admission No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's Degree in Data Science trains professionals with strong cross-disciplinary skills capable of working in multidisciplinary environments. The graduate with a master's degree in Data Science will be able to manage and analyze large volumes of data produced by natural and social systems to support decision-making processes in economic-production, political-social contexts, and scientific research activities in public administration, industry, public and private services, and the third sector.
The graduate with a master's degree in Data Science will be able to hold high-level technical and/or managerial roles in contexts requiring a good combination of skills in computer science, mathematics, statistics, and social, psychological, and economic disciplines.
At the end of the program, the graduate with a master's degree in Data Science will be able to analyze the elements contributing to the formation of the data under study and identify possible sources of noise, distortion, and uncertainty; will be able to use computer platforms for data storage, management, and transformation, being aware of the performance limitations and/or advantages offered by various platforms; will be able to identify strategic objectives that can be best pursued through data analysis, effectively combining methodologies from social, psychological, and business management and public and private administration sciences with computer technologies and methodologies, possessing expertise in each area.
In greater detail, the graduate in Data Science:
- is able to understand the origin and characteristics of the data processed; knows the ICT technologies related to the data lifecycle and their performance limitations; can analyze and manage the flow of data generation, acquisition, transmission, and access; can manage and integrate heterogeneous archives of statistical and administrative data;
- is able to combine methods and techniques from social and psychological sciences, business management, and public and private administration with computer technologies and methodologies, and mathematical and statistical data analysis, possessing expertise in each area and effectively interpreting technological and organizational change in companies and administrations;
- is able to analyze and interpret data according to their nature and variety, applying the most appropriate analytical approach to respond to the activities or objectives of the organization or public or private entity.
- is able to identify and access data sources and choose the most suitable methods and models to support and guide decision-making and strategic choices in business and management, able to develop evolution paths, operational plans, and generate indications and development programs for action, also through the application of dimensionality reduction techniques and the development of predictive models to create advanced knowledge systems.
- is able to work in interdisciplinary teams and use the most appropriate communication and storytelling methods to present empirical evidence in a form suitable to support tactical and strategic management decisions, paying particular attention to issues related to the synthesis and effective representation and visualization of information; is able to fluently use English in written and oral form, in addition to Italian, with reference to disciplinary terminology.
- has basic legal knowledge in areas and issues related to the use of information technologies and data processing (referring, among others, to security, privacy protection, and legal validity issues).
The interdepartmental nature of the study course allows for the inclusion of students from diverse backgrounds, providing them with a strongly interdisciplinary curriculum.
The initial courses will have programs aimed at integrating different competencies and will cover the fundamental disciplines of Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, and Social, Psychological, and Economic Sciences. Subsequent courses and laboratories will focus on relevant applications of Data Science, particularly for Social, Psychological, and Economic Sciences. A substantial offer of optional courses and laboratories will allow for the design of paths tailored to specific areas. Finally, the graduate with a master's degree in Data Science will possess a basic cultural, scientific, and methodological preparation enabling access to higher university study levels beyond the master's degree (second-level master's and doctoral programs).
Required knowledge for admission Admission to the master's degree program will be subject to verification of the following requirements, whose possession is a necessary condition for enrollment:
a) academic requirements:
− hold a first-level degree, obtained at Italian universities or another foreign degree deemed suitable;
− possess English language skills at least at B2 level;
− hold at least 6 CFU related to courses belonging to the SSD Computer Science (INF*/ING-INF*), 6 CFU related to courses belonging to the SSDs of Humanities, Social, Legal, and Economic disciplines (SPS*/SECS-P*/M-PSI*/IUS*), 6 CFU related to courses belonging to the SSDs of technical-scientific disciplines in Mathematics (MAT*) and Statistics (SECS-S*), and at least an additional 24 CFU in these SSDs.
b) specific preparation requirements:
− demonstrate good analytical skills for topics in social sciences and information science,
− demonstrate good ability to address methodological problems,
− demonstrate good ability to read research data.
The assessment of personal preparation is carried out according to the criteria and methods defined by the course's didactic regulations.

− the methods for verifying English language knowledge, as well as the timing and methods for verifying students' personal preparation;

Program, Texts, and Objectives
Specific Educational Objectives of the Course and Description of the Study Path
The general objective of the Master's program is to train graduates with solid knowledge and skills for the development, experimentation, and management of technologies, instruments, and devices for biomedical applications and for the analysis and modeling of the complexity of physiological and healthcare systems.
Leveraging the faculty to provide additional courses beyond those specified by the degree class (Decree MUR December 19, 2023), the program extends the core activities beyond the reference SSDs ING-INF/06 and ING-IND/34 by adding two prerequisite disciplines to consolidate engineering skills essential for developing technologies and tools for advanced biomedical applications, focusing on materials and electronics for bio- and electro-medical applications. To this end, the core courses of the Master's program are identified as Biomedical Engineering: ING-IND/34 and ING-INF/06, totaling 39 CFU. These are supplemented by engineering disciplines in materials science and technology (ING-IND/22) and electronics (ING-INF/01), totaling 12 CFU, as foundational elements to strengthen knowledge in industrial engineering and computer and electronic engineering, which form the core educational pillars of the new program. Additionally, essential complementary courses include biomedical disciplines related to physiology, biology, and medical sciences to develop targeted competencies for the development of technologies and tools for personalized and precision medicine. The interdisciplinary and multi-disciplinary training is further ensured through a corpus of related and integrative activities aimed at consolidating engineering skills in biomechanics, computer science, medical robotics, and fluid dynamics.
The combination of these courses will provide graduates with fundamental skills for the development and evaluation of medical instrumentation, devices, and equipment, biomaterials and advanced manufacturing techniques, biomedical data and signal processing, physiology of systems, principles of diagnostics for personalized medicine, and the representation of medical-biological knowledge through advanced modeling. These competencies form the foundational knowledge for enabling modern individual-centered medicine. Graduates will also acquire knowledge in business organization, innovation processes, and professional ethics.
The courses of the program also offer specific in-depth insights that guide the study path toward technologies for prevention, precision diagnostics, therapeutic, rehabilitative, and assistive interventions, addressing information processing (data, signals, images), the study of advanced technologies for regenerative and precision medicine development, and the creation of devices, systems, services, and processes centered on the citizen/patient (personalized medicine).
The educational process will be implemented through lectures, expert meetings, and seminars, classroom exercises, and laboratory activities in the Department, involving companies and healthcare organizations for the development of application-based projects based on real scenarios and cases. These project activities, proposed within the statutory courses of the degree program, will serve to deepen technical/scientific knowledge, understand business rules, and guide career orientation. The internship and thesis conclude the educational path.
Throughout the educational path, the state of the art of the various disciplines will be highlighted, along with open challenges, emphasizing the continuous evolution of technology and the need for ongoing updates in the context of environmental, economic, and social sustainability of innovation. To support these goals, the program may organize specific seminars on topics of particular interest and meetings with the business world and company internships aimed at thesis activities, both technical and recruitment-related.
The educational path aims to achieve the following specific objectives:
- Provide in-depth and operational knowledge of innovation development pathways in biomedical sectors and individual-centered health technologies, with attention to sustainability and process safety;
- Develop the ability to analyze and model complex systems;
- Acquire mastery of the main reference methods for the design, development, characterization, and management of medical devices, systems, and services for biomedical applications;
- Provide a strong culture of innovation and the ability to assess the multidimensional impact of innovation;
- Provide skills for leading and coordinating research and development projects for innovative products, systems, and services;
- Provide specific competencies in signal, data processing, and information extraction for diagnostic, therapeutic, rehabilitative, and assistive purposes;
- Develop awareness of the social role of innovation in healthcare and the profession of Biomedical Engineer;
- Provide competencies in materials technologies for biomedical applications and biofabrication;
- Provide foundational skills for the development of Health 4.0;
- Provide basic knowledge of diagnostics and therapy for personalized medicine
Access Requirements

TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM: Interuniversity Joint Title
SECTION: Admission Procedures
URL: https://unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10761

Admission Procedures The master's degree course in Bioengineering for Personalized Medicine does not have a set number.
For enrollment in the master's degree course in Bioengineering for Personalized Medicine, it is required to hold a degree or other foreign academic qualification recognized as suitable.
Access to the course is also subject to meeting the academic requirements and verifying the adequacy of the personal preparation as specified below. For the academic requirements, see the previous Table A3.a.
The personal preparation for access to the master's degree in Bioengineering for Personalized Medicine is considered adequate for graduates who meet the academic requirements and have achieved an average grade, weighted by the corresponding credits, of at least 23/30 in the examination sessions taken for the degree (excluding the final exam). In the calculation of the average, a grade of 30 with honors is considered equivalent to 31/30.
To access the master's degree course, the student must also possess proven knowledge of English at least at level B2 (CEFR). The student who has not acquired this knowledge in their previous academic career must provide an appropriate certification of equivalent or higher level issued by an officially recognized body or by the University of Trento's Language Center (CLA). The list of accepted certificates is available on the CLA website (www.unitn.it/cla).
There are no interviews to verify the student's basic preparation, but the documents attesting the curriculum, the average grade, and English knowledge provided at the time of application via an online procedure active from early June to the end of November are considered.
For students from non-EU countries, a call with selection based on qualifications and an optional interview will be provided starting from the academic year 2025/26.

UNIVERSITY: University of Trento
COURSE: [0342H] ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEMS
TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM: General Description
SECTION: General Description
URL: https://unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10738

[0342H] ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEMS Master's Degree English
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration
2 years Order
2020
Status Open Credits
120 CFU Type Master's Degree Program Category Engineering, Computer Science and Technologies Regulation 270/04
Master's Degree Class LM-32 - Class of Master's Degrees in Computer Engineering Interdepartmental Course No Programmed Access (80 Places)
Location Hill Campus - Povo B - via Sommarive, 9 (Sustainable Capacity: 80)
Department Department of Engineering and Computer Science Prerequisites for Access No Course Program, Texts and Objectives Specific Educational Objectives and Description of the Educational Path SPECIFIC EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES Master's graduates in Artificial Intelligence Systems:
i) are able to develop and utilize innovative methods and tools to address emerging issues, designing, engineering, organizing and managing complex and innovative systems based on intelligent computer systems; for this purpose, they must acquire a broad set of skills centered in the field of Computer Engineering but extended towards interdisciplinary application contexts;
ii) possess a solid theoretical-scientific culture in mathematics and information engineering;
iii) are able to identify connections between ethical principles and legal rules, as well as understand the implications of technology use and the impact of their design choices.
Additionally, based on the chosen educational orientation, they may further expand their interdisciplinary skills to achieve one of the following objectives in addition to those previously listed:
1) deepen their theoretical and methodological knowledge to achieve a high degree of specialization in the field of design of artificial intelligence-based systems;
2) acquire advanced knowledge in various disciplines of information engineering for various industrial, environmental and biomedical applications;
3) propose strategies for bringing AI-based products, processes and organizations to market, competitive in terms of efficiency, productivity and sustainability;
4) integrate computational, behavioral approaches and neuroimaging technologies for a better understanding of human behavior and to provide inspiration for the development of new intelligent systems.
DESCRIPTION OF THE EDUCATIONAL PATH The educational path of the Master's Degree in Artificial Intelligence Systems is entirely delivered in English. It includes common activities in the following learning areas:
i) foundational and applied computer science disciplines of artificial intelligence, such as knowledge representation, automated reasoning, machine learning (also known as automatic learning), natural language processing, optimization, human-computer interaction;
ii) disciplines related to industrial and service robotics, operational autonomy of mechatronic devices, and automation of complex processes;
iii) disciplines related to acquisition, processing and analysis of information (signals, voice, images and video) and computer vision and their applications;
iv) disciplines related to the legal field, with particular reference to basic knowledge of legal regimes relevant for the design and application of artificial intelligence systems;
After a substantial common path, the educational offer is divided into multiple orientations, which will be defined in the Didactic Regulations of the study program. In particular:
1) The first orientation provides further in-depth study in mathematical and/or foundational and applied computer science disciplines of artificial intelligence and those related to robotics.
2) The second orientation aims to provide a stronger training in information engineering disciplines for the design and use of artificial intelligence systems in diverse application contexts.
3) The third orientation opens to disciplines related to the economic-management area, for the organization, management and innovation of decision and production systems based on artificial intelligence.
4) Finally, the last orientation is based on disciplines of cognitive neuroscience, language, and their applications to artificial intelligence models.
The educational path offered to the student includes substantial laboratory activities prioritizing various application and industrial domains, projects, seminars and company internships, which foster the evaluation and development of real systems and the ability to communicate and learn autonomously, considered essential in a professional profile linked to scientific and technological innovation in artificial intelligence.
Prerequisites for Access For access to the Master's Degree in Artificial Intelligence Systems, the possession of curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation as specified below is required.
Curricular Requirements:
1. possession of a degree in one of the following classes L-8, L-9, L-31 or another foreign degree recognized as suitable;
1.bis if the first-level degree held is in classes different from those indicated in point 1), at least 36 CFU in the following scientific sectors must have been acquired during the previous university career: CHIM/03, CHIM/06-07, FIS/01-03, MAT/01-09, SECS-S/01
2. at least 12 CFU in the scientific-disciplinary sectors INF/01 or ING-INF/05 must have been acquired.
Personal Preparation Requirements:
The candidate must demonstrate:
1) sufficient basic knowledge and skills to undertake the educational activities provided for the Master's Degree, according to the modalities defined in the Didactic Regulations of the Study Program;
2) knowledge of English at least at B2 level (according to CEFR);
- The Didactic Regulations specify the required level of Italian language knowledge and the verification modalities. Students may include activities in their study plan to achieve these linguistic competencies;
- Verification of personal preparation is mandatory; any curricular integrations must be acquired before the verification of personal preparation;
- The modalities for verifying personal preparation are outlined in the Didactic Regulations of the study program.

COURSE: [0126H] MANAGEMENT OF SUSTAINABILITY AND TOURISM
TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM: General Description
SECTION: General Description

[0126H] MANAGEMENT OF SUSTAINABILITY AND TOURISM Master's Degree
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration
2 years Order
2015
Status Open Credits
120 CFU Type Master's Degree Programs Category Economics, Management and Law Regulation Reform 270/04
Degree Class LM-77 - Class of Master's Degrees in Economic and Business Sciences Joint Course No Programmed Access (55 Places)
Location City Campus - Economics - via Inama, 5
Department Department of Economics and Management Entry Requirements Verification No Course Program, Texts and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's Degree in MaST aims to prepare qualified graduates with strong multidisciplinary competence oriented towards sustainability in the management of for-profit and non-profit enterprises, national and international, and public bodies and administrations operating in various sectors, particularly the tourism sector.
More specifically, the MaST Master's program sets the following specific educational objectives:
A. Ensure adequate economic-managerial preparation oriented towards sustainability, enabling graduates, regardless of their sector of employment, to identify and implement eco-sustainable business strategies and policies, and design innovative and sustainable services;
B. Ensure integration of advanced management preparation with multidisciplinary knowledge required by national and international standards for:
B.1 Analyze, design and manage companies and organizations operating in the tourism sector and sustainable environmental management,
B.2 Analyze, design, implement and monitor the integrated tourism offer planning of a territory,
B.3 Promote and manage customer satisfaction, quality and safety of tourism processes while respecting sustainable environmental management,
B.4 Carry out complex activities of guidance, coordination of decision-making processes, negotiation of agreements and management of conflicts related to the tourism sector and sustainable environmental management.
The main learning areas relate to: management of tourism and service enterprises, management of tourism systems and destinations, tourism marketing and territorial marketing, quality and environmental management systems and certification, economic history of tourism, environmental economics and techniques for environmental asset valuation, quantitative techniques for data analysis, decision models underlying consumer choice analysis and analysis of consumer/tourist behavior.
The internship typically involves a period at a company or organization, under the guidance of a company tutor and an academic tutor.
The thesis represents an important moment of in-depth study, also theoretical-conceptual, of topics typical of sustainability and tourism management, and is usually accompanied by an empirical component.
Entry Requirements for Admission Enrollment in the MaST Master's Degree program is subject to verification of the following requirements:
- Academic requirements:
• Hold a first-level degree, obtained at an Italian university or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent;
• Possess English language proficiency at least at B1 level or equivalent;
- Specific preparation requirements:
• Demonstrate good ability to read and comment on data regarding the economic performance of companies and the economic context;
• Demonstrate good analytical skills in addressing quantitative problems;
• Have adequate familiarity with basic statistical techniques;
• Have good ability to analyze economic and business problems.
The required knowledge typically includes the equivalent of at least 48 CFU related to courses belonging to the scientific-disciplinary sectors of the degree classes 17 and 28 (former DM. 509/99) or degree classes 18 and 33 (former DM. 270/04).
Specific disciplinary knowledge requirements are indicated in the Study Course Didactic Regulation that governs the verification of such requirements.
Personal preparation will be assessed according to the modalities defined in the Study Course Didactic Regulation. The verification of the possession of these requirements is regulated by the Study Course Didactic Regulation.

[0124H] MANAGEMENT Master's Degree English
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration
2 years Structure
2011
Status Open Credits
120 CFU Type Master's degree programs Category Economics, Management and Law Regulation Reform 270/04
Degree Class LM-77 - Class of Master's degrees in Economic and Business Sciences Joint Course No Open Access Location City Campus - Economics - via Inama, 5
Department Department of Economics and Management Verification of required knowledge for admission No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's degree in Management aims to prepare qualified graduates with strong competence in managing companies, for national and multinational enterprises, non-profit organizations, public bodies and administrations operating in various sectors.
The Master's degree aims to form professional figures capable of managing main business functions in different contexts, both through full mastery of analysis techniques and applied knowledge supporting decision-making processes, and by coordinating and organizing operational units.
The structure of the Master's degree in Management is also designed to enable the activation of an "equivalent" degree course (ex DM 50/2010, §31) entirely in English with the same educational objectives and employment opportunities. The equivalent course, organized and managed in partnership with foreign universities, provides for students to spend significant periods (at least one year) at other universities and to obtain a jointly accredited degree in different countries, or a double degree.
The internship typically involves a period at a company to address a specific issue of direct interest to the company, under the guidance of a company tutor and an academic tutor.
The thesis represents an important moment of in-depth study, also theoretical-conceptual, on typical management topics, and is accompanied by an empirical component.
Students participating in programs for the issuance of double degrees or joint degrees with other European universities and spending a period at one or more universities in other countries follow a common program for all participating students or otherwise compatible with their respective academic regulations, having the training activities carried out at foreign institutions recognized based on specific agreements between universities according to the European Credit Transfer System (ECTS) scheme. The evaluation of achievement tests is converted based on specific conversion tables.
The academic regulations of the study course may provide for the activation of training paths or curricula.
Required knowledge for admission Enrollment in the Master's degree in Management is conditional on verification of the following requirements:
- Academic requirements:
o Hold a first-level degree, obtained at Italian universities or another foreign degree recognized as suitable;
o Demonstrate proficiency in English at least at level B1 or equivalent;
- Specific preparation requirements:
o Demonstrate good ability to read and comment on data regarding the economic performance of companies and the economic-financial context;
o Demonstrate good analytical skills in addressing quantitative problems;
o Have adequate familiarity with basic statistical techniques;
o Demonstrate good ability to analyze economic and business problems.
The required knowledge typically include the equivalent of at least 60 CFU related to courses belonging to the scientific-disciplinary sectors of basic and characteristic disciplines of classes 17 and 28 (ex DM. 509/99) or classes 18 and 33 (ex DM. 270/04).
Specific disciplinary knowledge requirements are indicated in the academic regulations of the study course that governs the verification of such requirements.
Personal preparation is evaluated according to the modalities defined in the academic regulations of the study course.
Verification of the possession of these requirements is regulated by the academic regulations of the study course.
For Master's degree courses (equivalent courses) that can be activated entirely in a foreign language and provided for in the present structure, the language requirement for admission is set at least level B2 in English.
In the case of joint degrees with other universities, the entry requirements may be specified in the academic regulations of the study course to meet the requirements requested by the regulations of other countries in agreement.

CURRICULUM: Admission procedures
SECTION: Admission procedures

Admission procedures For access to the Master's degree in Management, a quota is set. Selection takes place from April to November and involves evaluation of academic requirements and verification of candidates' personal preparation.
Below are details on Academic Requirements and Methods for verifying students' personal preparation.
ACADEMIC REQUIREMENTS For specific academic requirements, admission to the Master's degree in Management requires acquisition of knowledge and skills in the following fields.
Economic Field Scientific disciplines: SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02
Credits: 12
Business Field Scientific disciplines: SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08;
Credits: 12 (at least half in SECS-P/07 - accounting)
Legal Field Scientific disciplines: IUS-01, IUS-05, IUS-09
Credits: 4.
Mathematical Field Scientific discipline: SECS-S/06
Credits: 8
Statistical Field Scientific discipline: SECS-S/01
Credits: 5
Commercial Legal Field Scientific discipline: IUS/04
Credits: 4
Corporate Finance Field Scientific disciplines: SECS-P/09, SECS-P/11
Credits: 5
METHODS FOR VERIFYING PERSONAL PREPARATION The adequacy of personal preparation is evaluated based on the weighted average of grades obtained in the previous first-cycle studies, and/or on the weighted average of grades obtained in the previous first-cycle studies in specific scientific disciplines and/or through the administration of specific disciplinary assessment tests. The annual admission notice will specify the assessment method, and if verification is based on the average from previous studies, the minimum admission threshold representing adequate personal preparation will be defined.
For verification of English language knowledge, which must be at least at B1 level or equivalent, assessment is normally based on results from internationally recognized tests or on language proficiency assessments issued by UniTrento or another university.
The possession of general and specific academic requirements is normally verified through evaluation of the curriculum. For students for whom the required knowledge cannot be assessed based solely on the curriculum, alternative verification methods may be adopted, specifically:
- specific tests administered directly;
- an interview focused on disciplines, to be conducted also via telephone conference.
Graduates who do not meet the minimum credit requirements specified in the previous paragraphs may request curriculum evaluation, after which they will be informed of the exams to take to meet the required minimum credits.
Graduates holding a foreign degree may undergo an interview, also via telephone conference, to verify personal preparation and possession of the required knowledge for admission to the Master's degree. They must also demonstrate proficiency in Italian language at least at B1 level or equivalent.
Further information and details are available on the website: http://offertaformativa.unitn.it/it/lm/management/requisiti-ammissione and in the attached admission notice.
