[0119H] INTERNATIONAL MANAGEMENT - MANAGEMENT INTERNAZIONALE Master's Degree English
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration
2 years Order
2011
Status Open Credits
120 CFU Type Master's Degree Program Category Economics, Management and Law Regulation Reform 270/04
Master's Degree Class LM-77 - Class of Master's Degrees in Economic and Business Sciences Joint Course No Programmed Access (35 Places)
Location City Campus - Economics - via Inama, 5 (Sustainable Capacity: 35)
Department Department of Economics and Management Entry Requirements Verification No Course Program, Texts and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's Degree in International Management aims to train individuals capable of making strategic and operational decisions of high complexity in companies operating in international markets. The Master's graduate in International Management will develop a multidisciplinary education strongly oriented towards decision-making during their studies. Their background will be characterized by three pillars: good analytical ability regarding markets and the institutions that regulate them, solid ability to use tools for forecasting and quantitative analysis of business data, and the ability to interact with different cultural and institutional contexts.
The curriculum of the Master's Degree in International Management, in order to promote the practical application of acquired knowledge, specifically includes a training internship at companies with an international orientation or institutions regulating trade in supranational contexts.
The training path of the International Management degree first requires students, coming from very different educational backgrounds, to homogenize their language on Economics and Management topics through participation in general courses on these subjects.
The training then focuses on deepening the critical aspects of the international dimension of managerial disciplines in various functional specializations and international economics. International legal training is part of the path, both in terms of norm formation and regulation of relations.
The path includes subsequent in-depth study of specific topics of international management.
An obligatory internship period, to be carried out in Italy and abroad, brings students into direct contact with business realities operating in the global context. Teaching activities include active student participation through projects, individual and group work, case discussions, and field work.
Required Entry Knowledge Access to the Master's Degree in International Management is subject to verification of the following requirements:
- Academic requirements:
o Hold a first-level degree, obtained at an Italian university or another foreign degree recognized as suitable;
o Possess English language proficiency at least at B2 level or equivalent;
o Proficiency in personal productivity applications (Open Office, Microsoft Office, etc.) at ECDL (European Computer Driving Licence) level or equivalent;
- Specific preparation requirements:
o Demonstrate good ability in reading and commenting on data regarding the economic performance of companies and the economic-financial context;
o Demonstrate good analytical skills in addressing quantitative problems;
o Have good familiarity with basic statistical techniques;
o Possess good ability to analyze economic and business problems.
These knowledge typically include at least 60 CFU related to courses belonging to the scientific-disciplinary sectors characteristic of the Master's Degree in International Management, particularly SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/06, JUS-/01.
The possession of these requirements is verified through curriculum screening and an assessment, to be conducted according to the procedures defined in the Course Study Didactic Regulations.
Personal preparation is also assessed according to the procedures defined in the Course Study Didactic Regulations.

UNIVERSITY: University of Trento
COURSE: [0119H] INTERNATIONAL MANAGEMENT - INTERNATIONAL MANAGEMENT
TYPE: Master's Degree
SECTION: Admission Procedures

Admission Procedures The access is limited to a set number. The selection takes place between February and July and is based on the following criteria: previous academic degree, certified English language proficiency (IELTS or TOEFL), any other international tests (e.g., GMAT, GRE), CV, reference letters, and overall profile assessment by the Selection Committee.
Local Admission Planning The Department Council annually proposes the set number within the deadlines set by current regulations and in sufficient time for adequate information. The Department Council's proposal is reviewed by the Academic Senate, expanded to include student representation, and subsequently approved by the Board of Directors.
Admission Requirements The admission to the Master's degree in International Management - International Management is handled by a dedicated committee (admission committee), annually appointed by the Department Council upon the proposal of the course coordinator. The committee's activities may, if necessary, also be conducted via telephone conference or online.
Access to the Master's degree course in International Management - International Management is subject to verification of the following requirements:
a) General Academic Requirements:
- holding a first-level degree obtained from an Italian university or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent;
- demonstrating English language proficiency at least at B2 level or equivalent;
- proficiency in personal productivity applications (Open Office, Microsoft Office, etc.) at ECDL (European Computer Driving Licence) level or equivalent;
b) Specific Academic Requirements:
- demonstrating good ability to read and comment on data related to the economic performance of companies and the economic-financial context;
- demonstrating good analytical skills in addressing quantitative problems;
- having good familiarity with basic techniques of descriptive statistics;
- having good ability to analyze economic and business-related problems.
These knowledge areas typically include the equivalent of at least 60 CFU related to courses belonging to the scientific-disciplinary sectors characteristic of the Master's degree in International Management - International Management, particularly SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/06, JUS/01.
c) Personal Preparation Requirements: The personal preparation is also assessed according to the following methods.
Method of Verifying Academic Requirements The possession of the requirements is typically verified through a review of the academic curriculum. For students for whom the required knowledge cannot be verified based on the curriculum, the Committee, based on available information, may adopt alternative assessment methods, specifically:
- based on the results of direct tests administered;
- based on an interview focused on the disciplines, which may also be conducted via alternative methods such as video conference;
- based on the results of tests offered by accredited organizations (e.g., GMAT or GRE).
For verifying English language proficiency at least at B2 level or equivalent, results of internationally recognized tests or other language proficiency assessments are used. Specific details are referenced in the annual admission notice. The aforementioned tests must typically be taken by the deadline for the admission application. Alternatively, a declaration from the applicant's previous university stating that the official language of the first-level degree course or equivalent followed by the candidate is English is considered sufficient. The assessment Committee may request an additional interview to verify language proficiency. The requirement is also considered fulfilled for candidates who are native English speakers.
Method of Assessing Personal Preparation The primary element for assessing personal preparation is the result of taking the GMAT (The Graduate Management Admission Test) or GRE (Graduate Record Examinations), available according to an annual international schedule set by the certifying bodies. Students who have not taken the test may still request an assessment of their previous academic results, which will be evaluated in relation to the distribution of academic outcomes from the educational institutions and/or countries of origin. This alternative assessment, classified as a secondary evaluation procedure, is assessed with an unreviewable judgment by the Entry Assessment Committee. The Committee may, at its discretion, assess personal preparation through an interview, which may also be conducted in other ways.
Other elements contributing to the evaluation are:
- submission of a brief essay in which the candidate describes which of the acquired skills and knowledge they consider particularly useful as a starting point for achieving the educational goals of the Master's degree;
- reference letters.
Candidate Selection The Department Council annually determines the maximum number of students eligible for the International Management - International Management Master's program. For this purpose, UniTrento annually issues an admission notice for a public selection, specifying the timing and evaluation methods, conducted by a dedicated committee (Admission Committee). The Committee's activities may, where possible, also be conducted via telephone conference or online. The submission deadlines for admission applications are set annually by Rector's Decree and include two deadlines: mid-February and mid-June. The evaluation of candidates for selection is based on the level of knowledge and skills required by the regulations, according to the criteria specified in the admission notice.

Department Department of Economics and Management Entry Requirements Verification No Course Program, Texts and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's Degree in Innovation Management aims to provide advanced knowledge and managerial and economic skills necessary to understand, manage and leverage innovation processes in a broad sense: technological innovation, organizational innovation, service innovation (referring to recent multidisciplinary approaches in service science and service management innovation), with the purpose of strengthening the competitive position of enterprises and enterprise systems, as well as the effectiveness/efficiency of non-profit organizations.
The Master's graduate in Innovation Management will have acquired the necessary skills to make high-complexity strategic and operational decisions aimed at initiating innovative strategies within enterprises and other market-oriented organizations (private and public). The Master's Degree in Innovation Management aims to provide a multidisciplinary education oriented towards problem-solving, primarily based on changing procedures, methods, and solutions to achieve radically more efficient and sustainable results. The mix of knowledge acquired in the Master's Degree in Innovation Management will cover strategic market analysis and innovation pathways, quantitative and analytical methods necessary to evaluate the strategic positioning of the enterprise relative to competitors, the peculiarities of innovation processes, their design and implementation through economic, managerial, and technological skills.
Required Entry Knowledge Access to the Master's Degree in Innovation Management is subject to verification of the following requirements:
1. General Academic Requirements:
- Hold a first-level degree, obtained at an Italian university or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent;

SECTION: Admission Procedures

Admission Procedures Admission is limited to a set number. The selection process takes place between December and June and is based on the following criteria: previous academic degree, certified knowledge of English, any other international tests (e.g., GMAT, GRE), Curriculum Vitae, reference letters, candidate's motivation letter, overall evaluation of the profile and motivation by the selection committee.
Admission Requirements Admission to the MAIN Master's Degree is managed by a dedicated committee, annually appointed by the Course Board. The committee's activities are conducted both in person and remotely. During the health emergency related to the CoVid pandemic, the admission committee's evaluation procedures were conducted online.
Access to the MAIN Master's Degree course is subject to verification of the following requirements:
a) General academic requirements:
- Hold a first-level degree, obtained from an Italian university or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent;
- Possess English language proficiency at least at the B2 level or equivalent;
b) Specific academic requirements:
- Demonstrate good ability in reading and commenting on data related to the economic performance of companies and the economic-financial context;
- Demonstrate strong analytical skills in addressing quantitative problems;
- Have a good grasp of basic statistical techniques;
- Possess good ability to analyze economic and business-related problems.
These knowledge requirements typically correspond to at least 40 CFU related to courses in the scientific-disciplinary sectors identifying economic, economic-management, mathematical-quantitative, technical-productive, and computer science knowledge, particularly those listed in the attached table in the minimum required amount.
c) Personal preparation requirements: The personal preparation will also be evaluated according to the following methods.
Method of verifying academic requirements The possession of the requirements specified in Article 5, point 2, letters a) and b) of the regulations is typically verified through a review of the academic curriculum.
For students for whom the required knowledge cannot be verified based on the curriculum, the committee may adopt alternative evaluation methods, specifically:
- Based on the results of tests administered directly;
- Based on an interview focused on the disciplines;
- Based on the results of tests offered by accredited organizations as per Article 7.
For verifying English language knowledge at least at the B2 level or equivalent, results from internationally recognized tests or language proficiency assessments issued by the candidate's previous university are used. The test mentioned above must typically be taken by the deadline for the admission application. Alternatively, a declaration from the candidate's previous university stating that the official language of the first-level degree program or equivalent followed by the candidate is English is considered sufficient. In the absence of certification, English language knowledge may be assessed through an interview with a designated evaluation committee.
Method of assessing personal preparation The primary element for evaluating personal preparation is the result of taking the GMAT (Graduate Management Admission Test) or GRE (Graduate Record Examinations), available according to an annual international schedule set by the certifying bodies.
Students who have not taken the test (as mentioned above) may still request an evaluation of their previous academic results, which will be considered in relation to the distribution of academic outcomes from the educational institutions and/or countries of origin. This alternative evaluation to the test, classified as a secondary evaluation procedure, is at the sole discretion of the entrance evaluation committee.
The committee may, at its discretion, assess personal preparation through an online interview.
The committee defines, for the above-mentioned methods, an equivalence criterion relative to the minimum required level of preparation.
Other elements contributing to the evaluation are:
- Personal motivations and goals directly related to the educational objectives of the MAIN study program;
- Any motivation and reference letters.
Selection of Candidates The competent bodies of UniTrento and the Sant’Anna Higher School annually, upon proposal by the Course Board, determine the maximum number of students eligible for the study program. For this purpose, an annual joint call for public selection is issued, specifying the timing and evaluation methods, conducted by a dedicated committee.
The committee's activities may, where possible, also be conducted online.
Two application deadlines are typically scheduled for admission: a first round between December and March (open to all but predominantly for non-European citizens) and a second round between April and June (open only to European citizens and equivalent).
The evaluation of candidates for selection is based on the level of knowledge and skills specified in paragraph 2 of Article 5 of the regulations, as well as on a motivation letter and any reference letters.

[0207H] GLOBAL LAW MAKING Master's Degree English
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration
2 years Organization
2024
Approval Date
15-2-2024
Status Open Credits
120 CFU Type Master's Degree Programs Category Economics, Management and Law Regulation Reform 270/04
Degree Class LM/SC-GI R - Legal Sciences Joint Course No Limited Access (50 Places)
Location City Campus - Law Faculty - via Verdi, 53
Department Law Faculty Entry Requirements Verification No Course Program, Texts and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Global Law Making Master's program offers an entirely English-taught curriculum and aims to provide Italian and international students with advanced legal education, attentive to the changes contemporary law is facing and will increasingly face, particularly due to significant legal, economic transformations and especially ongoing digital and environmental transitions. As expressed in its very name "Global Law Making," the program seeks to train a jurist capable of effectively contributing to the normative process in a broad sense, including interpretative, application, drafting, argumentative, advisory, and analytical functions regarding law and related processes in a context where the normative process is characterized by (a) strong interaction between different levels (national, supranational, and international), (b) an unstoppable tendency to assume a global dimension, (c) expression outside state borders often through predominantly English-language legal language with conceptual categories independent of those dictated by national sources, and (d) increasing focus on ongoing transitions, particularly digital, environmental, economic, and ethical-political.

The innovative aspect of the Course lies in offering graduates a solid foundation in legal sciences while simultaneously providing a multidisciplinary approach to sectors enabling them to acquire the necessary skills to manage and respond to challenges posed by transitions affecting the current and future normative process.

The Master's graduate in Global Law Making is therefore able to:
- navigate and understand the content of domestic, European, and international regulations, as well as global law sources and their relationships, using comparative law methodologies, which will be part of the training;
- master the legal phenomenon using tools from some social sciences (economic, political, linguistic disciplines) as well as other sciences (computer science);
- analyze legal problems and develop solutions in contexts undergoing strong transformation;
- The Master's graduate in Global Law Making also possesses:
- in-depth multidisciplinary methodological knowledge suitable for legal professionals capable of addressing complex situations and developing solutions in public and private organizations, with strong attention to the supranational dimension, able to handle legal issues related to digital technologies and environmental sustainability;
- historical-legal and philosophical-legal knowledge, with particular reference to the legal space, including supranational and international, with specific attention to the ethical aspects of ongoing transitions;
- legal-linguistic competencies regarding law as a normative phenomenon undergoing strong transformation, in order to contribute to the formulation of norms, according to principles of clarity and conciseness, and to the legal qualification of concrete cases, even beyond traditional legal categories dictated by national sources.

Description of the training path.
The Master's program is structured over two years.
To implement the described training project, in the first year, courses addressing some cross-cutting conceptual areas are delivered: international, supranational, and global legal dimension, comparative and multidisciplinary methodology, technology-oriented, environmental, linguistic-legal courses, and courses related to the relationship between law and economics. Additionally, to create a common knowledge base for all students regardless of their undergraduate disciplinary orientation, a constrained elective teaching activity is offered in the first year for students coming from non-legal bachelor's programs (an activity complementing a "crash course" in legal subjects, activated in late August/early September, benefiting enrolled students not coming from IUS pathways). The multidisciplinary technological training includes a characteristic computer science course (SSD: INF/01 Computer Science).
In the second year, these foundational knowledge areas are complemented by deeper insights into the legal dimension and the themes previously introduced at a general level. The multidisciplinary nature of the Course continues with a course designed to help students develop the relationship between law and political science, with particular reference to the global dimension (SSD: SPS/2).
Combining traditional lectures with innovative teaching methods, the Master's program also offers, though not compulsorily but at the student's choice, the possibility of pursuing dual-degree programs with foreign universities.
To achieve the above educational objectives, the teaching activity, in addition to some traditional lectures, includes innovative teaching methods, adapted to the specific course and its subject:
- "Learning by doing" (field-based learning), particularly but not exclusively for courses transferring computer, technological, and linguistic-legal skills.
- Problem-solving learning, such as resolving judicial cases or specific problems related to the relationship between law, new technologies, and computer science.
- Active student participation in lectures (continuous assessment), including individual or group presentations, group work, guided classroom discussions, drafting reports and in-depth research on specific topics.

Entry Requirements for Access To access the Master's degree, candidates must possess curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation, which must be verified. Only candidates meeting the curricular requirements can undergo personal preparation verification.
Formal deficiencies or additional training obligations are not permitted.
Curricular Requirements:
Candidates must hold a first-level degree, or another foreign degree deemed equivalent:
- in the Legal Sciences class L-14,
or
- in other degree classes, where candidates have acquired at least 27 CFU in legal fields among the following SSDs: IUS/01-02-04-05-07-08-09-10-13-14-17-18-19-20-21.
Adequacy of Personal Preparation:
- Possession of curricular requirements cannot be considered as verification of personal preparation.
- Only candidates meeting curricular requirements can undergo personal preparation verification.
- Adequate personal preparation will be verified through evaluation of documentation related to the student's academic record.
- Additionally, for admission to the Master's program, candidates must possess English language knowledge at least at B2 level (CEFR). The verification methods will be specified in the Course's Didactic Regulations.
- For non-native Italian speakers, knowledge of the Italian language will be verified, using the methods specified in the Course's Didactic Regulations, which will also indicate - in cases of negative verification results - the training activities to be included in the Study Plan for acquiring the required Italian language knowledge for graduates.
The university may annually decide on the number of places available for entry. Selection of admitted candidates will occur only among those meeting curricular requirements and adequate preparation.

Department Department of Economics and Management Entry requirements verification No Course program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Master's Degree in Finance (class LM-16) aims to train a versatile figure capable of operating in contact with increasingly complex and competitive financial markets, providing an integrated set of economic, managerial, quantitative and legal knowledge.
The close interaction and common focus of the four disciplinary areas constitute an essential characteristic of the Master's Degree in Finance. Economic knowledge must form the reference framework, not only to develop this specific field of knowledge from the perspective of economic research, but also to be able to carry out high-level professional and managerial activities in corporate, banking and financial contexts. In this regard, the acquisition of specific managerial and forecasting knowledge and tools must now also include the ability to use advanced mathematical-statistical tools. On the other hand, economic activities related to finance, at every level, are now closely linked to increasingly extensive and complex regulatory provisions that require adequate competence in legal language and knowledge.
Applying the provided tools, the student will learn to:
- analyze the evolution of money, stock, debt and foreign exchange markets in the context of international macroeconomics, using statistical and econometric analysis tools;
- design coherent financial management strategies in corporate, banking and financial investment contexts;
- know and safely and appropriately apply a wide range of investment, financing and risk management tools, according to recent techniques of financial engineering and risk management.
The core of the training disciplines is complemented by the acquisition of indispensable linguistic skills (understanding, reading and expression in English).
The predominant teaching method consists of classroom lectures. Lectures with greater technical and operational content extensively use computer tools and aids. Different teaching interventions are aimed at:
1) acquiring operational skills and teamwork through simulation and financial forecasting laboratories,
2) developing discussion and critical analysis abilities through seminar sessions with course instructors and external experts,
3) gaining direct professional experience in a work environment through training internships in financial activities at companies and economic organizations, public and private institutions, national and international.
The training path is balanced over the two years both in terms of scientific-disciplinary areas and themes and tools. The first year focuses on foundational courses in economic areas (such as micro and macroeconomics) and corporate (such as market and financial intermediaries analysis), mathematics for finance (such as economic decisions, financial mathematics) and econometrics. The second year develops economic knowledge in the monetary and financial field, corporate knowledge in the field of risk management and advanced corporate finance, and econometric knowledge with specific applications for finance. The second year is also completed with the possibility to choose free courses, as well as applied activities (internships), linguistic courses and thesis preparation.
Entry requirements The Master's Degree in Finance aims to offer an advanced training path to graduates from the classes of Economic and Business Sciences, but also from the classes of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences and Engineering, whose graduates have growing professional opportunities in the financial field. To this end, the entry requirements are designed to balance knowledge in the economic and business economic field, and in the statistical-mathematical field.
Access to the Master's Degree in Finance is subject to verification of the following requirements:
- General curricular requirements:
o holding a first-level degree, obtained at Italian universities or another foreign degree recognized as suitable;
o having at least B1 level English proficiency or equivalent;
- Specific curricular requirements:
o having a solid basic knowledge of the general principles of micro and macroeconomics, and the structure, organization and economic and financial management of enterprises;
o having acquired adequate basic knowledge of mathematical and statistical methods and tools for economics;
o having acquired good ability to read, understand, process and communicate data related to macroeconomic trends, markets and companies, and the financial context.
These knowledge areas are considered acquired for graduates in the three-year classes of Economics and Business Economics. For graduates in other classes, the required knowledge typically includes at least 45 CFU related to courses belonging to the scientific-disciplinary sectors identifying economic, business, mathematical-quantitative knowledge, and in particular at least 15 CFU in SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/05, at least 15 CFU in SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/09, SECS-P/11, at least 15 CFU in MAT-05, MAT-06, MAT-09, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/06.
The possession of these requirements is verified through a curriculum screening and an assessment, to be carried out according to the modalities defined in the Study Course Didactic Regulations.
- Personal preparation requirements: assessment of personal preparation is carried out according to the modalities defined in the Study Course Didactic Regulations.

DEPARTMENT Department of Economics and Management Verification of Required Knowledge for Access No Program, Texts, and Objectives Specific Educational Objectives of the Course and Description of the Study Path The didactic-scientific project of the Master's Degree course in Behavioral and Applied Economics combines a perspective on the analysis of economic phenomena inspired by the Behavioral Economics method with a quantitative-applied approach. The basic idea is to make the aspects of the behavioral investigation method complementary with the techniques of applied research, providing tools from a theoretical side (also taken from standard economic theory) and from a statistical-quantitative side necessary for the analysis and interpretation of economic data. More precisely, the aim is to enable students to critically and innovatively interpret statistical sources and to design and implement field investigation tools (laboratory experiments, field experiments, surveys, etc.).
Upon completion of the study path, the Master's graduate will have acquired a solid economic education and advanced skills in the field of behavioral economics and applied economics. Applied training is also guaranteed through activities in laboratories for the study of economic behaviors.
The Master's graduate will have knowledge and skills in using behavioral guidance tools that will improve the well-being and efficiency of individual, business, and public organizational economic decisions.
The Master's Degree course in Behavioral and Applied Economics is structured around a basic framework centered on a group of common courses for the entire path and two possible alternative pathways. The common part of the study program will allow students to acquire the foundations of advanced economic theory and statistical knowledge for applied economics. The possibility of constructing two alternative pathways will allow the development of skills, knowledge, and the ability to apply the methods of behavioral and experimental economics or to work with observational data in the field of applied economics.
Prerequisites for Admission Access to the Master's Degree course in Behavioral and Applied Economics is subject to verification of the following requirements:
1. General Curricular Requirements:
- hold a first-level degree, obtained at an Italian university or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent
- have a command of written and spoken English at least at level B2 or equivalent.
2. Specific Curricular Requirements: the equivalent of at least 48 CFU related to courses belonging to the scientific-disciplinary sectors that identify economic, business, and mathematical-quantitative knowledge, with the constraint of having obtained a minimum number of credits for each of the following groups of disciplinary sectors:
1) at least 16 credits in the sectors SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/04, SECS-P/05, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/12,
2) at least 6 credits in the sectors SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/09, SECS-P/10, SECS-P/11,
3) at least 8 credits in the sectors MAT/05, MAT/06, MAT/09, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/04, SECS-S/06.
The possession of the above requirements is typically verified through the screening of the curriculum vitae and academic record.

Candidates who have not taken either test may still request evaluation of previous academic results, which will be assessed based on the distribution of results obtained at academic institutions and/or countries of origin. This alternative evaluation, classified as a secondary procedure, is implemented at the discretion of the Admission Committee.
At its discretion, the Committee may also assess personal preparation through an interview, conducted also via teleconference. The Committee defines, for the above procedures, an equivalence criterion relative to the minimum required level of preparation.
Relevant aspects include:
- Demonstrating good ability to read and comment on data regarding the economic performance of companies and the economic-financial context;
- Demonstrating good analytical skills in addressing quantitative problems, also through basic statistical techniques;
- Possessing good ability to analyze economic problems.
Evaluation is based on the following criteria: previous degree, certified English language proficiency (IELTS or TOEFL), other international tests (e.g., GMAT, GRE), CV, reference letters, overall assessment of profile and motivation by the selection committee.

[0419G] HISTORICAL AND PHILOLOGICAL-LITERARY STUDIES Bachelor's Degree
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration
3 years Order
2009
Status Open Credits
180 CFU Type
Three-year Bachelor's Degree Category
Humanities and Linguistics Regulation
Reform 270/04
Degree Class L-10 - Class of Bachelor's Degrees in Letters Interdepartmental Course No Programmed Access (131 Places)
Location City Campus - Palazzo Prodi - via Tommaso Gar, 14
Department Department of Letters and Philosophy Entry Requirements Verification
No Course Program, Texts, and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The "Historical and Philological-Literary Studies" Course is rooted in the tradition of studies based on the interaction between historical and philological-literary knowledge, within a perspective where philology is grounded in diachronic dimension, and the study of civilization refers to linguistic, critical, and philological evaluation of texts and documents. The Course aims to provide a systematic and articulated training that, covering the entire field of humanistic culture, also in reference to its classical and Romance roots, ensures the ability to directly and critically approach original sources from various eras and types.
Achieving a preparation corresponding to these prerequisites is the specific educational objective of the Course.
Graduates of the "Historical and Philological-Literary Studies" Course must therefore acquire significant skills in producing written texts in Italian, understanding and analyzing literary and documentary texts, and contextualizing them within European civilization.
To this end, the Course offers a varied range of common courses in historical and philological-literary fields. To allow graduates to deepen specific knowledge in a particular cultural area, also in preparation for access to master's studies, the following study paths are proposed:
- Classical Literature, beginning with the study of classical languages and literatures;
- Modern Literature, introducing linguistic, philological, and critical tools for reading modern literary texts, particularly Italian literature;
- History, focusing on the study of Western civilization history and critical evaluation of texts and documents.
The Course also provides an appropriate foundation, thanks to the cultural, communicative, and relational skills, as well as critical and interpretative abilities it promotes, for access to the workforce or specific professional training paths in administration, human resources management, communication, and cultural dissemination.
Entry Requirements
1. Required Knowledge for Entry To be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree in Historical and Philological-Literary Studies, the provisions of Article 6, paragraph 1 of Ministerial Decree No. 270 of October 22, 2004 apply: "To be admitted to a Bachelor's Degree Course, one must possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent."
Admission requires mastery of the Italian language, basic computer skills, and adequate knowledge in the following disciplines: Italian literature (fundamentals of literary history from origins to present), Latin (basic knowledge of language and Latin culture), history (fundamentals of European civilization from classical age to contemporary era), and geography (essential concepts for describing landscapes).
2. Method for Verifying Initial Preparation The possession of the required competencies and knowledge is verified through a written test, prepared by a commission composed of five teaching staff members appointed annually by the Department of Letters. The test, whose outcome is not binding for enrollment, will take place within October.
3. Criteria for Assigning Additional Educational Obligations The Commission refers students with educational gaps to the teachers of the relevant subjects to receive appropriate study guidance to address these gaps.

- Proficiency in the Italian language;

COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration

Degree class L-11 - Class of degrees in Modern Languages and Cultures Joint Course No Programmed Access (226 Places)
Location City Campus - Palazzo Prodi - via Tommaso Gar, 14
Department Department of Letters and Philosophy Entry requirements verification No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path Graduates in "Modern Languages" must acquire:
- C1 level in all four skills as defined by the Common European Framework of Reference in the two study languages.
- The necessary autonomy to develop their own skills and critically and methodologically deepen their knowledge in legal-economic, historical-geographical, philological-literary, and linguistic-cultural areas related to the countries of the study languages, also for potential continuation in master's degrees and subsequently in doctoral programs.
- The aptitude for international and intercultural communication and dialogue, appropriately supported by clarity of expression, effective argumentative ability in both written and oral form in the two study languages and in Italian, as well as possession of specific procedural competencies.
- The ability to manage communication within entities and companies operating in the specific fields of languages and cultures in both national and international contexts.
- Knowledge and understanding of linguistic-cultural differences/diversities and the ability to resolve conflicts, promote dialogue and cooperation, also to facilitate integration processes and new professional initiatives.
- The ability to analyze written texts through knowledge of linguistic-communicative acts and functions and the use of theoretical linguistics, contrastive analysis, as well as translation tools from and into the first language/Italian.
- Project management skills within communication in various professional sectors (journalism, publishing, linguistic mediation, tourism, commercial offices and international relations).
Within the framework of these shared competencies and skills, students will further develop specific competencies:
- In literary translation, through a solid theoretical foundation, knowledge of main translation tools including computerized and multimedia ones, and completion of internships in specific sectors;
- In the methodologies of philological and literary analysis of texts related to the cultures of the two foreign languages studied, with particular attention to linguistic phenomena and characteristic historical-literary events of those civilizations;
- In analytically and consciously addressing linguistic and cultural diversities;
- In using linguistic and interlinguistic mediation skills in national and international contexts, with particular attention to intercultural and professional communication aspects;
- In consciously using basic economic-business knowledge and enterprise management skills, particularly in marketing, strategy, and organization, with applications in the tourism sector;
- In applying basic geographical knowledge of territorial and environmental systems to develop a historical-artistic and landscape analysis of the territory, also with reference to tourist spaces;
- In implementing competencies related to planning, territorial design, and resource management.
The training path of the "Modern Languages" course is divided into two phases:
- An initial phase of acquiring and consolidating competencies in theoretical linguistics and written and oral Italian, study languages and cultures, and main computer and methodological tools;
- A second phase of acquiring competencies in communication, analysis and production of written and oral texts, and translation skills, both in linguistic-literary translation emphasizing methodological tools related to historical-cultural and philological-literary fields, including introductory literary translation, and in interlinguistic mediation in business and tourism contexts.
Entry requirements For admission and the entry requirements for the Modern Languages Bachelor's Degree course, the provisions of Article 6, paragraph 1 of Ministerial Decree 22 October 2004, No. 270 apply.
For admission to the Bachelor's Degree course, adequate mastery of the Italian language and basic computer tools are required.
Regarding the specific characteristics of the required knowledge and the methods for verifying their possession, refer to the Course Didactic Regulations, which may indicate any additional mandatory training obligations.

[0416G] PHILOSOPHY Bachelor's Degree
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration

180 CFU Type Undergraduate degree courses Category Humanities and Linguistic Studies Regulation 270/04
Degree class L-5 - Class of degrees in Philosophy Interuniversity Course No Programmed Access (121 Places)
Location City Campus - Palazzo Prodi - via Tommaso Gar, 14
Department Department of Letters and Philosophy Entry requirements verification No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path The specific educational objectives of the Bachelor's Degree in Philosophy are to acquire adequate familiarity with the different aspects of philosophical research in theoretical, ethical, religious, political, aesthetic, linguistic, logical and epistemological fields, as well as solid knowledge of the history of philosophical thought from antiquity to the present day.
The course provides ample space for the study of philosophical classics. The study of these texts aims not only at acquiring content but also at developing conceptual, philological and historical tools to understand their internal specificity and context. In this direction, the primary objective will be the critical reading and analysis of some fundamental philosophical works, both in Italian and in foreign languages, with attention to bibliographic research tools and philosophical historiography. Furthermore, an essential part of the teaching will concern the different methods and historical and logical structures of philosophical argumentative forms.
Acknowledging the relevance of other disciplines in contemporary philosophical debate, as well as the contribution of philosophical thought to various theoretical and applied fields, the course includes not only traditional philosophical teachings but also related teachings in pedagogical, psychological, sociological, religious, linguistic, mathematical, literary and historical areas. This broader perspective, in addition to improving the quality of training, aims to diversify the professional profiles of graduates, transmitting knowledge, skills and competencies that enable access to various sectors of the job market.
Students can pursue these educational objectives through study plans that particularly emphasize either the historical-philosophical and historical sciences area, or the ethical, political and religious area, or the logical and mathematical area.
Access to various professional sectors is also facilitated by targeted activation of internships, traineeships and specific training activities, as well as by consolidating knowledge of at least one EU language other than Italian. Language learning is generally supported to foster contacts with foreign universities and student mobility within Europe and beyond, the preferred form for encountering and understanding different study topics, research methodologies, and cultural contexts.
The training path is structured through frontal and seminar teaching activities, aimed at acquiring basic knowledge in the areas defined above and related methodological skills. Assessment of acquired competencies will consider both theoretical knowledge and methodological and analytical abilities.
Entry requirements For admission and the entry requirements for the Bachelor's Degree in Philosophy, the provisions of Article 6, paragraph 1 of Ministerial Decree 22 October 2004, No. 270 apply.
Students intending to enroll in the course must possess adequate mastery of the Italian language, basic computer knowledge, and sufficient knowledge of at least one foreign language.
Regarding the specific characteristics of the required knowledge and the related verification methods, please refer to the Course Didactic Regulations, which may indicate any additional educational obligations.

[0620G] INTERNATIONAL STUDIES Bachelor's Degree
COURSE INFORMATION General information referring to the current academic year Duration
3 years Curriculum
2015
Status Open Credits
180 CFU Type
Three-year Bachelor's Degree Category Sociology and International Studies Regulation
270/04 Reform
Degree Class L-36 - Class of Bachelor's Degrees in Political Science and International Relations Joint Course
No Programmed Access (200 Places)
Location City Campus - Sociology - via Verdi, 26
Department Department of Sociology and Social Research Admission Requirements Verification
No Course Program, Texts, and Objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path The main educational objective of the course is to help students understand the complexity of phenomena affecting contemporary societies by studying them from various disciplinary perspectives. The approach used is that of transformations induced by globalization, internationalization, and Europeanization processes on national social, political, and economic systems.
From its inception, the International Studies Bachelor's Degree program is based on the awareness that a full understanding of these phenomena can only be achieved through a multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary approach. Globalization and internationalization processes of national societies pose new questions to social sciences, making increasingly evident the need for interconnection and dialogue between economic, legal, political, sociological, historical disciplines, and others. This approach is reinforced and emphasized in the new Curriculum.
The Bachelor's Degree can be structured into pathways that differ in the professional and educational profiles they aim to achieve. While sharing a multidisciplinary approach, the courses offered in the two pathways may address complementary yet distinct themes.
The Bachelor's Degree is structured over three years. During the first year, students must acquire the "foundations" of major social sciences and statistics. In sociology, key concepts and notions necessary for analyzing society's configuration and social change are introduced. In modern and contemporary history, major events and developments of the modern and contemporary world and their key interpretations are presented. In political science, the discipline's language and conceptual frameworks are introduced, along with analysis of the democratic process. In political economy, particular attention is given to major macroeconomic theories. In public law, elements of European public law are introduced, understood as the combination of national and supranational public law. In statistics, basic principles of data analysis are presented. A significant emphasis is also placed on knowledge of the English language.
During the second year, essential tools for empirical research in social sciences and knowledge of international law are presented. Comparative political systems and their behavior and relations within the international system are also covered. Historically, the development of the modern state as a historically determined form of power organization in the European-Western context, from medieval origins to the consolidation of the modern age, is analyzed, concluding with some insights into the contemporary state's crisis in the face of globalization processes. As in the first year, a specialized English course completes the linguistic offering. Some courses may be specific to the educational pathways.
Finally, during the third year, courses focusing on more specific issues are offered. These address major research topics in European and International Studies, social inequalities, social movements and European civil society, citizenship and European democracy issues, conflict management, and more. A course in international economic policy completes the multidisciplinary training. By the end of the third year, students must also demonstrate knowledge of a second foreign language. To complete the training path, credit-bearing seminars on particularly relevant themes concerning the transformation of contemporary economic, political, and social systems are activated.
Admission Requirements Before accessing the Bachelor's Degree program, students must possess the following skills:
a) Analytical skills:
Among various types of analytical skills, logical reasoning abilities are particularly important; for example, students must be able to understand structured sets of relationships, deduce new information from them, analyze and evaluate arguments, draw precise and accurate inferences, and identify possible causal explanations, etc.
b) Verbal skills:
Among various verbal skills, the Bachelor's Degree program considers the following two particularly effective in determining the quality of the study path:
- Ability to understand texts: for example, students must be able to isolate the various steps where a fact is presented, exemplified, and developed; establish logical dependency connections between steps; synthesize information provided by the passage, etc.
- Ability to understand vocabulary: for example, students must be able to recognize analogies between terms in the vocabulary, identify the opposite of a given term, etc.
c) Knowledge skills:
The necessary knowledge for accessing the Bachelor's Degree program is as follows:
- Strong interest in subjects related to European, International, and Development Cooperation studies;

Department Department of Sociology and Social Research Admission Requirements Verification No Program, texts, and objectives Specific learning objectives of the course and description of the educational path The Sociology Bachelor's Degree provides students with the necessary tools, in terms of skills and understanding, to perform analytical, coordination, management, planning, communication, organizational, and evaluation functions in public and private professional contexts, which constitute the natural occupational destinations for the professional profile emerging from the Program.
Students receive a foundational sociological education enriched by contributions from major disciplines in the humanities and social sciences (anthropology, political science, history, psychology, economics, law, statistics), training in methods and techniques of major empirical research approaches, and more in-depth training in specialized sociologies. The fundamental goal of the Bachelor's Degree is to offer students, through a gradual and linear educational path, a set of tools enabling them to conduct analyses and interpretations of social reality.
Throughout the three years, students are introduced to concepts and theories of classical and contemporary sociological theory, with strong emphasis on their analytical applicability. At the same time, students learn the methods and techniques of social research and statistics, applying their knowledge through concrete research experiences. Concurrently, comparison with courses in anthropology, social psychology, political science, political economy, and law allows them to acquire the conceptual vocabulary of the broader field of social sciences, enriching the sociological perspective and integrating it with essential tools for understanding and capability to operate expertly and competently in professional contexts.
After a solid common foundational education, the study plan develops according to the path chosen by students as most appropriate. This enables graduates to develop the specific competencies required to operate effectively in one of the following professional fields: community development and collective action promotion with an environmental and social sustainability perspective; organizational innovation management and social entrepreneurship promotion; conducting socioeconomic and demographic descriptive and explanatory research; promotion and intervention in the field of cultural production and communication.
A general analysis of the disciplinary learning areas follows:
1. Sociological Disciplines: encompass courses focused on the study of major sociological theories and the deepening of related empirical research methods and techniques, including specialized sociologies such as economic and labor sociology, sociology of science, sociology of culture, sociology of inequalities and diversity.
2. Economic-Statistical Disciplines: include disciplines through which students acquire the fundamentals of economics and social statistics.
3. Legal-Political Disciplines: include disciplines through which students acquire the basics of law and political sciences.
4. Anthropological, Historical, and Psychological Disciplines: gather courses oriented towards the study of cultural anthropology, social psychology, and history.
Admission Requirements In addition to a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent, students must take an entrance test consisting of questions designed to verify:
- Text comprehension and knowledge of the Italian language;
- Knowledge and skills acquired during studies;
- Logical reasoning.
If the admission knowledge verification is not successful, specific additional academic obligations will be indicated to be fulfilled in the first year of the program. The course may be subject to limited admission.

To make the training offer more articulated, the course provides knowledge, skills, and tools related to reference legislation, analysis and intervention regarding different social issues, use of tools offered by various organizations, and methodologies typical of professional social work, enabling graduates to act guided by analytical and programmatic logic within an interdisciplinary work perspective. The main objective is to provide articulated skills to access the different segments characterizing the current and future dynamics of the labor market: public, private, and third sector.

Degree Class L-22 R - Sports and Motor Activities Sciences Interuniversity Program Partner Universities University of Verona Admission Quota (80 Places)
Location Rovereto Campus - Palazzo Piomarta - corso Bettini, 84 (Sustainable capacity: 80)
Department Department of Psychology and Cognitive Sciences Required Knowledge Verification No Course Program, Texts, and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path Graduates in Sports and Well-being Sciences are prepared to work in public and private sectors, where they conduct and manage motor and sports activities focused on individual and group psychological and physical well-being. They are capable of developing, maintaining, and recovering motor skills, considering factors such as age, gender, and ability, adapting to different sports and environments. They are also qualified in managing programs aimed at preventing postural dismorphisms and pathologies related to sedentary lifestyles.
To train graduates with these characteristics, the Study Program is organized around the following specific educational objectives: provide an in-depth understanding of the biological and biomechanical foundations of movement and adaptation to physical exercise, considering variations related to exercise type, duration, intensity, and the age and gender of the practitioner; enable the learning of preventive, compensatory, adaptive, and sports motor techniques, with particular emphasis on the correct transmission of these skills considering the specificities of gender, age, and physical condition of the practitioner, and possessing competencies also regarding the design of recovery strategies for gait or posture defects; provide a thorough understanding of methodologies for measuring and evaluating physical exercise, from both individual and group perspectives; provide competencies related to techniques and tools for muscle strengthening. Additionally, the Course Program aims to provide basic psychological knowledge for effectively interacting with practitioners based on variables such as age, gender, and social condition, as well as the foundational pedagogical, psychological, and didactic knowledge for transmitting both technical knowledge and ethical values and motivational frameworks aimed at promoting an active lifestyle and healthy, fair sports practice. Finally, the Course aims to provide specific preparation enabling graduates to access master's degree programs for training physical education teachers in secondary schools.
To achieve the aforementioned specific educational objectives, the Course is structured so that the sequence of teachings over the three years follows a learning path that, across disciplinary areas, prioritizes foundational aspects before focusing on the construction of operational and applied competencies. In pursuit of these objectives, the course is organized into 4 areas.
- Basic Sciences: Concerns both the availability and the ability to apply competencies, including methodological ones, related to the morphological, functional, and physical bases of motor and sports activities, as well as the interaction between motor activity, sports, and the functioning of various systems and organs.
- Human Sciences: Concerns understanding learning processes and foundational didactic aspects in motor and sports contexts, also in relation to psychological development stages; understanding the role of psycho-social, group, and cultural processes in sports; competence in promoting psychological well-being through sports.
- Law and Organization: Concerns competencies in relevant law and administration, organization of sports events, and sports jurisprudence.
- Motor and Sports Disciplines: Concerns solid competencies in techniques and methodologies of motor activities, with a focus on psychophysical development and well-being; mastery of the technical and didactic foundations of major sports disciplines, in an integrated perspective with physiological and metabolic knowledge; competencies in guiding individuals or groups in choosing and starting sports disciplines, using didactic techniques appropriate for teaching safe and effective physical exercise methods, and motivating the adoption of healthy lifestyles; ability to create suitable programs for various groups, including elderly and chronically ill individuals, to promote well-being and prevent sedentary-related diseases; competencies for performing first aid interventions in sports contexts. The necessary in-depth study is proposed for motor and sports disciplines also within related and integrative activities, where elective courses explore the educational, health, and recreational aspects of sports.
Required Knowledge for Admission To be admitted to the degree course, one must hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent.
The required knowledge for admission to the Study Program concerns basic knowledge of chemistry, mathematics, physics, and logic.
The methods for verifying the possession of the aforementioned knowledge will be defined in the course's didactic regulations. In case of negative verification results in some areas of the required knowledge, additional mandatory educational obligations must be fulfilled within the first year of the course.

[INT - TPAL] TECHNIQUES OF PREVENTION IN THE ENVIRONMENT AND WORKPLACES Bachelor's Degree InteruniversityJoint Title
INFO General information referring to the current academic year Duration
3 years Order
2024
Approval Date
16-3-2018
Status Open Credits
180 CFU Type Undergraduate Degree Category Medical, Health and Biological Sciences Regulation Reform 270/04
Degree Class L/SNT4 - Class of degrees in Health Prevention Professions Joint Degree Program Partner Universities University of Trento Access Open Location University of Verona Department Interdepartmental Center for Medical Sciences - CISMed Admission Requirements No knowledge verification Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path Graduates in the Course of Studies in Techniques of Prevention in the Environment and Workplaces must possess the necessary theoretical-practical preparation and scientific foundations, in accordance with Ministerial Decree 17 January 1997 No. 58, to practice the profession of Prevention Technician in the Environment and Workplaces; the Prevention Technician in the Environment and Workplaces is a health professional engaged in promoting and safeguarding public health and independently and responsibly carrying out all prevention, verification and control activities related to environmental hygiene and safety in living and working environments, food and beverage hygiene, veterinary public health hygiene, and environmental protection in accordance with the professional profile. Specifically, the graduate exercises their functions through surveillance, control, consultancy, opinions, investigations, information, training, education, management and research. At the end of the training path, the graduate must be able to:
- Independently and responsibly manage prevention, verification and control activities regarding the quality of living and working environments
- Manage sampling and data analysis methods for air, water, soil, food and biological matrices for prevention purposes in both living and working environments
- Define intervention priorities based on health and safety needs, organizational requirements and optimal use of available resources
- Design, implement and deliver, collaborating with other professionals, information and educational interventions for controlling and preventing risk factors for individuals and groups
- Utilize tools and methodologies for evaluating and reviewing professional, organizational and relational quality
- Manage prevention and control interventions to ensure food and beverage safety and wholesomeness from production to consumption
- Identify, analyze and evaluate risk factors for safety and health (equipment and installations, physical, chemical and biological agents, psychosocial, organizational and ergonomic factors) and identify the most effective and appropriate prevention techniques and measures for the identified problem
- Be responsible and professional, understanding ethical and professional issues in relation to users and in the context of interdisciplinary collaboration with other health professionals
- Conduct investigations into work accidents and occupational diseases
- Manage verification and control interventions on the safety conditions of installations and the compliance of structures and working environments with their connected activities
- In collective assistance activities within their field of competence, identify emerging health and safety needs, evaluating the need for subsequent specialized investigations when necessary
- Manage prevention and control interventions on public health hygiene, interacting with other professionals on issues related to animal-transmitted diseases
- Verify the safety and wholesomeness of dietary and cosmetic products
- Interpret and manage control activities in the application of legislative and regulatory provisions in the field of health and environmental prevention within the scope of their competencies
- Formulate opinions on public health, prepare, determine and communicate deviations or non-conformities, managing the process of alignment with safety and health criteria for identified issues
- Manage procedural activities for issuing authorizations or technical-sanitary approvals for controlled activities
- Integrate specialist assistance to support and collaborate with judicial administration in cases of environmental crimes and in relation to hygiene and safety conditions in workplaces and food that pose health risks
- Operate within the context of health promotion and primary prevention at the territorial level to promote network relationships, facilitate and support risk management in living and working contexts
- Evaluate the results of delivered interventions, readjusting planning based on outcomes, scientific evolution and research
- Demonstrate teaching and tutorial skills in the training of personnel and updating their professional profile
- Manage information systems supporting activities, interacting with other professional figures to manage and plan prevention projects within the services they operate
- Contribute constructively to the development of the profession, health structures and organizations
Training Path:
1st year – aimed at providing basic chemical-physical, biomedical and preventive hygiene knowledge, the foundations of the professional discipline as prerequisites for the first internship experience aimed at orienting the student towards the reference professional fields and acquiring basic competencies.
2nd year – aimed at deepening multidisciplinary knowledge characteristic of the different areas of intervention of the professional figure and professional competencies related to methods and techniques of prevention in different fields of competence (hygiene and health in living and working environments, food and beverages, public health hygiene). Internships are provided in contexts where students can experiment with the knowledge and techniques learned.
3rd year – aimed at deepening specialized knowledge in risk and quality management processes, as well as acquiring knowledge and methodologies related to professional practice, the ability to work in teams and in complex organizational contexts. Students acquire scientific research methodological skills to support thesis preparation. The relevance of internship experiences increases, allowing students to gradually assume autonomy and responsibility under expert supervision.
This curricular logic is reflected in the allocation of credits to internship experiences, which gradually increase from the 1st to the 3rd year.
Required Knowledge for Admission Candidates with a five-year secondary school diploma or equivalent foreign degree recognized as suitable may be admitted. Recognition of foreign degrees for admission to the degree course is decided in accordance with current international agreements.
The prerequisites required for students enrolling in the course should include:
good interpersonal skills, good teamwork ability, problem analysis and resolution skills.
Admission to the Bachelor's Degree course is quota-limited in accordance with Law 264/99 and requires an admission test. To successfully complete the Bachelor's Degree in Techniques of Prevention in the Environment and Workplaces, a sufficient preparation in biology and chemistry is required.
Students admitted to the course with a score below the minimum threshold will be assigned additional mandatory coursework in biology and chemistry as specified in the Course Regulations.

Degree Class L-2 - Class of degrees in Biotechnology Interuniversity Course No Quota Admission (75 Places)
Location Hillside Campus - Povo B - via Sommarive, 9 (Sustainable Capacity: 75)
Department Department of Cellular, Computational and Integrated Biology - CIBIO Entry Requirements Assessment No Program, textbooks and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Bachelor's Degree in Biomolecular Sciences and Technologies aims to prepare graduates with in-depth basic knowledge of the mechanisms of operation at molecular and cellular levels of biological systems. Graduates will possess conceptual and technical-practical tools for experimental work aimed at analyzing, modifying and utilizing cells or their components to enhance understanding of the fundamental mechanisms of biological systems and develop applications in areas where biotechnology impacts human life and demographic and environmental sustainability.
In particular, the course aims to provide graduates with the tools necessary to implement an "integrated" knowledge approach to biological systems. This term refers to an approach focused on studying the ensemble of molecular components, biological/physiological parameters and their interactions in complex systems. Through the use of model organisms, genomic sequences and high-throughput technologies, biomolecular sciences are now able to produce global monitoring of macromolecules and their interaction networks. This allows accurate knowledge of cellular metabolism under normal physiological conditions and its alterations under pathological conditions. Such an approach implies a strong "integration" of biological knowledge with mathematical, physical, chemical and computer science knowledge, capable of making significant contributions to a comprehensive understanding of biological systems.
The Bachelor's Degree in Biomolecular Sciences and Technologies is structured around a single training path. An adequate number of elective credits and the completion of training internships nevertheless offer students the possibility to define their own study plan.
The first two years focus on acquiring:
-solid knowledge in the fundamental aspects of biological sciences;
-adequate knowledge in chemistry, mathematics, physics and computer science;
-good knowledge of national and European Union regulations concerning bioethics, biolaw, protection of inventions and safety in the biotechnology sector;
-good knowledge of the English language, written and spoken.
The third year is dedicated to acquiring advanced knowledge of the conceptual and technical-practical tools of biotechnology and systems biology. The training path also includes internship or training activities at public or private institutions to facilitate graduates' operational readiness in the workplace. An additional opportunity to learn another official language of the European Union will also be offered to respond to the strong international mobility characterizing the sector.
Entry Requirements A secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent is required, along with a good initial preparation in mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology. Assessment of minimum essential knowledge in these disciplines will be conducted. Any additional educational requirements that the student must fulfill during the first year will be determined. English language knowledge is not required for admission as the course provides all opportunities for learning it. The Teaching Regulations provide a more detailed description of the disciplinary and general knowledge and skills required for admission to the Bachelor's Degree in Biomolecular Sciences and Technologies and specify the methods by which the competent teaching structure makes available to students and pre-enrollees appropriate forms of self-assessment and verification of such knowledge and skills.

COURSE: [0710G] PROFESSIONAL EDUCATION (ENABLING THE HEALTH PROFESSION OF PROFESSIONAL EDUCATOR)
