Bachelor's degree
COURSE INFORMATION General information for the current academic year Duration
3 years Curriculum
2022
Status Open Credits
180 CFU Type
Bachelor's degree programs Category
Medical, health and biological sciences Class
L/SNT2 - Class of degrees in Rehabilitation Health Professions Interdepartmental course No Programmed access (40 places)
Location Rovereto Campus - Palazzo Piomarta - corso Bettini, 84
Department Department of Psychology and Cognitive Sciences (Main)
Interdepartmental Center for Medical Sciences - CISMed Access requirements verification No Program, textbooks and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Bachelor's degree in Professional Education is an enabling degree dedicated to training the professional educator, a profession regulated through its own Register within the National Federation of Orders of Medical Radiology Technicians, Health Professions, Rehabilitation and Prevention. The Bachelor's degree aims to train a professional capable of operating in social and health areas and within their integration, using methods of individual, community and educational planning, and possessing specific competencies related to interprofessionalism. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF- WHO, 2001) is used as a reference.
The training path is structured in the following disciplinary areas:
-biomedical and health promotion area,
-psychological and pedagogical area,
-professional socio-health education area,
-sociological and human rights area,
-interdisciplinary linguistic, humanistic and computer science area.
The professional educator primarily operates through educational relationships, and for this reason the course offers important opportunities for developing relational skills with subjects experiencing various types of difficulties. In particular, this is dedicated to laboratories that are structured across different years. In the laboratories, students have the opportunity to analyze case studies, carry out simulations and role-playing games to acquire operational tools, relational skills and processing of emotional dimensions present in educational work. Central to this are internship activities, which occupy one third of the training path and take place at external health and socio-educational facilities. During the internship, students experience educational work methods, such as individualized educational plans, as well as educational relationships in different contexts. The internship allows for the practical application and field verification of acquired competencies. It is prepared, accompanied and supervised by expert tutors specialized in educational work operating within the university context. Transversal competencies are particularly relevant for the educational figure and are developed, not only in laboratories and internships, but also through active teaching methods, widely encouraged in the course, such as group work, presentations, etc. The study course pays particular attention to the connection between disciplines, between theoretical disciplines and internship, in order to foster the development of competencies and the ability to use acquired knowledge. Formal assessment moments of acquired competencies, not exceeding 20, will consider both theoretical knowledge and operational skills acquired by students, also within integrated courses across multiple disciplines. The professional growth of students is monitored and supported through laboratory moments and internship supervision. Within the internship, opportunities for meeting other professionals in the social and health area are promoted to develop interprofessionalism competencies.
The trained figure in this Bachelor's degree, consistently with what emerged in meetings with social partners, will have competence in promoting the biopsychosocial well-being of the community and the social inclusion of subjects in vulnerable conditions due to socio-health problems such as mental health, addiction, disability, marginalization, living in abusive and mistreated conditions, elderly age. The relational dimension is central to this figure's operation, which must have a solid theoretical, practical and personal emotional management preparation, extremely relevant in educational work. This represents the basis for professional autonomy that enables this figure to identify emerging socio-health needs, design innovative interventions, and participate in the construction and implementation of socio-health policies related to their area of competence.
The study course aims to train graduates with specific competencies in professional education. In particular, the course trains graduates with:
- knowledge and competencies in the health and health promotion field aimed at meeting care needs and basic assistance needs, and capable of promoting projects within the health protection framework, also based on specific modules for individual, social and territorial planning;
- relational competencies, understood as the ability to consciously perceive and manage the evolutionary process based on interaction and mutual recognition with others, also based on laboratories and reflection on internship experiences;
- educational-didactic competencies and knowledge in the interdisciplinary linguistic, humanistic and computer science area aimed at knowing how to teach, instruct and facilitate the learning of general and specific skills related to the entirety of the individual's aspects, also based on modules of methods and techniques of educational interventions;
- knowledge in psychological and social fields, and competencies related to reading social problems and phenomena relevant to educational work aimed at acquiring competencies to contextualize educational and rehabilitation processes within the specific socio-cultural fabric, also based on modules on tools for reading the individual and environment;
- methodological knowledge and programming-organization competencies in territorial contexts that allow the identification and implementation of operational strategies, organizational models and programming, functional to achieving objectives both at individual level and for educational and community projects, also based on modules of needs analysis and intervention planning.
Access requirements To be admitted to the Bachelor's degree, it is necessary to hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent. Admission to the Bachelor's degree is subject to national quota, in accordance with Law 264/1999. The number of places for admission, the modalities and content of the test are established by ministerial decrees.

No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Bachelor's Degree in Viticulture and Enology aims to train professionals with a first-level preparation, appropriately calibrated to perform the role of Enologist (Law 129 of 10.04.1991 and subsequent amendments). In particular, the graduate in Viticulture and Enology will have the necessary basic knowledge and skills in mathematics, physics, computer science, chemistry, biology, zoology and ecology, oriented towards practical applications within a multidisciplinary and systemic vision. The training path, therefore, is designed to build, on solid and broad knowledge, applied-depth studies that can be effectively used in the reality of the job market.
The graduate in Viticulture and Enology (Enologist) will be able to meet the needs in the sectors of grape production, with particular attention to environmental sustainability and protection of the viticultural territory. Furthermore, the Enologist manages the transformation of grapes, the production of wines and other vitivinicultural products, quality control, and the overall economic management of the supply chain.
Therefore, the graduate in Viticulture and Enology:
- will possess adequate knowledge of the core disciplines, particularly in agronomic, genetic, phytosanitary, and enological technologies;
- will have the ability to recognize and manage biotic (animals - especially arthropods, plants, microorganisms) and abiotic (atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere) factors of the agro-ecosystem, as well as those related to the transformation processes of raw materials;
- will have the ability to plan and manage all aspects related to field production and cellar transformation of raw materials in the vitivinicultural sector;
- will know the business contexts and their economic aspects specific to the vitivinicultural sector, but also generally to the agro-food sector;
- will possess operational laboratory knowledge in agricultural and microbiological fields, particularly in quality control of vitivinicultural products, analysis of biological matrices and agricultural soils;
- will know the scientific method of investigation and be able to collaborate in experimentation to solve practical problems in the vitivinicultural sector;
- will be able to make choices aimed at reducing the environmental impact of both viticultural and enological activities;
- will have the ability to receive innovative processes and transfer them promptly to the productive sector;
- will know the management and regulatory aspects of the sector, including the ability to contextualize them at national and international levels;
- will possess the basic cognitive tools for continuous formation and updating of their knowledge.
The didactic structure of the Bachelor's Degree in Viticulture and Enology is developed based on the guidelines proposed by the Organisation Internationale de la Vigne et du Vin (OIV, Paris), reflecting that of similar university courses in other European countries. It includes, besides basic disciplines, core, related, and integrative disciplines mostly of a professional and technical nature, as well as other training activities. The Bachelor's Degree is structured over three years. During the first year, students will acquire basic knowledge through theoretical lectures and classroom and laboratory exercises. In the second year, theoretical lectures on core disciplines will be complemented by laboratories, seminars, and study trips. In the third year, the study of core and related disciplines will be completed, a practical-applicative internship will be carried out, and a final thesis will be prepared.
The internship activities and those for preparing the final thesis may also be carried out at qualified production companies present in the territory and at Italian or foreign institutions with which specific agreements have been established. Practical-applicative internships may also be carried out in non-European countries in accordance with inter-university agreements or collaboration agreements for teaching and research. The Bachelor's Degree in Viticulture and Enology at Trento differs from those of other Italian universities as it particularly emphasizes and deepens themes related to the environmental sustainability of viticultural cultivation, and highlights the merits and specificities of mountain viticulture.
The study course aims to have an international character by providing students the opportunity to complete and enrich their training with experiences in other countries, also through double-degree agreements. Practical-applicative internships may also be carried out in non-European countries based on inter-university agreements or contacts for teaching and research collaboration.
The course adheres to European and/or international mobility programs, particularly investing in individual mobility for learning (study or internship).
Access Requirements For admission to the three-year Bachelor's Degree in Viticulture and Enology, the legal requirements must be met (diploma from secondary school or other foreign qualification recognized as equivalent), and an adequate initial preparation consisting of basic knowledge in mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology, as well as knowledge of the English language, the level of which is defined in the Course Regulations. Verification of these requirements is carried out through an entrance exam, which is also useful for identifying any additional educational obligations. The course may be subject to a controlled number. The modalities for conducting the entrance exam and any additional educational obligations to be fulfilled in the first year of the course are defined by the Course Regulations.
The exam will be organized taking into account the needs of candidates with disabilities, in accordance with Law 104/1992 and subsequent amendments, and Law 170/2010 and its implementing decree.

Admission procedures Access to the Bachelor's Degree program is conditional on passing an admission test (TOLC-AV), which consists of a written test with multiple-choice questions on Biology, Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry, Logic and Verbal Comprehension, and a section to verify English language knowledge at B1 level (CEFR). The assessment of requirements also provides students with a tool for self-assessment of their competencies in the areas considered preparatory to the course, to identify any Additional Educational Requirements (OFA).
Access to the Bachelor's Degree program requires English language knowledge, which will be verified during the admission test by achieving a score at least equal to the annual minimum threshold set by the Center. Passing the English language knowledge test is not required for candidates holding certification at or above B1 level (CEFR). Students who do not pass the English language knowledge test or do not possess valid certification must pass a test at the required level during the first year, according to procedures established by the Center.
Students who are included in the allocated number based on the total score obtained in the admission test may enroll in the Bachelor's Degree program. Students admitted with OFA (Additional Educational Requirements) are those who do not achieve a score at least equal to the annual threshold set by the Center in each section (Biology, Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, Logic and Verbal Comprehension) of the admission test. Candidates admitted with OFA must attend specific activities, such as recovery courses and/or tutor-guided activities in foundational subjects during the first year of the program, as defined by the Center's Council. The fulfillment of OFA must be verified within the first year; failure to fulfill OFA will prevent students from taking exams in subsequent years.

Three-year Bachelor's Degree Category Psychology and Neuroscience Regulation Reform 270/04
Degree class L-20 - Class of degrees in Communication Sciences Joint Course No Programmed Access (70 Places)
Location Rovereto Campus - Palazzo Piomarta - corso Bettini, 84
Department Department of Psychology and Cognitive Sciences Entry Requirements Verification No Course Program, Texts and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The study course aims to train graduates with skills in the cognitive and social aspects of communication mediated by communication technologies. In Italy, there are few institutions studying the specific aspects of communication technologies and human-machine interaction, and these are almost never considered together with the three "souls" of this field: computer science, cognitive sciences, and linguistic, graphical, and multi-modal user interface design. This complexity is reflected in the insufficient specific expertise currently present in Italy's production and service structures, and in the low international competitiveness. The course aims to offer a training curriculum for this type of professionalism, leveraging the specific expertise available in Trentino between the University and the Bruno Kessler Foundation.
This offering, centered on interactive information technology with particular attention to the person and the dynamic development of communication, could become especially important for the production of ergonomically based communication technologies usable in private services and public institutions, such as museums, tourism, and publishing. Moreover, it can also be noted that it could complement the more traditional view of "design," primarily linked to form, on which Italy has established itself but risks losing if it does not integrate it with other innovative aspects.
The course is intended to provide theoretical, methodological, experimental, and applied skills in the fundamental areas of user-oriented computing, primarily focusing on interfaces and communication between systems and users and intelligent information access. Therefore, it will lead to the acquisition of knowledge related to the design, production, and experimental evaluation of these systems, their social impact in different forms of implementation, and their utility in applications with users affected by cognitive-communication disorders. The graduate will therefore be able to contribute to planning, design, development, project management, estimation, testing, and management activities for interfaces and communication systems, and thus provide theoretical-technical support for the design, implementation, and analysis of human-machine interfaces that are ergonomic and effective from a communicative interaction perspective.
The training path is structured through frontal and seminar teaching activities, aimed at acquiring basic knowledge in the social, linguistic, cognitive, and computer science areas, and the related methodological skills. Laboratory activities are also provided for simulations and the acquisition of empirical-methodological skills, and internships are planned at external structures to operationalize the application of acquired skills. Students are also offered the possibility to attend courses abroad within the Erasmus program and numerous collaborations with foreign universities. The 20 assessment moments for acquired skills will consider both theoretical knowledge and the operational abilities acquired by students, also within integrated courses across multiple disciplines.
Entry Requirements Required knowledge for enrollment The following prerequisites are considered necessary for successful enrollment in the Bachelor's Degree course:
• Pre-intermediate level knowledge of English;
• Basic knowledge of mathematics;
• Adequate knowledge of fundamental computer science concepts.
These knowledge areas will be verified through a test conducted before the start of classes, with a dual purpose: on one hand, to provide students with a self-assessment tool for their skills in the areas deemed preparatory for the study course; on the other hand, to allow the teaching structure to prepare any recovery/consolidation activities, which may be assigned to students in the form of academic debts.
The study course's teaching regulations contain a detailed breakdown of the required knowledge and any recovery/consolidation activities that may be assigned to students in the form of academic debts in case the verification is not successful.

COURSE INFORMATION General information for the current academic year Duration

2021

180 ECTS credits Type Undergraduate degree program Category Mathematics and Physics Regulation 270/04
Degree Class L-30 - Class of degrees in Physical Sciences and Technologies Joint Course No Admission Quota (90 Places)
Location Hill Campus - Povo A - via Sommarive, 14 (Sustainable Capacity: 90)
Department Department of Physics Access Requirements Verification No Study Program, Texts and Objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path
1. The graduate in Physics from Trento:
a) possesses a solid preparation in disciplines included in the areas Mathematical and Computer Sciences and Chemical Sciences of the basic activities table of the present order, with particular reference to mathematics;
b) is able to prioritize the general and fundamental aspects of disciplines included in the areas Experimental and Applied, Theoretical and Foundations of Physics and Microphysics and Structure of Matter of the characteristic activities indicated in the table of training activities of the present order, and in particular the structure of matter up to the nuclear and subnuclear level;
c) has a solid experimental preparation acquired through the offer of advanced 'teaching laboratory' facilities;
d) is familiar with theoretical-mathematical, technological-experimental and also computer-informatic tools related to individual disciplines;
e) is able to integrate the tools mentioned in the previous point;
f) is able to carry out, directly or after a short internship, work activities requiring familiarity with innovative technologies;
g) is able to develop and analyze models for complex systems with applications in industrial, financial or service sectors where such requirements would be needed;
h) is able to profitably pursue any specialization within a Master's Degree course in the Physics class.
2. The language of instruction is Italian. Students may optionally include in their study plan freely chosen courses offered in English.
The training path at the first year includes acquiring basic competencies in Mathematical Analysis, General Physics, Computer Science and Geometry. Particular attention is devoted to the experimental training of the student, based on the conviction that the ability to understand physical phenomena is closely linked to laboratory activities.
The second year of the course completes the basic knowledge, with particular reference to Mathematical Analysis, Analytical Mechanics, General Physics and Chemistry. In the second year, the training path includes characteristic activities aimed at acquiring in-depth knowledge in the theoretical and foundational areas of physics and in laboratory activities, with particular reference to electrical phenomena and modern optics.
The third year of the course allows the student to complete their preparation in the areas of quantum mechanics fundamentals and microphysics and structure of matter. The related and complementary courses also enable the student to learn about the most recent developments in physics in the theoretical and foundational areas, nuclear and subnuclear physics, electronics and applications of physics to biology.
The course programs allow students to acquire knowledge related to the main contents of physics. In particular, emphasis is placed on reprocessing the acquired knowledge. Particular attention is given to stimulating active learning, for example by prioritizing the study of the same topic from diverse and qualified sources. Assessment criteria therefore aim to verify the degree of knowledge reprocessing, which will appear more sophisticated the greater the understanding.
In selecting freely chosen training activities, the student, while retaining the right to access the entire university's teaching offer, may choose to deepen the fields of general relativity, optics, biophysics and computational physics through the courses offered by the Department of Physics in these areas.
The study path may also include external activities such as study stays at other Italian and foreign universities, also within international agreements.
Access Requirements To be admitted to the three-year Bachelor's Degree in Physics, the following are required:
a) secondary school diploma or other foreign qualification recognized as suitable;
b) adequate basic knowledge of mathematics and basic sciences, ability to understand text, reasoning and problem-solving; knowledge of English at least at B1 level of the Common European Framework. Access requirements verification occurs through the admission test. It is possible to enroll students with scores below the annual minimum threshold set by the department: in this case, additional academic obligations must be fulfilled within the first year of the course.

Department Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering Required knowledge verification No Program, textbooks and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Bachelor's degree in Engineering for Environment and Territory aims to train a graduate with solid theoretical, practical and methodological foundations necessary for a modern and advanced engineering approach to the complexity of environmental issues. The natural outcome of this training path is access to a second-level program, although the preparation is fully adequate for entering the workforce according to the specifications of the degree class.
Regarding educational objectives, the course adopts the general objectives qualifying the class, tailored specifically. In particular, it pursues the following educational objectives:
- To provide, within Basic Training Activities, the necessary knowledge for describing and interpreting engineering problems, as well as developing a methodological approach to setting up and qualitatively and quantitatively solving problems specific to environmental engineering;
- To familiarize students with the basic principles, processes, analysis and measurement methodologies, types of works and plants, particularly in the environmental context, and to develop the ability to create design elements related to solid, fluid and earth mechanics, resource management and territory representation, through Characterizing Training Activities in the disciplinary fields of Civil Engineering, Safety and Civil Protection Engineering, Environmental and Territorial Engineering, and particularly Environmental and Territorial Engineering;
- To enable students to grasp the multiple perspectives necessary to understand the complexity of environmental issues, through the multidisciplinary and cross-sectoral training provided by Related or Complementary Activities;
- To allow deepening of themes close to the individual student's sensitivity but consistent with the overall training path, through Optional Training Activities.
The training path spans three years: typically, the first year is dedicated to basic science courses; the second year completes the basic training, supplemented by some more specifically engineering courses. The third year is entirely dedicated to purely engineering training, with characteristic courses in environmental and territorial engineering. Optional courses, distributed uniformly across both semesters, and the final exam complete the year. Activities dedicated to developing knowledge useful for entering the workforce and English language courses are distributed uniformly across the three years.
It is possible to offer non-mandatory courses in English.
Required knowledge for admission To enroll in the Bachelor's degree in Engineering for Environment and Territory, a secondary school diploma obtained in Italy or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent is required.
Additionally, a basic knowledge in logic, verbal comprehension (in Italian), Mathematics (Arithmetic and algebra, Analytical geometry and numerical functions, Trigonometry, Statistics), Sciences (Mechanics, Optics, Thermodynamics, Electromagnetism, Chemistry and structure of matter) and adequate knowledge of English are required.
Candidates must undergo a verification of the above-mentioned knowledge to access the Bachelor's degree. If the verification is not successful, Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) will be assigned, to be fulfilled within the first year of study.
The Study Program Regulations specify the methods for verifying such knowledge and detail the content of any Additional Educational Requirements.

UNIVERSITY: University of Trento
COURSE: [0326G] ENVIRONMENT AND TERRITORY ENGINEERING
TYPE: Bachelor's Degree
CURRICULUM: Admission Procedure
SECTION: Admission Procedure
URL: https://unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10130

Admission Procedure The study program has programmed access according to the procedures specified in the selection notice published on the university website at the beginning of each academic year. Admission to the program follows the following procedure:
1. Candidates must register and take the TOLC-I test (details are described below) to assess basic skills and knowledge. Three sessions are scheduled at the Trento campus during the calendar year 2023. The test is considered passed if the score obtained exceeds a threshold value that varies depending on the session.
2. Those who pass the TOLC-I can register for the selection notice. The ranking will be drawn up based on the result achieved in the TOLC-I. The first N students in the ranking will be declared 'eligible admitted', where N represents the number of available spots, which varies depending on the session (see below).
3. Students declared 'eligible admitted' may complete the admission process according to the procedures specified in the selection notice.
Candidates who fail to complete all parts of the described procedure will not be admitted.
AVAILABLE SPOTS AND TEST THRESHOLD VALUES FOR EACH SESSION For the academic year 2024/25, the total number of available spots is 130, distributed as follows:
- 100 spots for the first session (TOLC taken by February 29, 2024),
- 30 spots for the second session (TOLC taken by April 30, 2024),
- any remaining spots in the recovery session.
If in a session the available spots exceed the number of eligible admitted students, the surplus spots will be made available in the next session.
Registration for the first session is valid only for access to the first ranking. To compete for the second session with the same TOLC-I score or a new score obtained from another TOLC-I test, it is mandatory to re-register for the competition valid for the second ranking, starting from March 1, 2024.
For the purpose of the ranking for admission to the academic year 2024/25, the best TOLC score obtained from January 1, 2023, at any CISIA test site will be considered valid. It is specified that the score achieved in the TOLC will be considered valid regardless of the test site or date.
The test passing thresholds are defined as follows:
- score at least 18 for the first two sessions;
- score at least 15 for any recovery session;
For scores between 15 and 18, Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) will be applied according to the procedures established by the Department.
TOLC-I TEST The TOLC-I test is organized nationally by the Interuniversity Consortium for Access to Engineering and Architecture Schools (CISIA). The TOLC-I consists of 50 questions divided into 4 sections: Mathematics, Logic, Sciences, and Verbal Comprehension.
The test also includes an English language proficiency test with 30 questions, equivalent to B1-CEF level, with a score and result independent of the overall result.
EXTERNAL REFERENCES
- Candidates may access self-assessment opportunities offered by CISIA: the syllabus and a test simulation, with example questions similar to those in the TOLC-I test, are available at http://www.cisiaonline.it/.
- Information regarding the selection notice and test procedures is published on the university web portal at http://infostudenti.unitn.it/it/ammissioni/ammissione-alle-lauree-triennali-e-lauree-magistrali-a-ciclo-unico

No Knowledge Verification Program, textbooks and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Bachelor's Degree in Information Engineering, Communications and Electronics aims to train professionals with general competencies in the field of information engineering, depending on the student's chosen orientation, with specific competencies in telecommunications, electronics and computer science. These professionals respond to labor market needs, which often do not require specialization limited to a single sector, but rather a non-superficial understanding of systems, methodologies and technologies across the entire information area, along with the ability to recognize relationships between various disciplines and professionally address interdisciplinary problems.
The learning areas involved in achieving the educational objectives are:
- Mathematical and physical disciplines area to provide basic mathematical and physical knowledge necessary to correctly apply the scientific and experimental method in problem solving;
- Computer science disciplines area to offer solid competencies in computer programming and data structure management;
- Telecommunications technologies and systems area to provide knowledge related to signal processing and information transmission;
- Electronic devices and circuits area to provide basic competencies in designing digital and analog electronic systems and embedded systems;
- Specialization courses for acquiring more professional competencies.
COURSE STRUCTURE The Study Program provides a common basic training for all engineering degrees, followed by broad-spectrum engineering training in the field of information engineering. Subsequently, the Study Program is structured into pathways where the student, at their own choice, acquires specific and in-depth training in one of the areas characterizing information engineering, such as computer engineering, telecommunications engineering or electronic engineering.
To allow students to acquire and integrate in a harmonious and balanced way the different required knowledge, the teaching offer is structured in:
1) a basic training where both the methodological-operational aspects of mathematics and the fundamental knowledge and methodological aspects of basic sciences of interest for information technologies are covered;
2) a broad-spectrum engineering training in the field of information engineering, where the fundamental contents of disciplines qualifying the information area (electronics, computer science and telecommunications) and knowledge of related methodologies are acquired.
3) At this point, students can choose between different pathways:
3.1) Specific and in-depth training in the field of telecommunications and design of information acquisition, processing and transmission systems, to ensure methodological and applied preparation for the analysis, modeling and design of systems, devices and infrastructures related to information acquisition, processing and transmission;
3.2) Specific and in-depth training in the field of computer science and complex information processing systems, to ensure methodological and design preparation aimed at designing hardware and software architectures for automation and production support products and services;
3.3) Specific and in-depth training in the field of electronics and design of circuits and integrated systems, to ensure methodological and design preparation for the analysis, modeling, design and control of analog and digital hardware devices and systems related to information acquisition, processing and transmission methods and automation.
4) Student training will be complemented by preparation to manage digital transformation and data science in computer science, economics, statistics, business organization and management engineering disciplines, which students can deepen according to their interests.
5) Students can then complete their training path with elective courses, for example those from areas other than the predominant one or advanced courses.
To enable students to gain operational knowledge of the English language, the training path obligatorily includes at least three university credits aimed at achieving an adequate language level for attending teaching activities conducted in English.
The activities proposed in the final year of study also allow students to choose whether to complete their training path with methodological content or with project-based or internship activities aimed at acquiring more professional competencies.
Methodological deepening is aimed at providing students with the prerequisites necessary to successfully continue their training in a Master's Degree or a first-level Master's course, and is organized into pathways oriented towards telecommunications engineering, computer science, electronics and other technical-scientific degrees such as computer science.
The Study Program is strongly project-based, using laboratory teaching tools and developing activities for the design of devices and software.
Professionalizing deepening also includes acquiring design, technological and operational competencies, aimed at direct and effective entry into the labor market, which can also be acquired through training internships at companies operating in the sector.
Required knowledge for entry For enrollment in the Bachelor's Degree in Computer Engineering, Communications and Electronics, a secondary school diploma obtained in Italy or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent is required.
Additionally, candidates for the Bachelor's Degree in Computer Engineering, Communications and Electronics must possess the following knowledge:
Essential Knowledge
- Knowledge of the Italian language
- Adequate knowledge of the English language.
Basic Scientific Knowledge Mathematics
- Arithmetic and algebra: properties and operations on numbers (integers, rational, real); absolute value; powers and roots; logarithms and exponentials; algebraic calculation; polynomials (operations, factorization); algebraic equations and inequalities of first and second degree; systems of first-degree equations.
- Geometry: segments and angles (their measurement and properties); lines and planes; notable geometric loci; properties of basic plane figures; properties of basic solid figures.
- Analytic geometry and functions: Cartesian coordinates; concept of function; equations of lines and simple geometric loci; graphs and properties of elementary functions.
- Trigonometry: graphs and properties of trigonometric functions; main trigonometric formulas (addition, subtraction, duplication, bisection); relationships between elements of a triangle.
Physics and Chemistry
- Knowledge of elementary concepts on physical quantities and the structure of matter.
The Didactic Regulations describe in more detail the specific knowledge required for entry into the Bachelor's Degree and specifies the verification methods for such knowledge; additional educational obligations to be completed within the first year of the course will also be specified if the verification is not positive.

Admission Methods The bachelor's degree program in Computer Engineering, Communications and Electronics Engineering is quota-controlled and requires passing a selective test held in two or three sessions (spring and summer). Admission requirements and procedures for the Study Program are defined in the Didactic Regulations available at:
https://offertaformativa.unitn.it/it/l/ice-ingegneria-informatica-comunicazioni-elettronica/regolamenti-e-manifesti The Bachelor's Degree program in Computer Engineering, Communications and Electronics Engineering offers pathways in Italian and an English pathway. For the Italian pathways, the quota is set at 175 places, including 5 places for non-EU non-resident citizens selected through an admission test and a mandatory Italian language test. For the English pathway, the quota is set at 60 places, including 15 places for non-EU non-resident citizens selected through an admission test. For all pathways, non-quota places are open to Italian, EU, and equivalent citizens.
The selective test consists of multiple-choice questions common to the bachelor's degree programs in Engineering for the Environment and Territory, Civil Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Computer Engineering, and Computer Engineering, Communications and Electronics Engineering. The questions aim to assess:
a) mathematical and scientific knowledge
b) logical reasoning ability
c) text comprehension
Admission to the program is based on a ranking determined by the score obtained in the multiple-choice test. Candidates in the admission ranking must confirm their place by a specified date in the call. Vacant places due to withdrawals are filled by moving down the ranking.

No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Study Course trains engineers with in-depth methodological and operational knowledge in basic scientific disciplines (mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer science) and broad competencies in engineering disciplines, with particular emphasis on those specific to industrial engineering for a modern and advanced approach to the complexity of typical industrial manufacturing problems.
The specific objective of the Study Course is to train system engineers oriented towards the manufacturing industry, who have acquired tools for understanding subsystems of different nature (particularly mechanical, technological, electrical, electronic and computer science) and strong functional integration capabilities; they must also know conventional and innovative materials, the development of related production technologies, the management of industrial processes and plants, business organization, without neglecting the fundamental competencies of information engineering, necessary both to ensure a rational use of the potential offered by information technologies and to understand their impact in production realities.
The Study Course aims to provide, from various perspectives, an overall vision oriented to the life cycle of industrial products and their production processes, in a form useful for developing any material good, including the tools and production processes themselves, with particular attention to the development processes of new technologies and new products, their cognitive and connectivity functionalities. A modern methodological approach is privileged, according to which the form of a solution follows the function, thus preparing individuals capable of understanding the technical problems of engineering, identifying and acquiring useful information and data for analysis and problem solving, addressing even new problems, expanding their knowledge and generating specific knowledge, and communicating information and solutions clearly.
The natural outcome of the training path is access to a second-level degree course, although the preparation is also adequate for entering the workforce. Indeed, graduates will have acquired solid training and the necessary theoretical, applied and methodological foundations for continuing their education in second-level degree courses, particularly in the fields of Mechanical Engineering, Automation Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering and Management Engineering, but not only. A professionalizing path is not provided, however, at the end of the three years, graduates will possess fundamental interdisciplinary methodological competencies for direct entry into the workforce. They will be able to operate competently throughout the entire life cycle of products and can be integrated into the processes of developing new industrial products and new technologies. In particular, the theoretical knowledge and methodological and operational competencies necessary for continuing education in master's degrees are acquired through the study of basic scientific disciplines (mathematics, physics, chemistry and computer science) and by placing particular emphasis on the scientific and methodological aspects of the characteristic disciplines of mechanical engineering, materials engineering, electrical engineering, as well as the fundamental concepts of information engineering, essential in the evolution of industrial processes over the last two decades.
The technological, design and application knowledge and competencies important for entering the workforce are acquired by the student in all courses of mechanical engineering, materials engineering and electronic and information engineering disciplines, especially in those more oriented towards design and transformation and production technologies.
The training path is structured over three years, with the first year predominantly dedicated to basic disciplines, the second year completing the basic training alongside the main characteristic disciplines of industrial engineering that draw on the scientific knowledge acquired through the study of basic disciplines and provide the necessary methodological and operational knowledge and competencies for completing the training, which occurs during the third year when the student can access a wide range of characteristic industrial engineering courses. The third year is completed by elective courses, evenly distributed across both semesters, and the final exam. Activities dedicated to developing knowledge useful for entering the workforce and English language knowledge are uniformly distributed across the three years. The possibility of offering non-compulsory courses in English to students is provided.
The educational objectives of the Study Course will be achieved through the structuring of the educational offer into training paths that will share all basic courses and a solid core of characteristic industrial engineering courses. The training paths will begin to differentiate from the second year of the course, allowing in-depth study of specific topics such as the study of materials, production processes and transformation technologies, or the study of the fundamentals of automation, electrical and electronic engineering disciplines. The training paths will be detailed in the Study Course Didactic Regulations. To ensure completeness of preparation in industrial engineering disciplines, each training path, in addition to a solid core of mechanical engineering disciplines, will require the student to acquire a significant minimum number of credits in the fields of materials engineering and electrical engineering, to ensure the primary objective of training system engineers oriented towards the manufacturing industry. The training paths to be activated will allow in-depth study in different fields, but will still be characterized by a common solid foundational training in the above-mentioned fields.
This preparation makes the Industrial Engineering graduate particularly suitable for addressing the continuous challenges in product and process innovation imposed by global competition. Integrated into a work environment organized in teams and projects, or within autonomous activities, the graduate has the ability to use state-of-the-art design tools and methods, choose and employ materials, manage production processes and technologies, conduct experiments and analyze data; possesses synthesis and communication skills (also in a foreign language) and understands the social effects of technology.
Entry Requirements For enrollment in the Industrial Engineering Bachelor's Degree Course, a secondary school diploma obtained in Italy or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent is required.
The Industrial Engineering Bachelor's Degree Course requires candidates to have adequate abilities and knowledge, in particular:
- Ability to understand verbal communication and communicate effectively in written and oral Italian;
- Adequate knowledge of English (as established in the Course Regulations);
- Ability for logical deductive reasoning;
- Ability to analyze the behavior of a simple system starting from fundamental laws and the characteristics of its components;
- Ability to distinguish between necessary and sufficient conditions;
- Ability to distinguish between definition, theorem and proof.
Basic knowledge in Mathematics (Arithmetic and Algebra, Analytical Geometry and Numerical Functions, Trigonometry, Statistics, Computer Science), Physics and Chemistry (Mechanics, Optics, Thermodynamics, Electromagnetism, Chemistry and Matter Structure) is also required.
For access to the Bachelor's Degree Course, candidates must take the national entrance exam for Engineering organized by the Interuniversity Center for Access to Engineering and Architecture Schools (CISIA) and an English language knowledge test.
The entrance exam aims to determine whether the candidate possesses, and to what extent, the essential knowledge specified above.
The Study Course Didactic Regulations will establish the criteria and methods for verifying any additional educational obligations and the tools offered to fulfill them (DM 270/2004, art. 6, comma 1).

UNIVERSITY: University of Trento
COURSE: [0327G] INDUSTRIAL ENGINEERING
TYPE: Bachelor's Degree
CURRICULUM: Admission Procedures
SECTION: Admission Procedures
URL: https://unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10131

Admission Procedures The Bachelor's Degree in Industrial Engineering, starting from the 2015-2016 academic year, operates under a local quota system. Currently, the quota for the 2023-24 academic year is 245 places (including 5 reserved for non-EU residents abroad). Admission is subject to passing an admission test. The study program adheres to the national online test system (TOLC-I) developed by CISIA (Interuniversity Consortium for Integrated Systems for Access) for admission to Engineering and Architecture Schools. Eligible candidates include citizens of European Union countries and those specified in the admission notice. Some places are reserved for non-European citizens residing outside Italy, allocated according to the University's Unified Admission Notice for courses taught in Italian.

The TOLC-I test verifies knowledge (primarily in mathematics, physics, and chemistry) and simultaneously allows students to confirm they meet the required prerequisites. The admission test also includes an English language proficiency assessment to verify the level required by the Study Regulations (B1 CEFR).

Currently, three test sessions are held annually (April, July, and August). Based on the test result, applicants are placed in the merit ranking and must confirm their enrollment within a couple of weeks of the ranking publication. Admission may also be granted with a test score below the minimum threshold (18 points out of 50), provided the score meets a second threshold set by the Department Council. In such cases, specific additional educational obligations (OFA) must be fulfilled within the deadlines set by the Department Council. Students who fail to meet these additional obligations must pass the Analysis Mathematics 1 exam before all other exams in the study plan. English language proficiency at entry is not required for candidates holding certification at or above the level specified in the Study Regulations. Students who do not pass the English language proficiency test at entry must retake it during the first year, following Department-established procedures. Passing the English language proficiency test at entry is mandatory as a prerequisite for all subsequent exam sessions.

Transfers to the Industrial Engineering Bachelor's Degree program are also admitted based on available places in the second and third years for specific study paths. Applicants must submit a pre-evaluation request for credit recognition to assess their academic record for admission. The Department Council may recognize previously completed training activities from other study programs at the University or other Italian or foreign universities, along with corresponding grades. For all curricula, access to exams for courses in subsequent years is permitted only after acquiring at least 15 CFU corresponding to courses in the scientific disciplines MAT/03, MAT/05, and FIS/01, and after passing the English language proficiency test at entry.

Department Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering Prerequisites for Access No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Civil Engineering Bachelor's degree aims to train graduates capable of continuing with master's studies - where they can complete the full training of a civil engineer - and who, alternatively, can work within teams dedicated to the design or construction of engineering works, and are able to independently acquire further specific competencies in application fields of the civil engineering sector.
Upon completion of the study path, the graduate will have acquired:
- a basic education, with solid preparation in mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer science and programming, mechanics, thermodynamics, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics;
- solid preparation in the field of civil engineering disciplines;
- basic knowledge of methods and tools for the automatic design of conventional engineering works;
- operational knowledge and techniques in specific areas of Civil Engineering, such as Technical Architecture, Topography, Construction Techniques, Geotechnics, Road Infrastructure.
The graduate will be able to perform, immediately and independently, some simple tasks required in the professional world. The acquired preparation will also facilitate the choice of future master's study orientation for those who pursue this path.
The training path is therefore not intended to achieve a narrow professional expertise in a specific activity sector, recognizing that employment in the world of work is easier for graduates who, alongside a solid basic education, possess a sufficiently detailed knowledge of the main themes and applications of civil engineering. This preparation will therefore enable the graduate to apply to different problems, even not specifically treated during the study course, by appropriately using the basic and applied knowledge acquired during the study course.
The training path is carried out over three years: typically, the first year is essentially dedicated to basic science courses; the second year is dedicated to completing the basic education, supplemented by some more specifically engineering courses. The third year is entirely dedicated to purely engineering training, with characteristic courses in Civil Engineering, Environmental and Territorial Engineering, and Safety and Civil, Environmental and Territorial Engineering. The training path is completed by the student's free-choice activities, the final exam, activities dedicated to developing knowledge useful for entering the world of work, and activities aimed at achieving an adequate knowledge of English at the level specified in the Academic Regulations.
Prerequisites for Access For enrollment in the Civil Engineering Bachelor's degree, a high school diploma obtained in Italy or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent is required. Additionally, a basic knowledge in logic, verbal comprehension, Mathematics (Arithmetic and algebra, Analytical geometry and numerical functions, Trigonometry, Statistics), Sciences (Mechanics, Optics, Thermodynamics, Electromagnetism, Chemistry and structure of matter) and an adequate knowledge of English at B1-CEF level are required.
For access to the Bachelor's degree, candidates must undergo a verification of the above-mentioned knowledge. In case of negative verification result, Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) will be assigned. The Academic Regulations of the Bachelor's degree specify the verification methods for such knowledge as well as the content of the OFA.

UNIVERSITY: Università degli studi di Trento
COURSE: [0325G] CIVIL ENGINEERING
TYPE: Bachelor's Degree
CURRICULUM: Admission Procedure
SECTION: Admission Procedure
URL: https://unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10127

Admission Procedure The study course has programmed access according to the procedures specified in the selection notice published on the university website at the beginning of each year.
Admission to the course follows the following procedure:
1. Candidates must register and take the TOLC-I test (details are described below) to assess basic skills and knowledge. Three sessions are scheduled at the Trento campus during the calendar year 2024. The test is considered passed if the score obtained exceeds a variable threshold depending on the session.
2. Those who pass the TOLC-I can register for the selection notice. The ranking will be drawn up based on the TOLC-I result. The first N students in the ranking will be declared 'eligible admitted', where N represents the number of available places, variable depending on the session (see below).
3. Students declared 'eligible admitted' may complete the admission process according to the procedures specified in the selection notice.
Candidates who fail to complete all parts of the described procedure will not be admitted.
AVAILABLE PLACES AND THRESHOLD SCORES FOR THE TEST PER SESSION For the academic year 2024/25, the total number of available places is 100, distributed as follows:
- 80 places for the first session (TOLC taken by February 29, 2024),
- 20 places for the second session (TOLC taken by April 30, 2024),
- any remaining places in the recovery session.
- If available places exceed the number of eligible admitted in a session, surplus places will be made available in the next session.
- Registration for the first session is valid only for access to the first ranking. To compete for the second session with the same TOLC-I score or a new score from another TOLC-I test, it is mandatory to re-register for the competition valid for the second ranking, starting from March 1, 2024.
- For the purpose of the ranking for admission to the academic year 2024/25, the best TOLC score obtained from January 1, 2023, at any CISIA test site will be considered valid. It is specified that the score obtained in the TOLC will be considered valid regardless of the test site or date.
The test passing thresholds are defined as follows:
- score at least 18 for the first two sessions,
- score at least 15 for any recovery session.
For scores between 15 and 18, Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) will be applied according to the procedures established by the Department.
TOLC-I TEST The TOLC-I test is organized nationally by the Interuniversity Consortium for Access to Engineering and Architecture Schools (CISIA). The TOLC-I consists of 50 questions divided into 4 sections: Mathematics, Logic, Sciences, Verbal Comprehension.
The test also includes an English language proficiency test with 30 questions, equivalent to B1-CEF level, with a score and outcome independent of the overall result.
EXTERNAL REFERENCES
- Candidates can access self-assessment opportunities offered by CISIA: the syllabus and a test simulation with example questions are available at http://www.cisiaonline.it/.
- Information regarding the selection notice and test procedures is published on the university web portal at http://infostudenti.unitn.it/it/ammissioni/ammissione-alle-lauree-triennali-e-lauree-magistrali-a-ciclo-unico.

Department Department of Engineering and Information Science Admission Requirements Check No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Computer Science Bachelor's Degree aims to train individuals with solid foundations and a broad range of competencies in the field of information science and technology, serving as a starting point both for direct entry into the workforce and for further specialization in Master's, Master, and PhD programs. The Computer Science graduate is a professional capable of analyzing complex systems (companies, services, natural and artificial systems), systematically identifying critical processes, and proposing feasible models and solutions through software and information systems. The mindset, given the emphasis on universal scientific tools and methods, is naturally predisposed to quickly integrate into diverse work contexts, adapting to the rapid innovation characterizing the sector.
The Bachelor's Degree program includes a common set of courses providing foundational knowledge in mathematics and computer science. Subsequently, two possible pathways are distinguished:
- the Computer Science and Technology pathway, with two orientations: a methodological orientation for those intending to pursue a Master's Degree in Computer Science and Technology, and a professional orientation for those intending to complete their studies at the end of the Computer Science Bachelor's Degree.
- the Interdisciplinary pathway, intended for those who wish to complete their computer science education with complementary disciplines in biology, economics, and mathematics, and continue studies in other disciplines such as a Master's Degree in Medical Biotechnology, a Master's Degree in Finance, and a Master's Degree in Mathematical Sciences.
Required Knowledge for Admission Students holding a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable are admitted to the Bachelor's Degree program. Necessary requirements to begin studies regularly include the ability to reason rigorously, familiarity with mathematical language, and an interest in addressing and analyzing complex problems to determine strategies and methods for their solution.
No detailed computer science skills are required, and English language knowledge is not necessary as the course provides all opportunities to learn it. Students with a more humanistic background often achieve success in studies and careers comparable to students with an initial technical background.
Enrollment is conditional on passing the mandatory orientation and self-assessment test. The adopted test is the national CISIA test promoted and managed by the Interuniversity Consortium for Integrated Systems for Access (hereinafter CISIA), to which the University of Trento adheres, available both on an online platform (CISIA Online Test) and in paper format.
Candidates scoring above 20 for the paper format and 15 for the online format may enroll without academic debts. For the paper format, candidates scoring between 15 and 20 may enroll with academic debts. Further information is available at http://disi.unitn.it/test_ammissione_laurea_triennale_informatica. Practice tests are also available at http://www.cisiaonline.it/it/default/61/Test-di-allenamento-CISIA.html.

Admission Procedure The Bachelor's Degree in Informatics is quota-controlled and requires passing a selective test held in two or three sessions (spring and summer). Admission requirements and procedures are defined in the Didactic Regulations available at:
http://offertaformativa.unitn.it/it/l/informatica/regolamenti-e-manifesti For the Bachelor's Degree in Informatics, the quota is set at 175 places, including 5 quota places for non-EU citizens not residing in Italy, selected through an admission test and a ministerial Italian language test.
A total of 170 places are available for Italian, EU, and equivalent citizens. The selective test consists of solving multiple-choice questions common to the Bachelor's Degrees in Environmental and Territorial Engineering, Civil Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Informatics, Computer Engineering, and Communications and Electronics Engineering.
The questions aim to verify:
a) mathematical and scientific knowledge
b) logical reasoning ability
c) text comprehension ability
Admission to the study program is based on a ranking list established according to the score obtained in the multiple-choice test. Candidates in the available positions of the admission ranking must confirm their place by a date specified in the call. Places becoming available due to withdrawals are allocated through the ranking list's progression.

Department Department of Economics and Management Prerequisites for access No Course program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the study path The Bachelor's degree in Business Management aims to train professionals capable of understanding, managing and improving the processes through which companies create value, efficiently transforming production factors into goods and services that meet consumer or user needs. To develop these skills, Business Management graduates learn the tools for detection and analysis and decision models typical of management disciplines, and are guided in their application using mathematical and statistical methodologies and appropriate computer tools. They also understand the connections between the company and the economic and regulatory context, thanks to the acquisition of fundamental interpretative tools of economics and law.
In the first year, common to all Bachelor's degrees in the same class, students deepen topics typical of Economics, Business Economics and Law, as well as acquire the necessary basic mathematical-analytical and statistical skills.
Subsequently, the Business Management study program provides specific in-depth studies in various fields of management knowledge, legal integrations for commercial aspects, and the study of a foreign language, with some limited degrees of freedom for students in their choices.
Great emphasis is placed on laboratory activities, where statistical methodological knowledge and economic-business knowledge interact to define a learning path linked to business reality and problem solving. In these activities, the acquisition and use of communication skills play an important role.
Internship in a company is mandatory for all students in the Bachelor's degree program.
Specific training contracts may be activated depending on the student's commitment regime (part-time or full-time).
Prerequisites for access Students enrolling in the Bachelor's degree in Business Management must demonstrate a minimum level of knowledge in the following areas:
- Mastery of basic tools of logic and mathematics with particular reference to:
° elementary algebraic calculation: powers, absolute value,
polynomials, equations and inequalities of 1st and 2nd degree;
° fundamental notions of analytic geometry: straight line,
circle, parabola, ellipse and hyperbola;
- Mastery of a foreign language at B1 level, among French, English, German and Spanish;
- Mastery of personal productivity applications (Open Office, Microsoft Office, etc.), ECDL level, or equivalent (4 basic modules, to be integrated during the study path up to ECDL Full level, or equivalent).
Prerequisites for access will be verified according to modalities defined by the course's didactic regulations, which also specifies additional educational obligations in case of negative verification.

Admission Procedures Access to the study program is quota-limited. Selection is based on a test administered twice a year.
Local Admission Planning The Department Council annually decides the quota-limited number, based on sustainable student capacity, typically by deadlines set by current regulations and in sufficient time for adequate information. The Department Council's decision is reviewed by the Academic Senate with expanded representation including student representatives, and subsequently approved by the Board of Directors. The admission notice is typically published according to two different deadlines: an early spring deadline (usually in April) and a summer deadline (usually in August).
Required Knowledge for Admission and Initial Preparation Verification Students enrolling in the Bachelor's Degree in Business Management must demonstrate a minimum level of knowledge in the following areas:
a) Proficiency in basic tools of logic and mathematics, including:
- Elementary algebraic calculation: powers, absolute value, polynomials, first and second-degree equations and inequalities;
- Fundamental concepts of analytical geometry: straight line, circle, parabola, ellipse, and hyperbola;
b) Proficiency in a foreign language at B1 passive level, among French, English, German, and Spanish;
c) Proficiency in personal productivity software applications (Open Office, Microsoft Office, etc.) at ECDL Base or ECDL Start level (or equivalent) - 4 basic modules, intended to be integrated with learning during the study path until reaching ECDL Full Standard or ECDL Core Full level (or equivalent).
The possession of the required knowledge is demonstrated by passing the appropriate assessment tests. The language knowledge assessment tests may be replaced by adequate certification issued by accredited organizations or otherwise recognized by the Department. The list of recognized certifications is approved by the Department and regularly updated. The test for personal productivity software applications (Open Office, Microsoft Office, etc.) may be replaced by adequate ECDL (European Computer Driving Licence) certification or other certifications deemed suitable by the Department. Tests may be taken at the University's designated facilities:
- Before enrollment, according to the schedule prepared and published on the Department's website;
- After enrollment, at the start of the study program's teaching activities, according to the schedule prepared and published on the Department's website.
In case of failure to pass the tests, students are invited to attend the preparatory courses offered by the Department and University structures. The schedule and attendance modalities for these courses are published on the Department's website. In case of failure to pass the tests, they must be retaken in subsequent sessions set by the Department, and must be passed within the first year of study, typically by September of the following calendar year. If the tests are not passed by the deadline, students will be invited to reconsider the opportunity to pursue other educational paths. In any case, they cannot take further assessment tests until all tests are passed.
For students enrolling under the 'part-time' study commitment regime, which has a standard study duration of 4 years, the deadline for passing the aforementioned tests is extended to the end of February of the second year of enrollment.

Degree class L-33 - Class of Bachelor's Degrees in Economic Sciences Interclass L-18 - Class of Bachelor's Degrees in Economics and Business Management Joint Course No Programmed Access (235 Places)
Location City Campus - Economics - via Inama, 5 (Sustainable capacity: 235)
Department Department of Economics and Management Entry requirements verification No Program, textbooks and objectives Specific educational objectives and description of the training path The Bachelor's Degree in Economics and Management aims to provide a solid foundational methodological preparation in economic and managerial sciences, enabling students to correctly and up-to-date analyze economic systems at both the national level and the enterprise level, with particular attention to the growing interrelations between these two areas. Graduates in Economics and Management will be able to directly and autonomously address decision-making tasks and problems in various fields, applying updated analytical, measurement and forecasting tools. The Bachelor's Degree in Economics and Management also aims to provide an open education for continuous learning and innovation, allowing graduates to subsequently access the most updated knowledge in their profession or further training.
The Economics and Management study program is exclusively oriented towards a "methodological" approach and therefore strongly emphasizes providing solid and in-depth foundational knowledge in the reference disciplines and analytical tools, with particular focus on mathematical and statistical tools, especially the inferential aspects of statistics.
The study program includes a first part dedicated to the fundamentals of economic and managerial disciplines, with theoretical and methodological deepening. In particular, basic knowledge in economics and management will be deepened, with interrelations between the two areas, especially regarding markets, consumer behavior, and competition. In this foundational training area, typical topics of regulation and the formation of norms will be addressed. Additionally, general educational subjects such as economic history will be covered.
In the second part of the program, students will deepen specific theoretical areas common to both economics and management, focusing on the theme of economic decision-making. This theme will be explored both analytically and from a behavioral perspective, which is currently fundamental for those dealing with economic decisions, at both the aggregate level and the enterprise level. This aligns with the Faculty's prevailing orientation towards behavioral studies.
Finally, students will have the opportunity to orient their training by choosing from a range of thematic deepening courses in the previously covered study areas. A characteristic moment is the multidisciplinary laboratory activity, where the acquired theoretical knowledge and analytical tools will be used to develop practical skills in applying advanced decision evaluation tools, particularly using simulation techniques.
Language proficiency verified at entry will be reinforced through a "specific" language course for the field of study and courses taught in English.
The thesis, typically of a theoretical-methodological nature, concludes the program.
Entry requirements Students enrolling in the Bachelor's Degree in Economics and Management must demonstrate a minimum level of knowledge in the following areas:
- Mastery of basic logical and mathematical tools, particularly:
  • Elementary algebraic calculation: powers, absolute value, polynomials, first and second-degree equations and inequalities;
  • Fundamental concepts of analytic geometry: straight line, circle, parabola, ellipse, and hyperbola;
- Mastery of a foreign language at B1 level, among French, English, German, and Spanish;
- Proficiency in personal productivity applications (Open Office, Microsoft Office, etc.), at ECDL level or equivalent (4 basic modules, to be integrated during the study program with further learning up to ECDL Full or equivalent).
Entry requirements verification is scheduled according to the study program's didactic regulations, which also specifies additional educational obligations in case of negative verification.

[0206G] COMPARATIVE, EUROPEAN AND INTERNATIONAL LEGAL STUDIES Bachelor's degree English
INFO INSEGNAMENTI General information for the current academic year Duration
3 years Curriculum
2017
Status Open Credits
180 ECTS Type Bachelor's degree programs Category Economics, Management and Law Regulation D.M. 270/04
Degree class L-14 - Class of degrees in Legal Sciences Joint Course No Admission Quota (75 Places)
Location City Campus - Law Faculty - via Verdi, 53
Department Law Faculty Required knowledge verification for admission No Program, texts and objectives Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path The Bachelor's degree course aims to introduce students, both Italian and international, to the knowledge of primarily (though not exclusively) Western legal traditions, and on this basis provide them with a foundational preparation of an inter- and transnational nature, both in language and content: a preparation that offers students, alongside the main competencies traditionally forming the basis of a legal operator's training in the field of substantive and procedural law, and alongside the historical foundations of modern legal thought, a solid knowledge of comparative, European and international law, developing a particular inclination to address legal issues from a supranational perspective, as well as to professionally use languages other than their own (particularly English).
The course also aims to highlight the role and impact of European and international law on national systems, as well as the contribution of national legal traditions to the harmonization or approximation of legislation in European and international contexts where such phenomena emerge.
In this particular path, emphasis will be placed on: understanding the phenomenon subject to legal norms, according to methodologies that value the historical, philosophical, economic and linguistic perspective; contextualizing it within the framework of specific facts, categories, and operational models mainly used in different legal traditions and, where applicable, in European and international law; identifying general principles, with particular attention, where they exist, to those established in European and international contexts. The comparative method will be employed as a tool for understanding the main legal traditions and as a useful vehicle for future learning of specialized content that may be acquired during subsequent work or study paths.
The linguistic training within the Bachelor's degree holds particular relevance. This training no longer refers solely to learning one or more foreign languages, but also to teaching specific subjects and skills through a language other than one's mother tongue. In this sense, language is no longer merely a subject of teaching and learning, but a formative tool and methodology aimed at acquiring communicative, relational, cognitive competencies, as well as personal growth. Teaching in a foreign language is, rather than a mere tool for learning data, a dialectical and inter-systemic methodology.
It is also an objective of the Bachelor's degree course to enable students to acquire adequate computer skills, with particular emphasis on the use of major legal databases.
To pursue such educational objectives, the course introduces from the first year the study of comparative legal systems and European law alongside the foundational subjects of legal preparation and the historical-philosophical foundations of modern legal thought. Having acquired methodological elements in the first year, in the second and third years the student approaches, still from a comparative, European and international perspective, the study of substantive and procedural law disciplines in various private and public fields. An introduction to interdisciplinary methodologies will be covered in the study of the foundations of history, philosophy, economics and linguistics and their interaction with legal matters. The study path is completed with a consolidation of English language knowledge, the study of an additional European Union language other than the mother tongue (Italian being mandatory for international students), the study of legal informatics, and the completion of seminar-style training activities and/or internships, aimed at the practical application of knowledge acquired during the Bachelor's degree, as well as the acquisition of communicative and relational competencies.
Required knowledge for admission To be admitted to the Bachelor's degree course, one must:
- hold a high school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent to a university degree for admission to a comparable university program;
- possess English language proficiency at level B2 or higher, certified according to the methods specified in the teaching regulations. If this verification is unsuccessful, the student must fulfill the additional educational obligations specified in the teaching regulations.

Admission Requirements The Course of Study in 'Comparative, European and International Legal Studies' is quota-limited. Starting from the academic year 2021/2022, 75 students are admitted. The possibility of admitting an additional quota of candidates from countries not belonging to the European Union, as provided for in specific University resolutions, is reserved. Admission of such students is subject to meeting the same access requirements listed below, though the verification methods may vary and will be specified in a dedicated call.

Admission to the Comparative, European and International Legal Studies course is subject to the following academic requirements:
(1) Secondary school diploma obtained in Italy or, if obtained abroad, deemed equivalent. Diplomas obtained abroad are considered equivalent if they allow access to a similar course at universities in the country whose academic system they follow.
(2) Knowledge of English (B2 level).
The possession of requirements 1) and 2) is verified through document assessment.
In particular, requirement 2) will be verified through the possession of appropriate language certificates, identified by the University Language Center (CLA) resolution.
Should the verification of requirement 2) (English language knowledge at B2 level) be unsuccessful, the candidate may enroll in the course but must fulfill additional training obligations during the first year of study to demonstrate the required language level for taking the course examinations.
The selection of the 75 candidates will be carried out through a test and the subsequent formation of a ranking based on the test results.
The entrance test is administered twice a year, with one session in April and a second session in August.
Within the August entrance test, the ranking may also take into account the high school graduation grade, if specified in the relevant call.
The test is conducted in English and consists of 80 questions, divided as follows:
a) 70 general knowledge aptitude questions with an international focus;
b) 10 basic computer science questions.
The number of questions in the admission test may vary; the actual number of questions and the test administration methods will be specified in the admission call.
